title.zh: 卷二十一 列傳第九: 燕鳳 許謙 崔宏 張袞 鄧彥海
title.en: Volume 21 Biographies 9: Yan Feng, Xu Qian,Cui Hong, Zhang Gun, Deng Yanhai
title.raw: 卷二十一 列傳第九: 燕鳳 許謙 崔宏 張袞 鄧彥海 Volume 21 Biographies 9: Yan Feng, Xu Qian,Cui Hong, Zhang Gun, Deng Yanhai

sentences.zh: 燕鳳 許謙 崔宏 張袞 鄧彥海

translations.literal: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Cui Hong, Zhang Gun, Deng Yanhai
translations.idiomatic: Volume 21 Biographies 9: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Cui Hong, Zhang Gun, Deng Yanhai

sentences.zh: 燕鳳許謙崔宏子浩張袞弟恂鄧彥海

translations.literal: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Cui Hong (son Hao), Zhang Gun (younger brother Xun), Deng Yanhai
translations.idiomatic: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Cui Hong (son Hao), Zhang Gun (younger brother Xun), Deng Yanhai

sentences.zh: 燕鳳，字子章，代人也。

translations.literal: Yan Feng, style name Zizhang, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Feng, styled Zizhang, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少好學，博綜經史，明習陰陽讖緯。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, broadly mastered classics and history, and was skilled in yin-yang lore and prognostic texts.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved study, mastered the classics and histories, and was expert in yin-yang doctrine and prognostic texts.

sentences.zh: 昭成素聞其名，使以禮致之，鳳不應聘。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng had long heard his fame and sent men to summon him with ceremony; Feng did not accept the invitation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng had long heard of him and sent envoys to summon him with full rites; Feng declined to come.

sentences.zh: 及軍圍代，謂城人曰：「鳳不來者，將屠之。

translations.literal: When the army besieged Dai, he told the townspeople, "If Feng does not come, I shall slaughter you.
translations.idiomatic: When the army besieged Dai, he told the townspeople, "If Feng does not come, I shall slaughter you.

sentences.zh: 」代人懼，遂送鳳。

translations.literal: " The people of Dai were afraid and thereupon sent Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Dai were terrified and sent Feng forth.

sentences.zh: 昭成待以賓禮。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 後拜代王左長史，參決國事。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Left Chief Scribe to the King of Dai and took part in deciding state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Left Chief Scribe to the King of Dai and joined in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 又以經授獻明帝。

translations.literal: He also taught the classics to Emperor Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed Emperor Xianming in the classics.

sentences.zh: 嘗使苻堅，堅問鳳曰：「代王何如人？

translations.literal: Once he was sent on mission to Fu Jian; Jian asked Feng, "What sort of man is the King of Dai?
translations.idiomatic: He was once sent to Fu Jian, who asked Feng, "What manner of man is the King of Dai?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「寬和仁愛，經略高遠，一時雄主也。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Broad, harmonious, and humane, with far-reaching strategy—a warlord of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Feng answered, "Magnanimous and humane, with far-reaching strategy—the preeminent warlord of the day.

sentences.zh: 常有併吞天下之志。

translations.literal: He constantly harbors the will to swallow the realm under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly aims to unite the realm.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「卿輩北人，無剛甲利兵，敵弱則進，敵強則退，安能並兼邪？

translations.literal: " Jian said, "You northerners have no stout armor or sharp weapons; when the foe is weak you advance, when strong you retreat—how can you annex and absorb them?
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "You northerners lack stout armor and keen blades; when enemies are weak you advance, when strong you withdraw—how could you conquer and absorb them?

sentences.zh: 」鳳曰：「北人壯悍，上馬持三仗，驅馳若飛。

translations.literal: " Feng said, "Northerners are stalwart and fierce; mounted, each carries three weapons and gallops like flight.
translations.idiomatic: Feng said, "Northerners are hardy and fierce; on horseback each man bears three weapons and rides like the wind.

sentences.zh: 主上雄雋，率服北土，控弦百萬，號令若一。

translations.literal: Our lord is heroic and outstanding, rules the northern lands, commands a million bowmen, and his orders are as one.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord is heroic, has won the north, commands a million archers, and his orders are obeyed as one.

sentences.zh: 軍無輜重樵爨之苦，輕行速捷，因敵取資。

translations.literal: The army suffers none of the hardship of baggage trains or camp cooking; it marches light and swift and takes supplies from the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: His armies know none of the drag of supply trains or camp kitchens; they march light and fast and live off the foe.

sentences.zh: 此南方所以疲弊，北方所以常勝也。

translations.literal: This is why the south grows weary and broken while the north is ever victorious.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the south wears itself down while the north wins again and again.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「彼國人馬多少？

translations.literal: " Jian said, "How many men and horses does that state have?
translations.idiomatic: Jian asked, "How many men and horses does that state have?

sentences.zh: 」鳳曰：「控弦之士數十萬，見馬一百萬匹。

translations.literal: " Feng said, "Bowmen number in the hundreds of thousands; horses in pasture exceed a million.
translations.idiomatic: Feng said, "Archers number in the hundreds of thousands; grazing horses exceed a million.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「卿言人眾則可，說馬太多。

translations.literal: " Jian said, "What you say of men may stand, but you speak too many horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Your count of men may stand, but your horses are too many.

sentences.zh: 」鳳曰：「雲中川自東山至西河二百里，北山至南山百餘里，每歲孟秋，馬常大集，略為滿川。

translations.literal: " Feng said, "From East Mountain to West River along the Yunzhong valley is two hundred li; from North Mountain to South Mountain over a hundred li—every year in mid-autumn horses gather in great numbers and nearly fill the river valley.
translations.idiomatic: Feng said, "From East Mountain to West River along the Yunzhong stretch is two hundred li; from North Mountain to South Mountain is over a hundred li. Each year in mid-autumn the horses gather until the valley is nearly full.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，使人言猶未盡。

translations.literal: By this reckoning, even what men say does not tell the whole.
translations.idiomatic: By that measure, even what people say falls short of the truth.

sentences.zh: 」鳳還，堅厚加贈遺。

translations.literal: When Feng returned, Jian richly rewarded him with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng returned, Jian sent him lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 許謙，字元遜，代人也。

translations.literal: Xu Qian, style name Yuansun, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian, styled Yuansun, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有文才，善天文圖讖學。

translations.literal: In youth he had literary talent and was skilled in astronomy, charts, and prognostic learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he showed literary talent and mastered astronomy, charts, and prognostic lore.

sentences.zh: 建國時，將家歸附，昭成擢為代王郎中令，兼掌文記。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state his family came over in submission; Zhaocheng promoted him to Palace Gentleman to the King of Dai and put him in charge of written records.
translations.idiomatic: When the state was founded his family submitted; Zhaocheng made him Palace Gentleman to the King of Dai and put him in charge of documents.

sentences.zh: 與燕鳳俱授獻明帝經。

translations.literal: Together with Yan Feng he taught the classics to Emperor Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yan Feng together instructed Emperor Xianming in the classics.

sentences.zh: 昭成崩後，謙徙長安。

translations.literal: After Zhaocheng died, Qian moved to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhaocheng's death, Qian went to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 苻堅從弟行唐公洛鎮和龍，請謙之鎮。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's younger cousin, the Duke of Xingtang, Luo, held Helong and invited Qian to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's younger cousin, the Duke of Xingtang, Luo, governed Helong and asked Qian to join him there.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以繼母老，辭歸。

translations.literal: Before long, because his stepmother was old, he begged leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with his stepmother aged, he asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 登國初，遂歸道武，以為右司馬，與張兗等參贊初基。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he returned to Daowu and was made Right Marshal, joining Zhang Gun and others in founding the new order.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Dengguo he returned to Daowu, who made him Right Marshal to help Zhang Gun and others lay the foundations of rule.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶之來寇也，道武使謙告難於姚興。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Daowu sent Qian to report the crisis to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao invaded, Daowu sent Qian to seek aid from Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興遣將楊佛嵩來援。

translations.literal: Xing sent the general Yang Fosong in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xing sent the general Yang Fosong to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 佛嵩稽緩，道武命謙為書遺之，佛嵩乃倍道兼行。

translations.literal: Fosong was slow and dilatory; Daowu ordered Qian to write and send him a letter, and Fosong then marched day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Fosong dragged his feet; Daowu had Qian write to him, and Fosong then pressed forward at double speed.

sentences.zh: 道武大悅，賜謙爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Daowu was greatly pleased and enfeoffed Qian as Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu was delighted and enfeoffed Qian as Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 寶敗，佛嵩乃還。

translations.literal: When Bao was defeated, Fosong returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Bao's defeat, Fosong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及慕容垂死，謙上書勸進。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui died, Qian submitted a memorial urging accession to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui died, Qian memorialized urging Daowu to take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 并州平，以謙為陽曲護軍，賜爵平舒侯。

translations.literal: When Bing Province was pacified, Qian was made Protector of Yangqu and enfeoffed Marquis of Pingshu.
translations.idiomatic: After Bing Province was pacified, Qian became Protector of Yangqu and Marquis of Pingshu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史、高陽公，諡曰文。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Governor of You Province and Duke of Gaoyang, posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Governor of You Province and Duke of Gaoyang, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 子洛陽襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Luoyang inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luoyang succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 明元追錄謙功，以洛陽為雁門太守。

translations.literal: Mingyuan later recorded Qian's service and made Luoyang Governor of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan later honored Qian's service and appointed Luoyang Governor of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 洛陽家田三生嘉禾，皆異畝同穎。

translations.literal: On Luoyang's family fields three stalks of fine grain grew, each with different furrows but a single ear.
translations.idiomatic: On Luoyang's family fields three stalks of fine grain grew, each from a different furrow yet bearing one ear.

sentences.zh: 太武善之，進爵北地公。

translations.literal: Taiwu was pleased and advanced his rank to Duke of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu was pleased and raised him to Duke of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: On his death his posthumous name was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his posthumous name was Gong.

sentences.zh: 崔宏，字玄伯，清河東武城人，魏司空林之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Hong, style name Xuanbo, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe, sixth-generation descendant of Wei Minister of Works Cui Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong, styled Xuanbo, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe, sixth in descent from Cui Lin, Minister of Works of Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖悅，仕石季龍，位司徒右長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue served Shi Jilong as Right Chief Scribe to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yue served Shi Jilong as Right Chief Scribe to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 父潛，仕慕容痈，為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Qian served Murong Yong as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian served Murong Yong as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 並以才學稱。

translations.literal: Both were famed for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Both were renowned for learning and ability.

sentences.zh: 宏少有雋才，號曰冀州神童。

translations.literal: Hong in youth had outstanding talent and was called the divine child of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hong as a youth showed exceptional talent and was called the prodigy of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 苻融之牧冀州，虛心禮敬。

translations.literal: When Fu Rong governed Ji Province he received him with humble courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Rong governed Ji Province he treated Hong with humble respect.

sentences.zh: 拜陽平公侍郎、領冀州從事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman to the Duke of Yangping and Concurrent Administrator of Ji Province retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Gentleman to the Duke of Yangping and Concurrent Administrator of Ji Province staff.

sentences.zh: 出總庶事，入為賓友，眾務修理，處斷無滯。

translations.literal: Going out he oversaw all affairs; coming in he was a guest and companion—all business was put in order and decisions never stalled.
translations.idiomatic: Abroad he managed affairs; at court he was counselor and friend—every task was set in order and nothing hung unresolved.

sentences.zh: 苻堅聞之，徵為太子舍人。

translations.literal: Fu Jian heard of him and summoned him as Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian heard of him and summoned him as Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 辭以母疾，不就。

translations.literal: He declined on grounds of his mother's illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded his mother's illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 左遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Assistant in the Office for Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Assistant in the Office for Compilation.

sentences.zh: 太原郝軒名知人，稱宏有王佐之材，近代所未有也。

translations.literal: Hao Xuan of Taiyuan, famed for knowing men, said Hong had the talent of a chief minister—unmatched in recent generations.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Xuan of Taiyuan, famed for judging men, said Hong had the makings of a chief minister, unmatched in his generation.

sentences.zh: 堅亡，避難齊魯間，為丁零翟釗及晉叛將張願所留。

translations.literal: When Jian fell, Hong took refuge between Qi and Lu and was detained by the Dingling Zhai Zhao and the Jin rebel general Zhang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian's state collapsed, Hong fled to Qi and Lu and was held by the Dingling leader Zhai Zhao and the Jin rebel Zhang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 郝軒歎曰：「斯人也，遇斯時，不因扶搖之勢，而與鴳雀飛沈，豈不惜哉！」

translations.literal: Hao Xuan sighed, "Such a man, in such a time—without the wind beneath a soaring ascent, he sinks and flies with sparrows; how regrettable!"
translations.idiomatic: Hao Xuan sighed, "A man like this, in a time like this—without the updraft of fortune he sinks to fly with sparrows. What a waste!"

sentences.zh: 仕慕容垂，為吏部郎、尚書左丞、高陽內史，所曆著稱。

translations.literal: He served Murong Chui as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Left Assistant in the Secretariat, and Internal Governor of Gaoyang—every post won praise.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Chui as Director of Personnel, Left Assistant in the Secretariat, and Internal Governor of Gaoyang, winning praise in every office.

sentences.zh: 立身雅正，雖在兵亂，獨厲志篤學，不以資產為意，妻子不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Upright in conduct, even amid war he alone kept his will and pursued learning zealously, caring nothing for property; wife and children did not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Upright in character, even in war he held to study and took no thought for wealth; his wife and children knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 道武征慕容寶，次中山。

translations.literal: When Daowu campaigned against Murong Bao he halted at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu marched against Murong Bao he camped at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 棄郡走海濱。

translations.literal: Hong abandoned his commandery and fled to the seacoast.
translations.idiomatic: Hong abandoned his commandery and fled toward the sea.

sentences.zh: 帝素聞其名，遣求。

translations.literal: The emperor had long heard his name and sent men to seek him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long heard of him and sent men to find him.

sentences.zh: 及至，以為黃門侍郎，與張兗對總機要，草創制度。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and, with Zhang Gun, jointly managed the keys of state and drafted institutions anew.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival he was made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; with Zhang Gun he shared control of state affairs and drafted new institutions.

sentences.zh: 時晉使來聘，帝將報之，詔有司議國號。

translations.literal: At that time Jin envoys came on a friendly mission; the emperor wished to respond and ordered the relevant offices to deliberate the state name.
translations.idiomatic: Jin envoys then came on a friendly mission; the emperor wished to reply and ordered deliberation on the dynastic name.

sentences.zh: 宏議曰：「三皇、五帝之立號也，或因所生之土，或以封國之名。

translations.literal: Hong argued, "The titles of the Three August Ones and Five Emperors were sometimes taken from the land where they arose, sometimes from the name of the state they enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong argued, "The Three August Ones and Five Emperors took their titles either from the soil that bore them or from the states they were enfeoffed to rule.

sentences.zh: 故虞、夏、商、周始皆諸侯，及聖德既隆，萬國宗戴，稱號隨本，不復更立。

translations.literal: Thus Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou at first were all feudal lords; when sagely virtue rose high, the myriad states honored them, and their titles followed their origins without change.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou began as feudal lords; when their virtue towered, all realms acclaimed them and their titles kept to their roots without change.

sentences.zh: 唯商人屢徙，改號曰殷。

translations.literal: Only the Shang people moved repeatedly and changed their title to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Shang moved their seat again and again and changed their name to Yin.

sentences.zh: 然猶兼行，不廢始基之號。

translations.literal: Yet both names were still used and the title of the founding base was not cast off.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both names were used together and the founding title was never abandoned.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》云'殷商之旅'，此其義也。

translations.literal: Thus the Odes say 'the host of Yin and Shang'—this is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Odes speak of 'the host of Yin and Shang'—that is the sense.

sentences.zh: 國家雖統北方廣漠之土，逮于陛下，應運龍飛。

translations.literal: Though our state now rules the broad northern wastes, down to Your Majesty it has answered the times and risen like a dragon in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Though our state rules the vast northern wastes, under Your Majesty it has answered Heaven and risen like a dragon.

sentences.zh: 雖曰舊邦，受命惟新。

translations.literal: Though called an old domain, its mandate is wholly new.
translations.idiomatic: Though called an old domain, its mandate is wholly new.

sentences.zh: 以是登國之初改代曰魏。

translations.literal: Therefore at the beginning of Dengguo Dai was changed to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at the opening of Dengguo Dai was renamed Wei.

sentences.zh: 慕容永亦奉進魏土。

translations.literal: Murong Yong also presented the territory of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong likewise offered up the lands of Wei.

sentences.zh: 夫魏者大名州之上國，斯乃革命之征驗，利見之玄符也。

translations.literal: Wei is the great name of a state above the provinces—this is the proof of revolution and the dark sign of favorable seeing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei is the great name of a state above the commanderies—the sign of revolution and the omen of Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜號為魏。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and thinks the title should be Wei.
translations.idiomatic: This humble servant believes the dynastic name should be Wei.

sentences.zh: 」道武從之，於是稱魏。

translations.literal: " Daowu followed this, and thereafter they were called Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu agreed, and from then on they were called Wei.

sentences.zh: 及帝幸鄴，曆問故事。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Ye he questioned him repeatedly on precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Ye he questioned Hong at length on precedent.

sentences.zh: 宏應對若流，帝善之。

translations.literal: Hong answered as if flowing; the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hong answered fluently and won the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 還次恆嶺，帝親登山頂，撫慰新人，適遇宏扶老母登嶺，賜以牛米。

translations.literal: Returning he halted at Mount Heng; the emperor in person climbed the summit to comfort the newly relocated people and happened upon Hong supporting his aged mother up the ridge; he granted them oxen and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he stopped at Mount Heng; the emperor climbed the summit to comfort new settlers and found Hong helping his old mother up the path—he gave them oxen and grain.

sentences.zh: 因詔諸徙人不能自進者，給以車牛。

translations.literal: He then ordered that migrants unable to go on their own be given carts and oxen.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered carts and oxen for migrants who could not travel on foot.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Hong was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時命有司制官爵，撰朝儀，協音樂，定律令，申科禁，宏總而裁之，以為永式。

translations.literal: When orders went out to fix ranks and titles, draft court ritual, harmonize music, establish laws and statutes, and enforce prohibitions, Hong oversaw and trimmed all of it as lasting model.
translations.idiomatic: When the court set ranks and titles, drafted ritual, harmonized music, fixed laws, and enforced prohibitions, Hong directed and shaped them into lasting forms.

sentences.zh: 及置八部大夫，以擬八坐。

translations.literal: When the Eight Departments grandees were established to mirror the Eight Dignitaries,
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Department grandees were created on the model of the Eight Dignitaries,

sentences.zh: 宏通署三十六曹，如令、僕統事。

translations.literal: Hong broadly supervised the thirty-six bureaus like ministers and vice-ministers directing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hong broadly supervised the thirty-six bureaus as ministers and vice-ministers direct government.

sentences.zh: 深被信任，勢傾朝廷。

translations.literal: Deeply trusted, his power tilted the court.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply trusted, his influence dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 約儉自居，不營產業，家徒四壁；

translations.literal: Frugal in his own living, he built no estates; his house had nothing but four bare walls;
translations.idiomatic: He lived frugally and amassed no property; his home was bare to the four walls;

sentences.zh: 出無車乘，朝晡步上。

translations.literal: going out he had no carriage and morning and evening he walked to court.
translations.idiomatic: abroad he had no carriage and walked to court morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 母年七十，供養無重膳。

translations.literal: His mother was seventy; he could not supply her with rich fare.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was seventy and he could not give her lavish meals.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，益重之，厚加饋賜。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he esteemed him all the more and sent rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he esteemed him further and sent generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 時人亦或譏其過約，而宏居之愈甚。

translations.literal: Some in the age also mocked his excessive frugality, yet Hong lived all the more strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked his austerity, yet Hong lived more strictly still.

sentences.zh: 常引問古今舊事，王者制度，宏陳古人製作之體，及往代廢興之由，甚合上意。

translations.literal: He was often summoned to ask about old affairs of past ages and the institutions of kings; Hong set forth the forms of ancient making and the causes of rise and fall in former dynasties, greatly matching the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He was often called to discuss antiquity and royal institutions; Hong explained ancient forms and the causes of dynastic rise and fall, greatly pleasing the emperor.

sentences.zh: 未嘗謇諤忤旨，亦不諂諛苟容。

translations.literal: He never spoke bluntly against the will, nor flattered to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: He never spoke bluntly to offend, nor flattered for favor.

sentences.zh: 及道武季年，大臣多犯威怒，宏獨無譴者，由於此也。

translations.literal: In Daowu's last years many great ministers provoked imperial wrath, yet Hong alone was never punished—because of this.
translations.idiomatic: In Daowu's last years many ministers drew imperial wrath, yet Hong alone was never rebuked—for this reason.

sentences.zh: 帝曾引宏講論《漢書》，至婁敬說漢祖，欲以魯元公主妻匈奴，善之，嗟歎者良久。

translations.literal: The emperor once summoned Hong to discuss the Book of Han; when they came to Lou Jing urging the Han founder to marry the Princess of Lu to the Xiongnu, he was pleased and sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once had Hong discuss the Book of Han; at Lou Jing's counsel to marry the Princess of Lu to the Xiongnu he was pleased and sighed long.

sentences.zh: 是以諸公主皆嫁于賓附之國，朝臣子弟、良族美彥不得尚焉。

translations.literal: Therefore all imperial princesses were married to tributary states; sons of court ministers and fine clans could not marry them.
translations.idiomatic: Hence all imperial princesses were married to tributary states, and courtiers' sons and eminent families could not wed them.

sentences.zh: 尚書職罷，賜宏爵白馬侯，加周兵將軍。

translations.literal: When the Secretariat post was abolished, Hong was enfeoffed Marquis of Baima and made General of Zhoubing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat was abolished, Hong was enfeoffed Marquis of Baima and made General of Zhoubing.

sentences.zh: 與舊功臣庾岳、奚斤等同班，而信寵過之。

translations.literal: He shared rank with old meritocrats Yu Yue and Xi Jin, yet favor and trust passed beyond them.
translations.idiomatic: He stood in the same rank as veterans Yu Yue and Xi Jin, yet enjoyed greater favor.

sentences.zh: 道武崩，明元未即位，清河王紹因人心不安，大出財帛，班賜朝士。

translations.literal: When Daowu died, Mingyuan had not yet taken the throne; the Prince of Qinghe, Shao, because hearts were unsettled, distributed great wealth and silks, bestowing gifts on court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu died, before Mingyuan had taken the throne, Prince Shao of Qinghe, seeing unrest in men's hearts, lavished wealth and silks on the court.

sentences.zh: 宏獨不受紹財，長孫嵩以下咸愧焉。

translations.literal: Hong alone did not accept Shao's gifts; from Changsun Song down all were ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong alone refused Shao's gifts; from Changsun Song downward the courtiers were ashamed.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使者循行郡國，糾察守宰不如法者，令宏與宜都公穆觀等案之，帝稱其平當。

translations.literal: An edict sent envoys to tour the commanderies and kingdoms to investigate governors and magistrates who failed the law, ordering Hong together with the Duke of Yidu, Mu Guan, and others to review them; the emperor praised their fairness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent envoys through the commanderies to investigate lawless officials; Hong and the Duke of Yidu, Mu Guan, and others were ordered to judge the cases, and the emperor praised their fairness.

sentences.zh: 又詔宏與長孫嵩等朝堂決刑獄。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Hong with Changsun Song and others to decide criminal cases in the hall of court.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict set Hong with Changsun Song and others to decide criminal cases in open court.

sentences.zh: 明元以郡國豪右大人蠹害，乃優詔征之。

translations.literal: Mingyuan, because powerful magnates in the commanderies and kingdoms were harming the realm, issued a generous edict summoning them.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan, seeing great local magnates ruining the realm, issued a gentle edict summoning them in.

sentences.zh: 人多戀本，而長吏逼遣之。

translations.literal: Many clung to their homelands while local chiefs forced them to go.
translations.idiomatic: Many wished to stay home while local chiefs drove them onward.

sentences.zh: 於是輕薄少年，因相扇動，所在聚結。

translations.literal: Thereupon frivolous youths stirred one another and bands gathered everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Then idle youths incited one another and bands formed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 西河、建興盜賊並起，守宰討之不能禁。

translations.literal: In Xihé and Jianxing bandits rose together; governors could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose together in Xihé and Jianxing; local officials could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 帝乃引宏及北新侯安同、壽光侯叔孫建、武元城侯元屈等問焉。

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned Hong and the Marquis of Beixin, An Tong, the Marquis of Shouguang, Shusun Jian, the Marquis of Wuyuan, Yuan Qu, and others to ask their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Hong, Marquis An Tong of Beixin, Marquis Shusun Jian of Shouguang, Marquis Yuan Qu of Wuyuan, and others for counsel.

sentences.zh: 宏欲大赦以紓之。

translations.literal: Hong wished a great amnesty to ease the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Hong urged a general amnesty to ease the crisis.

sentences.zh: 屈曰：「不如先誅首惡，赦其黨類。

translations.literal: Qu said, "Better first execute the ringleaders and pardon their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Qu said, "Better first execute the ringleaders and pardon the rest.

sentences.zh: 」宏曰：「王者臨天下，以安人為本，何顧小曲直也。

translations.literal: " Hong said, "A king facing the realm takes securing the people as his root—why fret over petty right and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "A king holds the realm by keeping the people secure—why cling to petty right and wrong?

sentences.zh: 夫赦雖非正道，而可以權行。

translations.literal: Amnesty is not the straight path, yet it may be used as expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty is not orthodox policy, yet it may serve as expedient.

sentences.zh: 若赦而不改，誅之不晚。

translations.literal: If after pardon they do not reform, execution will not be late.
translations.idiomatic: If after pardon they do not reform, punishment can wait no longer.

sentences.zh: 」明元從之。

translations.literal: " Mingyuan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan accepted Hong's view.

sentences.zh: 神瑞初，詔宏與南平公嵩等坐止車門右，聽理機事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenrui an edict set Hong with the Duke of Nanping, Song, and others to sit and halt at the right of the Chariot-Halting Gate and hear weighty affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenrui an edict seated Hong with the Duke of Nanping, Song, and others at the right of the Chariot-Halting Gate to hear state business.

sentences.zh: 并州胡數萬南掠河內，遣將軍公孫表等討之，敗績。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of Hu in Bing Province raided south into Henei; the emperor sent the general Gongsun Biao and others to attack them and they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Hu from Bing Province raided south into Henei; the general Gongsun Biao and others were sent against them and were beaten.

sentences.zh: 帝問計於群臣。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the ministers for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers for counsel.

sentences.zh: 宏曰：「表等諸軍，不為不足，但失於處分，故使小盜假息耳。

translations.literal: Hong said, "Biao's armies and the rest are not insufficient—they only failed in disposition, so petty bandits gained a breathing space.
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "Biao's forces were ample—they only mishandled deployment, letting petty raiders catch their breath.

sentences.zh: 胡眾雖多，而無猛健主將，所謂千奴共一潆詹也。

translations.literal: Though the Hu are many, they have no fierce, able commander-in-chief—what is called a thousand slaves sharing one beam.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Hu are numerous, they lack a fierce chief—they are like a thousand slaves sharing one rafter.

sentences.zh: 宜得大將素為胡所服信者，將數百騎，就攝表軍以討之。

translations.literal: One should get a great general long trusted by the Hu, lead several hundred horsemen, go and take command of Biao's army to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Send a great general the Hu have long trusted, with a few hundred horsemen, to take over Biao's army and strike them.

sentences.zh: 賊聞，必望風震怖。

translations.literal: When the bandits hear it they will surely tremble in fear at the wind.
translations.idiomatic: At the news the raiders will surely break in terror.

sentences.zh: 壽光侯建，前在并州，諸將莫及。

translations.literal: Marquis Shusun Jian, formerly in Bing Province, was unmatched among the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Shusun Jian, who once held Bing Province, outshone every general there.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，遂平胡寇。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this and thereupon pacified the Hu raiders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and the Hu raiders were pacified.

sentences.zh: 尋拜天部大人，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Grandee of the Heavenly Division and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 泰常三年夏，宏病篤，帝遣侍中穆觀就受遺言，侍臣問疾，一夜數返。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year of Taichang, Hong's illness grew grave; the emperor sent the Palace Attendant Mu Guan to receive his last words; attendants inquired after his health and returned several times in one night.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of Taichang year three, Hong grew desperately ill; the emperor sent Palace Attendant Mu Guan for his final counsel; attendants called through the night again and again.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈司空，諡文貞公。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous name Duke Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 喪禮一依安城王叔孫俊故事。

translations.literal: Funeral rites wholly followed the precedent of Prince Ancheng, Shusun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His funeral wholly followed the precedent of Prince Ancheng, Shusun Jun.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣及附國渠帥皆會葬，自親王以外，盡命拜送。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all ministers and attached tribal chieftains to attend the burial; from princes down all were commanded to bow in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required all ministers and subject tribal chiefs to attend; every rank below the princes was ordered to bow him forth.

sentences.zh: 子浩襲。

translations.literal: His son Hao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 太和中，孝文追錄先朝功臣，以宏配饗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Xiaowen recorded the merit of the former court and granted Hong a place in the temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era Xiaowen honored founders of the prior reign and gave Hong a place in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 浩字伯深，少好學。

translations.literal: Hao, style name Boshen, in youth loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, styled Boshen, loved learning from youth.

sentences.zh: 博覽經史，玄象陰陽百家之言，無不該覽。

translations.literal: He broadly read classics and histories, dark signs, yin-yang, and the hundred schools—nothing escaped his survey.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in classics, histories, astronomy, yin-yang, and the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 研精義理，時人莫及。

translations.literal: Probing essence and principle, none of the age could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Probing principle to the root, none of his day could match him.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為通直郎，稍遷著作郎。

translations.literal: At twenty he was Direct Attendant; he was gradually promoted to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was Direct Attendant and later rose to Compiler.

sentences.zh: 道武以其工書，常置左右。

translations.literal: Daowu, because of his skill at calligraphy, kept him constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu kept him always near, for his skill at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 道武季年，威嚴頗峻，宮省左右，多以微過得罪，莫不逃避，隱匿目下之變。

translations.literal: In Daowu's last years his majesty grew stern; many in the palace staff were punished for slight faults, and all fled and hid the changes before their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: In Daowu's last years his wrath was sharp; palace staff were punished for trifles and all hid what they saw.

sentences.zh: 浩獨恭勤不怠，或終日不歸。

translations.literal: Hao alone was respectful and diligent without slackening, sometimes not returning home for a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Hao alone stayed respectful and diligent, sometimes not leaving court for a full day.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，輒命賜以禦粥。

translations.literal: When the emperor learned of it he would order imperial gruel bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of it he sent imperial gruel.

sentences.zh: 其砥直任時，不為窮通改節若此。

translations.literal: His upright bearing in office and refusal to change with fortune or ruin were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his upright service and refusal to bend with fortune or ruin.

sentences.zh: 明元初，拜博士祭酒，賜爵武城子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingyuan he was made Libationer of the Erudites and enfeoffed Viscount of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingyuan's accession he was made Libationer of the Erudites and enfeoffed Viscount of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 常授帝經書，每至郊祀，父子並乘軒軺，時人榮之。

translations.literal: He regularly taught the emperor the classics; whenever they went to suburban sacrifice, father and son both rode in light carriages—the age envied them.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly taught the emperor the classics; at each suburban sacrifice father and son rode in light carriages, to the envy of the court.

sentences.zh: 明元好陰陽術數，聞浩說《易》及《洪範》五行，善之。

translations.literal: Mingyuan loved yin-yang and numerology; hearing Hao explain the Changes and the Great Plan's Five Phases, he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan loved yin-yang and numerology; pleased by Hao's lectures on the Changes and the Five Phases of the Great Plan,

sentences.zh: 因命筮吉凶，參觀天文，考定疑惑。

translations.literal: He then ordered divination of fortune and ill, joint observation of the heavens, and fixing of doubtful matters.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered Hao to divine fortune, scan the heavens, and settle doubtful matters.

sentences.zh: 浩總核天人之際，舉其綱紀者，數家多有應驗。

translations.literal: Hao grasped the junction of Heaven and man and set forth their guiding threads; many families had verified results.
translations.idiomatic: Hao mastered the meeting of Heaven and man and laid out their patterns; many of his forecasts proved true.

sentences.zh: 恆與軍國大謀，甚為寵密。

translations.literal: He was constantly joined to the great plans of army and state and was deeply favored in secret.
translations.idiomatic: He was constantly drawn into army and state plans and enjoyed deep, secret favor.

sentences.zh: 時有兔在後宮，檢無從得入，帝令浩推之。

translations.literal: At the time a hare appeared in the rear palace and search found no way it could have entered; the emperor ordered Hao to deduce it.
translations.idiomatic: A hare then appeared in the inner palace with no entry found; the emperor had Hao reason it out.

sentences.zh: 浩以為當有鄰國貢嬪嬙者。

translations.literal: Hao judged that a neighboring state would present a tribute concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said a neighboring state would soon send a tribute woman.

sentences.zh: 明年，姚興果獻女。

translations.literal: The next year Yao Xing indeed presented a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yao Xing did present a daughter.

sentences.zh: 神瑞二年，秋穀不登，太史令王亮、蘇坦因華陰公主等言：「讖書云：國家當都鄴，大樂五十年。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenrui the autumn grain failed; the Grand Astrologer Wang Liang and Su Tan, through Princess Huayin and others, said, "Prognostic books say the state should move its capital to Ye and great music for fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenrui year two the autumn crop failed; Grand Astrologers Wang Liang and Su Tan, through Princess Huayin and others, said, "Prognostic books say the capital should move to Ye and great fortune for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 」勸帝遷都於鄴，可救今年之饑。

translations.literal: " They urged the emperor to move the capital to Ye to relieve this year's famine.
translations.idiomatic: They urged moving the capital to Ye to ease the famine.

sentences.zh: 帝以問浩。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「非長久策也。

translations.literal: Hao said, "That is not a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "That is no lasting policy.

sentences.zh: 東州之人，常謂國家居廣漠之地，人畜無算，號稱牛毛之眾。

translations.literal: The people of the eastern provinces constantly say the state dwells in a vast waste, men and beasts beyond counting, called a host like ox-hair.
translations.idiomatic: Easterners constantly say we live in boundless wastes, with men and beasts beyond count, like ox-hair on a hide.

sentences.zh: 今留守舊都，分家南徙，恐不滿諸州之地。

translations.literal: Now if the old capital is left guarded while families move south, I fear they will not fill the lands of the commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: If we leave the old capital lightly held while families move south, they may not even fill the eastern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 參居郡縣，處榛林之下，不便水土，疾疫死傷，情見事露，則百姓意阻。

translations.literal: Scattered among counties, dwelling beneath scrub forest, unaccustomed to soil and water, plague and death will show the matter plainly; the people's will will falter.
translations.idiomatic: Set among counties under scrub and forest, unfit for soil and water, sickness and death will expose the plan and hearts will fail.

sentences.zh: 四方聞之，有輕侮之意，屈丐及蠕蠕必提挈而來。

translations.literal: When the four quarters hear it they will hold us in light contempt; Juqu and the Rouran will surely seize the moment and come.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm hears, contempt will follow; Juqu and the Rouran will surely press in.

sentences.zh: 雲中、平城則有危殆之事，阻隔恆、代，千里之際，須欲救援，赴之甚難。

translations.literal: Yunzhong and Pingcheng will face peril; Heng and Dai cut off, a thousand li apart—rescue will be desperately hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong and Pingcheng will be in peril; Heng and Dai cut off a thousand li away, rescue will come too late.

sentences.zh: 如此，則聲實俱損矣。

translations.literal: Thus fame and substance will both suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Fame and strength will both be lost.

sentences.zh: 今居北方，假令山東有變，輕騎南出，燿威桑梓之中，誰知多少？

translations.literal: To dwell in the north now—suppose the east should stir, light horse can ride south and blaze glory in the homeland—who knows how many would submit?
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in the north, if the east should stir, light cavalry can ride south and awe the homeland—who knows how many would bow?

sentences.zh: 百姓見之，望塵震伏。

translations.literal: When the people see it they will turn to dust in fear and submission.
translations.idiomatic: The people would see them and tremble into submission.

sentences.zh: 此是國家威制諸夏之長策也。

translations.literal: This is the state's long strategy for commanding the Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: That is the long strategy for ruling the Huaxia.

sentences.zh: 至春草生，乳酪將出，兼有菜果，足接來秋。

translations.literal: When spring grass grows and dairy and cheese come forth, with vegetables and fruit as well, it will suffice until the coming autumn.
translations.idiomatic: When spring grass returns and dairy comes, with vegetables and fruit besides, we can hold until autumn.

sentences.zh: 若得中熟，事則濟矣。

translations.literal: If the middle harvest succeeds, the matter is saved.
translations.idiomatic: If the mid-year crop succeeds, the crisis passes.

sentences.zh: 」帝深然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was fully convinced.

sentences.zh: 復使中貴人問浩曰：「今既無以至來秋，或復不熟，將如之何？

translations.literal: He again sent a palace favorite to ask Hao, "Now we have nothing to carry us to next autumn, or the crop may again fail—what then?
translations.idiomatic: He again sent a palace officer to ask Hao, "We may not last until next autumn, or the crop may fail again—what then?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「可簡窮下之戶，諸州就穀。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "Select the poorest households and send the commanderies to gather grain where it may be found.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Relieve the poorest households and send the commanderies to gather grain where it exists.

sentences.zh: 若秋無年，願更圖也。

translations.literal: If autumn brings no harvest, we may plan again—but the capital must not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: If autumn fails, we can plan anew—but do not move the capital.

sentences.zh: 但不可遷都。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon divided people to seek food in the three eastern provinces and opened granaries to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent people to the three eastern provinces for grain and opened storehouses to feed them.

sentences.zh: 」帝於是分人詣山東三州就食，出倉穀以稟之。

translations.literal: The next year brought a great harvest; Hao was given a concubine each and imperial robes of silk and cotton.
translations.idiomatic: The next year brought abundance; Hao received a concubine each and imperial silks.

sentences.zh: 來年遂大熟，賜浩妾各一人，及御衣綿絹等。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the year before Yao Xing's death, the astrologers reported Mars in the Dipper constellation; one night it suddenly vanished, none knew where.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the year before Yao Xing died, astrologers reported Mars in the Dipper; one night it vanished, none knew where.

sentences.zh: 初，姚興死之前歲，太史奏熒惑在匏瓜星中，一夜忽然亡失，不知所在。

translations.literal: Some said it had entered a state on the brink of ruin and would bring children's songs and strange talk before the disaster struck.
translations.idiomatic: Some said it had entered a doomed state and would bring ballads and omens before disaster fell.

sentences.zh: 或謂下入危亡之國，將為童謠妖言，而後行其災禍。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned eminent Confucians and the clerks to seek where it had gone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned leading scholars and clerks to find its course.

sentences.zh: 帝乃召諸碩儒，與史官求其所詣。

translations.literal: Hao replied, "According to the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a spirit descended on Mount Cui, on the day of arrival each thing had its sign.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "The Zuo Commentary says when a spirit descended on Mount Cui, on the day of arrival each thing had its sign.

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「案《春秋左氏傅》說神降於萃，其至之日，各其物也。

translations.literal: Please calculate by day and branch.
translations.idiomatic: Calculate by the day and its branches.

sentences.zh: 請以日辰推之。

translations.literal: On the evening of gengwu and the morning of xinwei the sky was cloudy; Mars's disappearance should fall within these two days.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of gengwu and morning of xinwei the sky was overcast; Mars's vanishing should fall within those two days.

sentences.zh: 庚午之夕，辛未之朝，天有陰雲，熒惑之亡，當在此二日之內。

translations.literal: Geng and wu both belong to Qin; xin is the western barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Geng and wu both belong to Qin; xin marks the western Yi.

sentences.zh: 庚與午，皆主于秦，辛為西夷。

translations.literal: Now Yao Xing holds Xianyang—Mars has entered Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing holds Xianyang—Mars has entered Qin.

sentences.zh: 今姚興據咸陽，是熒惑入秦矣。

translations.literal: " All changed color and said, "A star lost in heaven—how can a man know where it goes and speak groundless words!
translations.idiomatic: All flushed and said, "A star is lost in heaven—how can a man know its path and speak without proof!

sentences.zh: 」諸人皆作色曰：「天上失星，人安能知其所詣，而妄說無征之言！

translations.literal: " Hao smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Hao smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 」浩笑而不應。

translations.literal: After more than eighty days Mars indeed came forth at the Well constellation and lingered there.
translations.idiomatic: After eighty-odd days Mars indeed appeared at the Well and lingered there.

sentences.zh: 後八十餘日，熒惑果出東井，留守盤旋。

translations.literal: In Qin a great drought scorched the land; the Kunming Pool dried up.
translations.idiomatic: Qin suffered great drought; the Kunming Pool ran dry.

sentences.zh: 秦中大旱赤地，昆明池水竭。

translations.literal: Children's ballads and false talk made the realm clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: Ballads and rumors threw the realm into uproar.

sentences.zh: 童謠訛言，國中喧擾。

translations.literal: The next year Yao Xing died; his two sons fought each other and in three years the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yao Xing died; his two sons fought and in three years the state was gone.

sentences.zh: 明年，姚興死，二子交兵，三年國滅。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Then all were convinced.

sentences.zh: 於是諸人乃服。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang the Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, wishing to ascend the river westward and request passage.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang year one the Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong and asked to march up the river west with passage granted.

sentences.zh: 泰常元年，晉將劉裕伐姚泓，欲泝河西上，求假道。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered deliberation among the ministers.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣議之。

translations.literal: The outer court dukes and ministers all said, "Hangu Pass is heaven's barrier—how can Yu enter west?
translations.idiomatic: The outer court said, "Hangu Pass is heaven's rampart—how could Yu enter the west?

sentences.zh: 外朝公卿咸曰：「函谷天險，裕何能西入？

translations.literal: He proclaims attack on Yao but his intent may be hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: He claims to attack Yao but his aim may be obscure.

sentences.zh: 揚言伐姚，意或難測。

translations.literal: We should first send troops to cut the upper river and not let him pass west.
translations.idiomatic: Send troops first to block the upper river and forbid his westward march.

sentences.zh: 宜先發軍斷河上流，勿令西過。

translations.literal: " The inner court wholly agreed with the outer plan; the emperor was about to follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The inner court agreed; the emperor was ready to follow.

sentences.zh: 」內朝咸同外計，帝將從之。

translations.literal: Hao said, "This is not the superior plan.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "That is not the best course.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「此非上策也。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi and his faction are harrying Jing Province; Liu Yu has long gnashed his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi's faction troubles Jing Province; Liu Yu has long burned for revenge.

sentences.zh: 司馬休之徒擾其荊州，劉裕切齒久矣。

translations.literal: Now with Xing dead and the heir young, striking their peril and ruin—by my reading he is sure to enter the Pass himself.
translations.idiomatic: With Xing dead and the heir a child, he will seize their weakness—I read his intent as certain entry into the Pass.

sentences.zh: 今興死子幼，乘其危亡而伐之，臣觀其意，必自入關。

translations.literal: A man fierce and rash does not look to later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Men fierce and rash do not weigh later harm.

sentences.zh: 勁躁之人，不顧後患。

translations.literal: If we now block his western road, Yu will surely come ashore and raid north.
translations.idiomatic: Block his western road now and Yu will surely land and raid north.

sentences.zh: 今若塞其西路，裕必上岸北侵。

translations.literal: Then Yao will be unharmed while we bear the blow.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yao is untouched while we take the blow.

sentences.zh: 如此則姚無事而我受敵矣。

translations.literal: The Rouran raid within; grain is again scarce—send troops south and the northern foe advances;
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran raid within and grain runs short—send armies south and the northern enemy presses in;

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕內寇，人食又乏，發軍赴南，則北冠進擊；

translations.literal: if we rescue the north, the southern provinces are again in peril—better grant passage on the waterway and let Yu go west.
translations.idiomatic: rescue the north and the south is endangered again—better grant the water road and let Yu go west.

sentences.zh: 若其救北，則南州復危，未若假之水道，縱裕西入。

translations.literal: Then raise troops to block his road east when he returns.
translations.idiomatic: Then raise troops to block his road home to the east.

sentences.zh: 然後興兵塞其東歸之路。

translations.literal: This is what is called Bian Zhuang stabbing the leopard and gaining both—
translations.idiomatic: This is Bian Zhuang stabbing the leopard—gaining both at once—

sentences.zh: 所謂卞莊刺彪，兩得之勢也。

translations.literal: the posture of gaining both.
translations.idiomatic: the posture of winning both prizes.

sentences.zh: 使裕勝也，必德我假道之惠；

translations.literal: If Yu wins he will surely be grateful for our grace in granting passage;
translations.idiomatic: If Yu wins he will owe us for the passage we granted;

sentences.zh: 令姚氏勝也，亦不失救鄰之名。

translations.literal: if the Yao clan wins we likewise do not lose the name of aiding a neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: if Yao wins we still keep the name of aiding a neighbor.

sentences.zh: 縱裕得關中，懸遠難守。

translations.literal: Even if Yu takes Guanzhong, it hangs far and is hard to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yu takes Guanzhong, it lies far and he cannot hold it.

sentences.zh: 彼不能守，終為我物。

translations.literal: He cannot hold it—ultimately it becomes our possession.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot hold it—in the end it becomes ours.

sentences.zh: 今不勞兵馬，坐觀成敗，鬥兩彪而收長久之利，上策也。

translations.literal: Now without troubling horses and troops, sit and watch success and failure, fight two leopards and reap lasting gain—this is the superior plan.
translations.idiomatic: Without moving horses or troops, sit and watch the contest, let two leopards fight and reap lasting gain—that is the superior plan.

sentences.zh: 夫為國之計，擇利為之，豈顧婚姻，酬一女子之惠也？

translations.literal: In planning for a state one chooses profit—why heed marriage bonds or repay the favor of one woman?
translations.idiomatic: States choose profit—why heed marriage ties or repay one woman's favor?

sentences.zh: 假國家棄恆山以南，裕必不能發吳越之兵爭守河北也。

translations.literal: Even if the state abandoned lands south of Mount Heng, Yu could not raise Wu-Yue armies to contest Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we abandoned lands south of Mount Heng, Yu could not raise Wu and Yue armies to fight for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 」議者猶曰：「裕西入函谷，則進退路窮，腹背受敵。

translations.literal: " The debaters still said, "If Yu enters Hangu westward his advance and retreat are cut off and he suffers foe before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: Critics still said, "If Yu enters Hangu from the west he is trapped with enemies fore and aft.

sentences.zh: 北上岸，則姚軍必不出關助我。

translations.literal: If he comes ashore north, Yao's army will surely not leave the Pass to aid us.
translations.idiomatic: If he lands north, Yao's army will not leave the Pass to help us.

sentences.zh: 揚聲西行，意在北進，其勢然也。

translations.literal: Proclaiming march west while intent is north—that is how the momentum runs.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaims a western march while aiming north—that is how the thrust runs.

sentences.zh: 」帝遂從群議，遣長孫嵩拒之。

translations.literal: " The emperor then followed the assembly and sent Changsun Song to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed the assembly and sent Changsun Song to block him.

sentences.zh: 戰于畔城，為晉將硃超石所敗。

translations.literal: They fought at Pancheng and were defeated by the Jin general Zhu Chaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: They fought at Pancheng and were beaten by the Jin general Zhu Chaoshi.

sentences.zh: 帝恨不用浩言。

translations.literal: The emperor regretted not using Hao's words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted not taking Hao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 二年，晉齊郡太守王懿來降。

translations.literal: In the second year the Jin Governor of Qi Commandery, Wang Yi, came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In year two the Jin Governor of Qi Commandery, Wang Yi, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 陳計，稱劉裕在洛，勸以軍絕其後路，則裕軍不戰而可克。

translations.literal: He offered a plan, saying Liu Yu was at Luoyang and urging that troops be sent to cut his rear so Yu's army could be taken without battle.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that with Liu Yu at Luoyang, troops should cut his rear so Yu's army could be taken without fighting.

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝善之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 會浩在前，進講書傳。

translations.literal: Hao happened to be before him lecturing on texts.
translations.idiomatic: Hao happened to be before him lecturing on the classics.

sentences.zh: 帝問浩曰：「裕西伐已至潼關，卿觀事得濟否？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Hao, "Yu has marched west to attack and has reached Tong Pass—do you think the affair will succeed?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Hao, "Yu has marched west to Tong Pass—will he succeed?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「姚興好養虛名而無實用，子泓又病，眾叛親離。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "Yao Xing loved empty fame without real use; his son Hong is ill and the masses have turned away.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Yao Xing cultivated empty fame without substance; his son Hong is sick and men have deserted him.

sentences.zh: 乘其危亡，兵精將勇，克之必矣。

translations.literal: Strike their peril and ruin with keen troops and brave generals—conquest is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Strike their weakness with keen troops and brave generals—victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「裕武能何如慕容垂？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "How does Yu's martial ability compare with Murong Chui?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How does Yu's martial prowess compare with Murong Chui?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「垂承父祖之資，生便尊貴。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "Chui inherited his father's and grandfather's resources and was noble from birth.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Chui inherited power and was noble from birth.

sentences.zh: 同類歸之，若夜蛾之赴火；

translations.literal: His kind rallied to him like moths to flame;
translations.idiomatic: His kind flocked to him like moths to flame;

sentences.zh: 少加倚仗，便足立功。

translations.literal: with slight support he could achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: with slight backing he could win glory.

sentences.zh: 劉裕挺出寒微，不因一卒之用，奮臂大呼，而夷滅桓玄。

translations.literal: Liu Yu rose from bitter poverty; without the use of a single soldier he raised his arm and shouted and destroyed Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu rose from deep poverty; without a single soldier's rank he raised his arm, shouted, and destroyed Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 北禽慕容超，南摧盧循。

translations.literal: North he seized Murong Chao; south he shattered Lu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: North he took Murong Chao; south he broke Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 裕若平姚而篡其主。

translations.literal: If Yu pacifies Yao he will usurp his master.
translations.idiomatic: If Yu pacifies Yao he will supplant his lord.

sentences.zh: 秦地戎夷混並，裕亦不能守之。

translations.literal: The Qin lands mix Di and Yi; Yu likewise cannot hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Qin mixes Di and Yi peoples; Yu cannot hold it either.

sentences.zh: 秦地亦終當為國家所有。

translations.literal: Qin in the end will belong to our state.
translations.idiomatic: Qin will in the end belong to us.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「裕已入關，不能進，不能退，我遣精騎南襲彭城、壽春，裕亦何能自立？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Yu has entered the Pass and cannot advance or retreat—if I send elite horse south to strike Pengcheng and Shouchun, how can Yu stand alone?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yu is in the Pass, unable to advance or retreat—if I send elite cavalry south against Pengcheng and Shouchun, how can he stand alone?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「今西北二寇未殄，陛下不可親禦六師。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "The northwestern foes are not yet destroyed; Your Majesty cannot personally lead the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Foes in the northwest are not yet crushed; Your Majesty cannot lead the Six Armies in person.

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩有經國之用，無進取之能，非劉裕敵也。

translations.literal: Changsun Song has talent for governing the state but not for aggressive advance—he is no match for Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Song can govern but cannot press an attack—he is no match for Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 臣謂待之不晚。

translations.literal: I say waiting is not late.
translations.idiomatic: I say to wait is not too late.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「卿量之已審矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed and said, "Your measure is already settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed, "Your judgment is already made.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「臣常私論近世人物，不敢不上聞。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "Your servant has often privately judged men of recent times and dares not withhold it from Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "I have often privately weighed men of recent times and dare not withhold it.

sentences.zh: 若王猛之經國，苻堅之管仲也；

translations.literal: Wang Meng in governing the state was Fu Jian's Guan Zhong;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng governing the state was Fu Jian's Guan Zhong;

sentences.zh: 慕容恪之輔少主，慕容痈之霍光也；

translations.literal: Murong Ke in assisting the young lord, Murong Chui was Murong Jun's Huo Guang;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke guiding a young ruler, Murong Chui was Murong Jun's Huo Guang;

sentences.zh: 劉裕之平逆亂，司馬德宗之曹操也。

translations.literal: Liu Yu in pacifying rebellion was Sima Dezong's Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu crushing rebellion was Sima Dezong's Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿謂先帝如何？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "What do you say of the late emperor?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What of the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「太祖用漠北淳樸之人，南入漢地，變風易俗，化洽四海。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "The Grand Ancestor used the plain folk of the desert north, entered the Han lands, changed customs, and transformed the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "The Grand Ancestor took the plain folk of the northern wastes, entered the Han lands, changed customs, and harmonized the realm.

sentences.zh: 自與羲、農、舜、禹齊烈，臣豈能仰名。

translations.literal: He stands with Fu Xi, Shennong, Yao, and Shun—how could your servant presume to name him?
translations.idiomatic: He stands with Fu Xi, Shennong, Yao, and Shun—I cannot presume to name his rank.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「屈丐何如？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "What of Juqu?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What of Juqu?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「屈丐家國夷滅，一身孤寄，為姚氏封植。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "Juqu's house and state were destroyed; he alone clings in exile, fostered by the Yao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Juqu's house and state are gone; he clings alone in exile, kept alive by Yao.

sentences.zh: 不思樹党強鄰，報復仇恥，乃結蠕蠕，背德于姚。

translations.literal: He does not think to build factions and strengthen neighbors or repay the shame of revenge, but instead joins the Rouran and turns his back on Yao's grace.
translations.idiomatic: He does not build alliances or avenge his shame but joins the Rouran and betrays Yao.

sentences.zh: 撅豎小人，無大經略，正可殘暴，終為人殘滅耳。

translations.literal: A petty upstart without great strategy—fit only for brutality, in the end to be destroyed by others.
translations.idiomatic: A petty upstart without grand strategy—fit only for cruelty, in the end to be destroyed by others.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，說至中夜。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased and talked until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and talked until midnight.

sentences.zh: 賜浩縹醪酒十斛，水精戎鹽一兩，曰：「朕味卿言，若此鹽酒，故與卿同其味也。」

translations.literal: He granted Hao ten hu of pale ale and one liang of crystal war-salt, saying, "I taste your words as I taste this salt and wine—therefore I share the flavor with you."
translations.idiomatic: He gave Hao ten hu of pale ale and one liang of crystal war-salt, saying, "I savor your words as this salt and wine—so I share the taste with you."

sentences.zh: 三年，彗星出天津，入太微，經北斗，絡紫微，犯天棓。

translations.literal: In the third year a comet came forth at Tianjin, entered Taiwei, passed the Northern Dipper, threaded Ziwei, and violated Tianbang.
translations.idiomatic: In year three a comet appeared at Tianjin, entered Taiwei, crossed the Northern Dipper, threaded Ziwei, and struck Tianbang.

sentences.zh: 八十餘日，至天漢而滅。

translations.literal: For more than eighty days it reached the Heavenly River and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: For eighty-odd days it reached the Heavenly River and faded.

sentences.zh: 帝復召諸儒、術士問之，曰：「災咎將在何國？

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned Confucians and technicians and asked, "In which state will the disaster fall?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again summoned scholars and technicians and asked, "Which state will bear the omen?

sentences.zh: 朕甚畏之。

translations.literal: I greatly fear it.
translations.idiomatic: I fear it deeply.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「災異由人而起，人無ＩＯ，妖不自作。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "Strange events arise from men; when men harbor no fault, portents do not arise of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Omens rise from men; when men harbor no fault, portents do not arise of themselves.

sentences.zh: 《漢書》載王莽篡位之前，彗星出入，正與今同。

translations.literal: The Book of Han records that before Wang Mang usurped the throne the comet's coming and going was exactly as today.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han records that before Wang Mang seized the throne the comet's course matched today's.

sentences.zh: 國家主尊臣卑，人無異望。

translations.literal: Our state has a respected lord and humble ministers; the people have no other wish.
translations.idiomatic: Our state has a revered lord and humble ministers; the people have no other wish.

sentences.zh: 是為僭晉將滅，劉裕篡之之應也。

translations.literal: This is the response to Jin's usurpation about to perish and Liu Yu's seizure of it.
translations.idiomatic: This answers to Jin's usurping house about to fall and Liu Yu's seizure of it.

sentences.zh: 」諸人莫能易浩言，帝深然之。

translations.literal: " None could overturn Hao's words; the emperor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: None could refute Hao; the emperor was fully convinced.

sentences.zh: 五年，宋果代晉，南鎮上宋改元赦書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Song indeed replaced Jin; the southern garrisons presented Song's amnesty changing the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Song replaced Jin; southern garrisons presented Song's amnesty and new era name.

sentences.zh: 時帝幸東南舄氵齒池，射鳥，聞之，驛馳召浩，告曰：「往年卿言彗星之占驗矣。

translations.literal: The emperor was then at the southeastern Chichi Pool shooting birds; hearing it, he sent post-horses to summon Hao and told him, "Years ago you spoke of the comet's verification—it has come true.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shooting birds at the southeastern Chichi Pool; hearing the news he summoned Hao by post horse and said, "Years ago your comet reading proved true.

sentences.zh: 朕今日始信天道。

translations.literal: Today I first trust Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: Today I first trust Heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 」初，浩父疾篤。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hao's father was gravely ill,
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Hao's father lay gravely ill,

sentences.zh: 乃翦爪截發，夜在庭中仰禱鬥極，為父請命，求以身代。

translations.literal: he cut his nails and clipped his hair and at night in the courtyard prayed upward to the Dipper Pole, begging life for his father and asking to die in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Hao cut his nails and hair and at night in the courtyard prayed to the Pole Star, begging life for his father and offering his own in exchange.

sentences.zh: 叩頭流血，歲餘不息，家人罕有知者。

translations.literal: He knocked his head until blood flowed for more than a year without cease; few in the household knew.
translations.idiomatic: He knocked his head until blood ran for more than a year; few in the household knew.

sentences.zh: 及父終，居喪盡禮，時人稱之。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning in full rite; the age praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he mourned in full rite; the age praised him.

sentences.zh: 襲爵白馬公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Baima.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the dukedom of Baima.

sentences.zh: 自朝廷禮儀，優文策詔，軍國書記，盡關於浩。

translations.literal: From court ritual and elegant documents, policy edicts, and army-state records, all passed through Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual, edicts, policy documents, and military records all passed through Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩能為雅說，不長屬文，而留心於制度科律及經術之言。

translations.literal: Hao could deliver elegant discourse but was not skilled at linked prose; he focused on institutions, statutes, and classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Hao excelled at refined discourse but not at literary composition; he focused on institutions, law, and classical learning.

sentences.zh: 作《家祭法》，次序五宗，蒸嘗之禮，豐儉之節，義理可觀。

translations.literal: He composed a Family Sacrificial Code, ordering the five ancestral lines and the rites of seasonal offering, with rules of abundance and restraint that could be admired for principle.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a Family Sacrificial Code, ordering the five lines of ancestry and seasonal rites with rules of plenty and restraint that stood on principle.

sentences.zh: 性不好莊老之書，每讀不過數十行，輒棄之，曰：「此矯誣之說，不近人情，必非老子所作。

translations.literal: By nature he disliked Zhuangzi and Laozi; after a few tens of lines he would cast them aside, saying, "These are deceiving doctrines, remote from human feeling—they cannot be Laozi's own work.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked Zhuangzi and Laozi; after a few dozen lines he would cast them aside, saying, "These are deceiving doctrines, remote from human feeling—they cannot be Laozi's work.

sentences.zh: 老聃習禮，仲尼所師，豈設敗法之言以亂先王之教。

translations.literal: Old Dan studied ritual and was teacher to Confucius—how could he set words to ruin law and disorder the teaching of the former kings?
translations.idiomatic: Old Dan studied ritual and was Confucius's teacher—how could he write to ruin law and disorder the sages' teaching?

sentences.zh: 袁生所謂家人筐篋中物，不可揚于王庭。」

translations.literal: What Yuan Sheng called household goods in a basket—things not to be displayed in the royal court."
translations.idiomatic: What Yuan Sheng called goods kept in a family basket—not to be aired in the royal court."

sentences.zh: 帝恆有微疾，而災異屢見，乃使中貴人密問浩曰：「今茲日蝕於胃、昴，盡光趙、代之分野。

translations.literal: The emperor constantly had slight illness while strange events repeatedly appeared; he sent a palace favorite to ask Hao in secret, "This year the sun is eclipsed in the Stomach and Pleiades, wholly darkening the territories of Zhao and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often fell ill while omens multiplied; he secretly asked Hao, "This year the sun eclipses the Stomach and Pleiades, darkening the territories of Zhao and Dai.

sentences.zh: 朕疾疹彌年，恐一旦奄忽，諸子並少，其為我設圖後計。

translations.literal: My illness has lasted years; I fear sudden collapse—the sons are all young; devise a plan for afterward for me.
translations.idiomatic: My illness has lasted years; I fear sudden death—all my sons are young; plan for what follows.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「陛下春秋富盛，聖業方融，德以除災，幸就平愈。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "Your Majesty's years are still full and the sacred enterprise is unfolding; virtue removes disaster—may you recover in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Your years are still full and your sacred work is rising; virtue dispels disaster—you will recover in peace.

sentences.zh: 昔宋景見災修德，熒惑退舍。

translations.literal: In old times Song Jing saw disaster and cultivated virtue, and Mars withdrew its lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing once met omens with virtue and Mars withdrew.

sentences.zh: 願陛下遺諸憂慮，恬神保和，無以暗昧之說，致損聖思。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to put aside anxious thoughts, calm the spirit and preserve harmony, and not let obscure doctrines harm your sacred mind.
translations.idiomatic: Put aside anxious thoughts, calm your spirit, and do not let obscure doctrines harm your mind.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，請陳瞽言。

translations.literal: If it must be, I offer blind words.
translations.idiomatic: If you must have counsel, I offer blind words.

sentences.zh: 自聖化龍興，不崇儲貳，是以永興之始，社稷幾危。

translations.literal: Since the sacred transformation rose like a dragon, the heir apparent has not been honored—thus at the beginning of Yongxing the altars nearly fell.
translations.idiomatic: Since the sacred rise, the heir has not been firmly established—at the opening of Yongxing the altars nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 今宜早建東宮，選公卿忠賢陛下素所委仗者，使為師傅；

translations.literal: Now the Eastern Palace should be built early; choose among the dukes and ministers loyal and worthy whom Your Majesty has long trusted to be tutors;
translations.idiomatic: Build the Eastern Palace early; choose loyal ministers you have long trusted as tutors;

sentences.zh: 左右信臣簡在帝心者，以充賓友。

translations.literal: choose trusted ministers close to Your Majesty's heart to fill the posts of guests and companions.
translations.idiomatic: choose trusted men close to your heart as companions.

sentences.zh: 入總萬機，出統戎政，監國撫軍，六柄在手。

translations.literal: Entering, grasp the myriad engines; going out, command military affairs; oversee the state and comfort the armies—the six handles in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Let him govern within, command armies without, oversee the realm and comfort the hosts—six handles in his grasp.

sentences.zh: 若此，則陛下可以優遊無為，頤神養壽。

translations.literal: Then Your Majesty may roam free without labor, nurturing spirit and prolonging life.
translations.idiomatic: Then Your Majesty may roam at ease, nurturing spirit and prolonging life.

sentences.zh: 此乃萬代之令典，塞禍之大備也。

translations.literal: This is the eternal statute of ten thousand generations and the great safeguard against calamity.
translations.idiomatic: That is the eternal statute and the great safeguard against calamity.

sentences.zh: 今長皇子諱，年漸一紀，明睿溫和，眾情所系，時登儲副，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: The eldest imperial son, taboo name Tao, is nearing twelve, bright, gentle, and the hope of all hearts—if he is installed as heir, the realm will be fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Tao is nearing twelve, bright and gentle, the hope of all—install him as heir and the realm is blessed.

sentences.zh: 立子以長，禮之大經，若須並大，成人而擇，倒錯天倫，則生履霜堅冰之禍。

translations.literal: To establish the eldest son is the great canon of ritual; if all must be grown before choosing, reversing the natural order brings the calamity of treading on thin ice over deep water.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son is ritual's great canon; wait until all are grown and you reverse heaven's order and invite the calamity of thin ice.

sentences.zh: 自古以來，載籍所記，興衰存亡，鮮不由此。

translations.literal: From antiquity in the records, rise, fall, survival, and ruin—few are without this cause.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity in the records, few rises and falls lack this cause.

sentences.zh: 」帝納之，於是使浩奉策告宗廟，令太武為國副主，居正殿臨朝。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted it; he then had Hao present the edict at the ancestral temple, made Taiwu national deputy, and had him preside at the main hall in court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; Hao presented the edict at the ancestral temple, made Taiwu national deputy to preside in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 司徒長孫嵩、高陽公奚斤、北新公安同為左輔，坐東廂，西面。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Changsun Song, Duke of Gaoyang Xi Jin, and Duke of Beixin An Tong were left assistants, seated in the east wing facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Changsun Song, Duke Xi Jin of Gaoyang, and Duke An Tong of Beixin were left assistants in the east wing, facing west.

sentences.zh: 浩與太尉穆觀、散騎常侍丘堆為右弼，坐西廂，東面。

translations.literal: Hao with Grand Marshal Mu Guan and Palace Attendant Qiu Dui were right assistants, seated in the west wing facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Hao with Grand Marshal Mu Guan and Palace Attendant Qiu Dui were right assistants in the west wing, facing east.

sentences.zh: 百寮總己以聽焉。

translations.literal: The hundred offices were wholly subject to their hearing.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred offices reported wholly to them.

sentences.zh: 明元居西宮，時隱而窺之，聽其決斷。

translations.literal: Mingyuan dwelt in the Western Palace and sometimes hid to watch, listening to their decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan stayed in the Western Palace and sometimes watched in secret, listening to their judgments.

sentences.zh: 大悅，謂左右侍臣曰：「長孫嵩宿德舊臣，曆事四世，功存社稷；

translations.literal: Greatly pleased, he told the attendants at his side, "Changsun Song is an old minister of long virtue, serving four reigns, merit preserved in the altars;
translations.idiomatic: Greatly pleased, he told his attendants, "Changsun Song is an old minister of four reigns whose merit preserved the altars;

sentences.zh: 奚斤辯捷智謀，名聞遐邇；

translations.literal: Xi Jin is quick-witted in debate and famed far and near;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin is quick in debate and famed far and wide;

sentences.zh: 安同曉解俗情，明於校練；

translations.literal: An Tong understands popular feeling and is clear in drill and training;
translations.idiomatic: An Tong understands the people and excels at drill;

sentences.zh: 穆觀達政事要，識吾旨趣；

translations.literal: Mu Guan grasps the essentials of government and knows my intent;
translations.idiomatic: Mu Guan grasps government and knows my mind;

sentences.zh: 崔浩博聞強識，精於天人之會；

translations.literal: Cui Hao is broadly learned with strong memory, skilled in the meeting of Heaven and man;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao is learned with prodigious memory, skilled in Heaven and man;

sentences.zh: 丘堆雖無大用，然在公專謹。

translations.literal: Qiu Dui though without great use is scrupulous in public duty.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Dui lacks grand talent but is scrupulous in office.

sentences.zh: 以六人輔吾子，足以經國。

translations.literal: With these six to assist my son, it is enough to govern the state.
translations.idiomatic: These six can govern the state for my son.

sentences.zh: 吾與汝曹遊行四境，伐叛柔服，可以得志於天下矣。

translations.literal: I with you shall roam the four borders, chastising rebels and soothing submission—we may fulfill our will under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I with you will roam the four borders, crushing rebels and soothing the submitted—we may fulfill our will under heaven.

sentences.zh: 」群臣時奏事所疑。

translations.literal: " The ministers at the time presented doubtful matters for decision.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers then brought doubtful matters for their decision.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此非我所知，當決之于汝曹國主也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is not for me to know; it should be decided by you, the lords of the state."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is not for me to decide—it belongs to you, the lords of the realm."

sentences.zh: 會聞宋武帝殂，帝欲取洛陽、武牢、滑台。

translations.literal: It happened that word came that Emperor Wu of Song had died; the emperor wished to take Luoyang, Wulao, and Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: When news arrived that Emperor Wu of Song had died, the emperor wanted to seize Luoyang, Wulao, and Huatai.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「陛下不以劉裕欻起，納其使貢，裕亦敬事陛下。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Your Majesty, though Liu Yu rose suddenly, received his envoys and tribute, and Yu also honored Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Your Majesty accepted Liu Yu when he rose abruptly, received his tribute, and Liu Yu in turn honored the throne."

sentences.zh: 不幸今死，乘喪伐之，雖得之，不令。

translations.literal: Now that he has unfortunately died, to attack while they mourn, though you might gain territory, would not be proper.
translations.idiomatic: "Now that he is dead, to invade in their hour of mourning might win ground but would not be honorable."

sentences.zh: 《春秋》晉士丐侵齊，聞齊侯卒，乃還。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, Jin's Shi Gai invaded Qi; hearing the Marquis of Qi had died, he turned back.
translations.idiomatic: "The Spring and Autumn Annals records how Shi Gai of Jin invaded Qi but turned back on hearing the marquis had died."
