sentences.zh: 君子大其不伐喪，以為恩足以感孝子，義足以動諸侯。

translations.literal: The noble man praised his not attacking during mourning, holding that such grace could move filial sons and such righteousness could stir the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: "The noble man praised refusing to strike a house in mourning—grace enough to touch filial sons, righteousness enough to move the feudal lords."

sentences.zh: 今國家未能一舉而定江南，宜遣人弔祭，恤其凶災，布義風於天下，令德之事也。

translations.literal: Now the state cannot settle the south in one stroke; you should send men to mourn and offer relief for their calamity, spreading righteous renown through the realm—a deed of commanding virtue.
translations.idiomatic: "The realm cannot conquer the south in a single campaign. Send envoys to mourn, succor their disaster, and spread righteous fame under heaven—that is the deed of a ruler of commanding virtue."

sentences.zh: 且裕新死，黨與未離，不如緩之，待其惡稔。

translations.literal: Moreover, with Yu newly dead, his faction has not yet dispersed; better to wait until their evil ripens.
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, Liu Yu is newly dead and his faction not yet split apart. Better to wait until their wickedness ripens."

sentences.zh: 如其強臣爭權，變難必起，然後命將揚威，可不勞士卒而收淮北之地。

translations.literal: If powerful ministers contend for power, trouble will surely arise; then you may command generals to display might and take the lands north of the Huai without tiring the troops.
translations.idiomatic: "If powerful ministers fight for power, crisis will follow. Then send generals to show force and take the Huai north without exhausting the army."

sentences.zh: 」帝銳意南伐，語浩曰：「劉裕因姚興死而滅其國。

translations.literal: " The emperor was keen on a southern campaign and said to Hao: "Liu Yu destroyed Yao Xing's state because Yao Xing died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was set on war in the south and told Hao, "Liu Yu destroyed Yao Xing's state when Yao Xing died."

sentences.zh: 裕死，我伐之，何為不可！

translations.literal: Yu is dead—why may I not attack!"
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Yu is dead—why should I not attack?"

sentences.zh: 」浩固執曰：「興死，二子交爭，裕乃伐之。

translations.literal: Hao stubbornly said: "When Xing died, his two sons fought each other—only then did Yu attack."
translations.idiomatic: Hao held firm: "Yao Xing died and his two sons fought each other—only then did Liu Yu attack."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，不從。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 遂遣奚斤等南伐，議于監國之前曰：「先攻城，先略地？

translations.literal: He then sent Xi Jin and others south, and before the heir apparent's court they debated: "Attack cities first, or seize territory first?"
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xi Jin and others south. Before the heir apparent's court they debated whether to take cities first or overrun territory first.

sentences.zh: 」斤請先攻城。

translations.literal: Jin asked to attack cities first.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin asked to attack the cities first.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「南人長於固守，苻氏攻襄陽，經年不拔。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Southerners excel at stubborn defense; Fu Jian's attack on Xiangyang took more than a year without success.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Southerners excel at stubborn defense. Fu Jian's siege of Xiangyang dragged on more than a year without success."

sentences.zh: 今以大國之力，攻其小城，若不時克，挫損軍勢，危道也。

translations.literal: Now with the great state's strength to attack their small cities, if you do not take them quickly, you will blunt the army's momentum—a perilous course.
translations.idiomatic: "With the full strength of the empire against their small towns, failure to take them quickly will blunt the army's momentum—a dangerous course."

sentences.zh: 不如分軍略地，至淮為限，列置守宰，收斂租穀。

translations.literal: Better to divide the army to overrun territory, taking the Huai as the limit, setting governors and magistrates to gather rent and grain.
translations.idiomatic: "Better to divide the army and overrun territory up to the Huai, posting governors and magistrates to collect rent and grain."

sentences.zh: 滑台、武牢反在軍北，絕望南救，必沿河東走。

translations.literal: Huatai and Wulao would lie north of the army; cut off from southern rescue, they would surely flee east along the river.
translations.idiomatic: "Huatai and Wulao would lie north of our forces, cut off from southern relief, and would surely flee east along the river."

sentences.zh: 若或不然，即是囿中之物。

translations.literal: If not, they would be game within an enclosure."
translations.idiomatic: "Otherwise they would be beasts inside a pen."

sentences.zh: 」公孫表請先圖其城。

translations.literal: Gongsun Biao asked to take their cities first.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Biao urged attacking the cities first.

sentences.zh: 斤等濟河，先攻滑台，經時不拔，表請濟師。

translations.literal: Jin and the others crossed the river and first attacked Huatai; after a long time without success, Biao asked for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin crossed the river and attacked Huatai first. After a long stalemate, Gongsun Biao asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，乃親南巡，拜浩為相州刺史，隨軍謀主。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and personally toured south, appointing Hao Governor of Xiangzhou and chief strategist with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, enraged, marched south in person, made Hao governor of Xiangzhou, and kept him as chief strategist with the army.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還，浩從幸西河、太原，下臨河流，傍覽川城，慨然有感。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Hao accompanied him to Xihe and Taiyuan, descended to view the river, and gazed at the towns along the banks, moved to deep feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial train returned, Hao accompanied the tour to Xihe and Taiyuan, stood above the river, looked along the towns on its banks, and was stirred to deep reflection.

sentences.zh: 遂與同寮論五等郡縣之是非，考秦皇、漢武之違失。

translations.literal: He then debated with colleagues the rights and wrongs of the five ranks and commanderies and counties, examining the errors of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He then debated with colleagues the merits of restoring the five ranks of nobility versus the commandery-county system, weighing the failures of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han.

sentences.zh: 時伏其言。

translations.literal: At the time all respected his words.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all were impressed by his argument.

sentences.zh: 天師寇謙之每與浩言，聞其論古興亡之跡，常自夜達旦，竦意斂容，深美之，曰：「斯人言也惠，皆可底行，亦當今之皋陶也。

translations.literal: The Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi often spoke with Hao; hearing his discourse on the rise and fall of antiquity, he would stay from night till dawn, straightening his manner and composing his face, deeply admiring him, and say: "This man's words are beneficent and all can be carried out; he is a Gao Yao for our age.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi often talked with Hao. Hearing him trace the rise and fall of past ages, Kou would sit from night till dawn, rapt and composed, and say in deep admiration, "This man's words are beneficent and can all be put into practice. He is a Gao Yao for our age."

sentences.zh: 但人貴遠賤近，不能深察之耳。

translations.literal: Only men prize what is distant and slight what is near, and cannot examine him deeply."
translations.idiomatic: "Only men prize what is far away and slight what is close at hand, and fail to study him deeply."

sentences.zh: 」因謂浩曰：「吾當兼攸儒教，輔助太平真君，而學不稽古。

translations.literal: He then said to Hao: "I shall embrace both Ru and teaching, assist the Perfect Lord of Great Peace, yet my learning does not examine antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He then told Hao, "I mean to embrace both Confucian teaching and the Way, to assist the Perfect Lord of Great Peace, yet my learning does not reach back to antiquity."

sentences.zh: 為吾撰列王者政典，並論其大要。

translations.literal: Compose for me the political canons of successive kings and discuss their main points."
translations.idiomatic: "Compose for me the political canons of successive kings and set out their main themes."

sentences.zh: 」浩乃著書二十餘篇，上推太初，下盡秦、漢變弊之跡，大旨先以復五等為本。

translations.literal: Hao then wrote more than twenty chapters, reaching back to the Grand Beginning and down through the traces of Qin and Han change and decay, the great theme first taking restoration of the five ranks as its root.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wrote more than twenty chapters, reaching from the Grand Beginning down through the rise and fall of Qin and Han, with restoration of the five ranks as the central theme.

sentences.zh: 太武，左右忌浩正直，共排毀之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu's attendants, resenting Hao's uprightness, jointly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Those about Emperor Taiwu, resenting Hao's uprightness, joined in slandering him.

sentences.zh: 帝雖知其能，不免群議，故浩以公歸第。

translations.literal: Though the emperor knew his ability, he could not escape the clamor of the multitude; therefore Hao was sent home on his noble title.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor knew his talent, he could not defy the crowd's clamor, and Hao was sent home while retaining his noble title.

sentences.zh: 及有疑議，召問焉。

translations.literal: When doubts arose, he was summoned to be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever doubts arose, he was summoned for counsel.

sentences.zh: 浩纖妍白皙如美婦人。

translations.literal: Hao was slender, fair, and white as a beautiful woman.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was slight, fair-skinned, and delicate as a beautiful woman.

sentences.zh: 性敏達，長於謀計，自比張良，謂己稽古過之。

translations.literal: By nature quick and penetrating, skilled in stratagem, he compared himself to Zhang Liang and said his mastery of antiquity surpassed Zhang's.
translations.idiomatic: Quick and penetrating by nature, skilled in stratagem, he likened himself to Zhang Liang and claimed his command of antiquity surpassed Zhang's.

sentences.zh: 既歸第，因欲修服食養性術，而寇謙之有《神中錄圖新經》，浩因師事之。

translations.literal: After returning home, he wished to practice ingestion and nourishing life; Kou Qianzhi had the Scripture of the Divine Central Record and New Classic, and Hao therefore took him as master.
translations.idiomatic: Back at home he wished to practice dietetics and longevity arts. Kou Qianzhi possessed the Scripture of the Divine Central Record and New Classic, and Hao became his disciple.

sentences.zh: 始光中，進爵東郡公，拜太常卿。

translations.literal: In the Shiguang era he was advanced to Duke of Dongjun and appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shiguang era he was raised to Duke of Dongjun and made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時議伐赫連昌，群臣皆以為難，唯浩曰：「往年以來，熒惑再守羽林，越鉤陳，其占秦亡。

translations.literal: At the time they debated attacking Helian Chang; the ministers all thought it difficult, but only Hao said: "In years past Mars twice held the Feathered Forest and crossed the Hooked Array—its omen is the fall of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated attacking Helian Chang, every minister called it hard—only Hao said, "For years Mars twice held the Feathered Forest and crossed the Hooked Array—an omen of Qin's fall."

sentences.zh: 又今年五星並出東方，利以西伐。

translations.literal: Moreover this year the five planets all appear in the east, favorable to a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: "This year the five planets all stand in the east, favoring a western campaign."

sentences.zh: 天應人和，時會並集，不可不進。

translations.literal: Heaven answers man and the seasons converge—one must advance."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven answers man, the seasons converge—you must advance."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃使奚斤等擊蒲阪，而親率輕騎掠其都城，大獲而還。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Xi Jin and others to strike Puban while he personally led light cavalry to raid their capital, returning with great booty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xi Jin and others against Puban while he personally led light cavalry to raid their capital and returned with great booty.

sentences.zh: 後復討昌，次其城下，收眾偽退。

translations.literal: Later he campaigned against Chang again, halting below his walls and gathering troops in a feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attacked Chang again, halted below his walls, and feigned a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 昌鼓噪而前，舒陣為兩翼。

translations.literal: Chang advanced with drums and shouts, spreading his array in two wings.
translations.idiomatic: Chang advanced with drums and shouts and spread his line into two wings.

sentences.zh: 會有風雨從東南來，揚沙昏冥，宦者趙倪進曰：「今風雨從賊後來，我向彼背，天不助人。

translations.literal: Wind and rain came from the southeast, raising sand and darkening the sky; the eunuch Zhao Ni stepped forward and said: "Now wind and rain come from behind the enemy; we face their backs—Heaven does not help us.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and rain came from the southeast, whipping sand until the sky went dark. The eunuch Zhao Ni stepped forward and said, "The storm comes from behind the enemy while we face their backs—Heaven is not with us."

sentences.zh: 又將士饑渴，願陛下攝騎避之，更待後日。

translations.literal: Moreover the officers and men are hungry and thirsty; I beg Your Majesty to gather the cavalry and withdraw, and wait for another day."
translations.idiomatic: "The troops are hungry and thirsty. I beg Your Majesty to gather the cavalry and withdraw until another day."

sentences.zh: 」浩叱之曰：「是何言歟！

translations.literal: Hao shouted at him: "What words are these!"
translations.idiomatic: Hao shouted him down: "What talk is this!"

sentences.zh: 千里制勝，一日之中，豈得變易？

translations.literal: To win a thousand li away, within a single day—how can you change plans?
translations.idiomatic: "Victory a thousand li away cannot be thrown away in a single day—how can plans be changed?"

sentences.zh: 賊前行不止，後已離絕，宜分軍隱山，掩擊不意。

translations.literal: The enemy advances without stopping and their rear is already cut off; you should divide the army to hide in the hills and strike them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: "The enemy presses on without pause and their rear is already cut off. Divide the army, hide in the hills, and strike them unawares."

sentences.zh: 風道在人，豈有常也？

translations.literal: The way of wind lies with men—how could it be constant?"
translations.idiomatic: "Wind serves those who use it—how could it be constant?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 」分騎奮擊，昌軍大潰。

translations.literal: Dividing the cavalry they struck fiercely and Chang's army collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: They split the cavalry, struck hard, and Chang's army collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 神抅二年，議擊蠕蠕，朝臣內外盡不欲行，保太后亦固止帝，帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenjue they debated striking the Rouran; courtiers within and without all wished not to go, and Empress Dowager Bao also firmly stopped the emperor, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenjue the court debated attacking the Rouran. Ministers inside and out opposed the campaign, and Empress Dowager Bao also firmly dissuaded the emperor, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 唯浩贊成之。

translations.literal: Only Hao approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hao supported it.

sentences.zh: 尚書令劉潔、左僕射安原等乃使黃門侍郎仇齊推赫連昌太史張深、徐辯說帝曰：「今年己巳，三陰之歲，歲星襲月，太白在西方，不可舉兵。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing An Yuan, and others had Yellow Gate Attendant Qiu Qi recommend Helian Chang's grand astrologer Zhang Shen and Xu Bian to tell the emperor: "This year is jisi, a year of triple yin; the Year Star assaults the moon and the White Star is in the west—arms must not be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Director Liu Jie, Left Vice Director An Yuan, and others had Yellow Gate Attendant Qiu Qi bring forward Helian Chang's grand astrologer Zhang Shen and Xu Bian to tell the emperor, "This year is jisi, a year of triple yin. The Year Star assaults the moon and the White Star stands in the west—arms must not be raised."

sentences.zh: 北伐必敗，雖克不利於上。

translations.literal: A northern campaign will surely fail; even if you conquer, it will not benefit the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: "A northern campaign will fail; even victory will not benefit the throne."

sentences.zh: 」又群臣共贊深等云：「深少時常諫苻堅不可南征，堅不從而敗。

translations.literal: Moreover the ministers together praised Shen and the rest, saying: "In his youth Shen often admonished Fu Jian not to campaign south; Jian would not listen and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers together praised Shen and the others, saying, "In youth Shen often warned Fu Jian against a southern campaign. Jian would not listen and was defeated."

sentences.zh: 今天時人事都不和協，如何舉動？

translations.literal: Now the seasons, heaven, and human affairs are all out of harmony—how can you act?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now heaven, the seasons, and human affairs are all out of harmony—how can we move?"

sentences.zh: 」帝意不快，乃召浩與深等辯之。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and summoned Hao to debate with Shen and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and summoned Hao to debate Shen and the others.

sentences.zh: 浩難深曰：「陽者德也，陰者刑也，故月蝕修刑。

translations.literal: Hao refuted Shen, saying: "Yang is virtue and yin is punishment; therefore an eclipse of the moon means repairing punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hao refuted Shen: "Yang is virtue and yin is punishment, so a lunar eclipse means repairing punishment."

sentences.zh: 夫王者之用刑，大則陳之原野，小則肆之市朝。

translations.literal: When a king uses punishment, on a large scale he displays it in the wilds, on a small scale he exposes it in market and court.
translations.idiomatic: "When a king uses punishment, on a grand scale he displays it in the wilds; on a small scale he exposes it in market and court."

sentences.zh: 戰伐者，用刑之大者也。

translations.literal: War is the greatest use of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: "War is the greatest use of punishment."

sentences.zh: 以此言之，三陰用兵，蓋得其類，修刑之義也。

translations.literal: From this view, to use arms in a triple-yin year fits the category and the meaning of repairing punishment.
translations.idiomatic: "From this view, using arms in a triple-yin year fits the category—it is the meaning of repairing punishment."

sentences.zh: 歲星襲月，年饑人流，應在他國，遠期十二年。

translations.literal: The Year Star assaulting the moon means famine and people wandering—it applies to another state, twelve years distant.
translations.idiomatic: "The Year Star assaulting the moon means famine and exodus—it applies to another state, twelve years hence."

sentences.zh: 太白行蒼龍宿，于天文為東，不妨北伐。

translations.literal: The White Star moving through the Azure Dragon lodges—in astronomy that is the east; it does not hinder a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: "The White Star moving through the Azure Dragon lodges—in astronomy that is the east. It does not hinder a northern campaign."

sentences.zh: 深等俗生，志意淺近，牽於術數，不達大體，難與遠圖。

translations.literal: Shen and the rest are vulgar scholars, shallow in purpose and near in vision, dragged by numerology, not reaching the great body—hard to plan far with them.
translations.idiomatic: "Shen and the rest are vulgar scholars, shallow in purpose and near in vision, dragged by numerology and unable to grasp the larger design—hard to plan far with them."

sentences.zh: 臣觀天文，比年以來，月行掩昴，至今猶然。

translations.literal: Your servant observes the heavens: in recent years the moon's course has covered the Pleiades, and it is still so.
translations.idiomatic: "I observe the heavens: in recent years the moon's course has covered the Pleiades, and it still does."

sentences.zh: 其占，三年天子大破旄頭之國。

translations.literal: Its omen: in three years the Son of Heaven will greatly break the Mao-tou country.
translations.idiomatic: "Its omen: within three years the Son of Heaven will shatter the Mao-tou peoples."

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕、高車，旄頭之眾也。

translations.literal: The Rouran and Gaoche are Mao-tou multitudes.
translations.idiomatic: "The Rouran and Gaoche are Mao-tou peoples."

sentences.zh: 夫聖明禦時，能行非常之事。

translations.literal: When a sage illumines the age, he can perform extraordinary deeds.
translations.idiomatic: "When a sage illumines the age, he can perform extraordinary deeds."

sentences.zh: 古人語曰：'非常之原，黎人懼焉；

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'At the source of the extraordinary, the people fear;
translations.idiomatic: "The ancients said, 'At the source of the extraordinary the people fear;

sentences.zh: 及其成功，天下晏然。

translations.literal: when it succeeds, all under heaven is tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: 'when it succeeds, all under heaven is tranquil.'

sentences.zh: '願陛下勿疑。

translations.literal: ' I beg Your Majesty not to doubt."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty not to doubt."

sentences.zh: 」深等慚曰：「蠕蠕荒外無用之物，得其地不可耕而食，得其人不可臣而使。

translations.literal: Shen and the rest said in shame: "The Rouran are useless things beyond the wilds; gain their land and you cannot farm and eat, gain their people and you cannot make them subjects and use them.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and the rest said shamefacedly, "The Rouran are useless folk beyond the wilds. Take their land and you cannot farm it; take their people and you cannot make them serve."

sentences.zh: 輕疾無常，難得而制，有何汲汲而勞苦士馬。」

translations.literal: Light and swift without constancy, hard to seize and control—why be so eager and weary horses and men?"
translations.idiomatic: "They are light, swift, and unsteady—hard to seize and control. Why be so eager and weary horses and men?"

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「深言天時，是其所職；

translations.literal: Hao said: "Shen speaks of heaven's seasons—that is his office;
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Shen speaks of heaven's seasons—that is his office."

sentences.zh: 若論形勢，非彼所知。

translations.literal: if one discusses situation and form, that is not what they know.
translations.idiomatic: "If one discusses situation and form, that is not what they know."

sentences.zh: 斯乃漢世舊說常談，施之於今，不合事宜。

translations.literal: That is Han-era old talk and common saying; applied to today it does not fit the affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: "That is Han-era platitude applied to today—it does not fit the affairs of the time."

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: "How so?"

sentences.zh: 夫蠕蠕者，舊是國家北邊叛隸，今誅其元惡，收其善人，令復舊位，非無用也。

translations.literal: The Rouran were formerly the state's northern border rebels and slaves; now execute their chief villains, gather their good men, and restore them to their old posts—not without use.
translations.idiomatic: "The Rouran were once our northern border rebels and thralls. Execute their chief villains, gather their good men, restore them to their old posts—they are not useless."

sentences.zh: 漠北高涼，不生蚊蚋，水草美善，夏則北遷，田牧其地，非不可耕而食也。

translations.literal: North of the desert it is high and cool, without gnats and mosquitoes; grass and water are fine; in summer they migrate north and pasture and farm the land—not impossible to farm and eat.
translations.idiomatic: "North of the desert it is high and cool, free of gnats and mosquitoes, with fine grass and water. In summer they migrate north to pasture and farm—not land that cannot feed you."

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕子弟來降，貴者尚公主，賤者將軍、大夫，居列滿朝。

translations.literal: Rouran youths who come over are married to princesses if noble, made generals and grandees if humble, filling the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: "Rouran youths who surrender marry princesses if noble or become generals and grandees if humble—they fill the court ranks."

sentences.zh: 又高車號為名騎，非不可臣而畜也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Gaoche are famed as named horsemen—not impossible to make subjects and keep.
translations.idiomatic: "The Gaoche are famed horsemen—not impossible to make subjects and keep."

sentences.zh: 夫以南人追之，則患其輕疾；

translations.literal: If southerners pursue them, they fear their lightness and speed;
translations.idiomatic: "If southerners pursue them, they fear their lightness and speed."

sentences.zh: 于國兵則不然。

translations.literal: with the state's troops it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: "With the state's troops it is not so."

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: "How so?"

sentences.zh: 彼能遠走，我亦能遠逐，非難制也。

translations.literal: They can flee far; we can pursue far—not hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: "They can flee far; we can pursue far—not hard to control."

sentences.zh: 往數入塞，國人震驚。

translations.literal: In past years they entered the passes many times and the people were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: "In past years they raided the passes again and again and the people were shaken."

sentences.zh: 今夏不乘虛掩進，破滅其國，至秋復來，不得安臥。

translations.literal: If this summer you do not strike while they are open and advance to break and destroy their state, when autumn comes they will return and you cannot rest in peace.
translations.idiomatic: "If this summer you do not strike while they are exposed and destroy their state, they will return in autumn and you cannot rest in peace."

sentences.zh: 自太宗之世，迄於今日，無歲不警，豈不汲汲乎哉？

translations.literal: From the era of Emperor Taizong down to today there has been no year without alarm—is that not eager?
translations.idiomatic: "From Emperor Taizong's day to now there has been no year without alarm—is that not urgent?"

sentences.zh: 世人皆謂深、辯通解數術，明決成敗，臣請試之。

translations.literal: The world all says Shen and Bian understand numerology and clearly decide success and failure; your servant asks to test them.
translations.idiomatic: "The world says Shen and Bian master numerology and judge success and failure. I ask to test them."

sentences.zh: 問其西國未滅之前，有何亡征？

translations.literal: Ask what signs of ruin their western state had before it was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: "Ask what signs of ruin their western state showed before it fell."

sentences.zh: 知而不言，是其不忠；

translations.literal: If they knew and did not speak, that is disloyalty;
translations.idiomatic: "If they knew and did not speak, that is disloyalty."

sentences.zh: 若實不知，是其無術。」

translations.literal: if they truly did not know, that is lack of skill."
translations.idiomatic: "If they truly did not know, that is lack of skill."

sentences.zh: 時赫連昌在坐，深等自以無先言，慚不能對。

translations.literal: Helian Chang was present; Shen and the rest, knowing they had no prior warning, were ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Chang was present. Shen and the rest, knowing they had given no prior warning, were ashamed and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，謂公卿曰：「吾意決矣。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said to the ministers: "My mind is decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and told the ministers, "My mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 亡國之臣不可與謀，信哉！

translations.literal: One cannot plot with ministers of a destroyed state—how true!"
translations.idiomatic: "One cannot plot with ministers of a destroyed state—how true!"

sentences.zh: 」而保太后猶疑之。

translations.literal: Yet Empress Dowager Bao still doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Empress Dowager Bao still doubted.

sentences.zh: 復令群臣至保太后前評議，帝命浩善曉之令寤。

translations.literal: She again had the ministers debate before the empress dowager; the emperor ordered Hao to explain well and awaken her.
translations.idiomatic: She had the ministers debate again before the empress dowager, and the emperor ordered Hao to explain matters clearly and win her over.

sentences.zh: 既罷朝，或有尤浩曰：「吳賊侵南，舍之北伐，師行千里，其誰不知？

translations.literal: When court ended, some blamed Hao, saying: "Wu bandits invade the south yet you leave that and campaign north—a host marching a thousand li, who does not know?"
translations.idiomatic: When court ended, some blamed Hao: "Wu bandits invade the south, yet you leave that and march north—a host a thousand li on the road, who does not know it?"

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕遠遁，前無所獲，後有南侵之患，此危道也。

translations.literal: The Rouran flee far; before you gain nothing, behind you the trouble of southern invasion—this is a perilous course."
translations.idiomatic: "The Rouran flee far—you gain nothing ahead while southern invasion threatens behind. That is a perilous course."

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「今年不摧蠕蠕，則無以禦南賊。

translations.literal: Hao said: "If this year you do not crush the Rouran, you cannot defend against the southern bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "If we do not crush the Rouran this year, we cannot defend against the southern enemy."

sentences.zh: 自國家並西國以來，南人恐懼，揚聲動眾，以衛淮北。

translations.literal: Since the state annexed the western kingdom, southerners have feared and raised voices and moved hosts to guard the Huai north.
translations.idiomatic: "Since the state annexed the western kingdom, the south has lived in fear, raising alarms and moving armies to guard the Huai north."

sentences.zh: 彼北我南，彼征我息，其勢然矣。

translations.literal: They north, we south; they campaign, we rest—the situation is so.
translations.idiomatic: "They are north, we south; they campaign, we rest—that is the pattern."

sentences.zh: 北破蠕蠕，往還之間，故不見其至也。

translations.literal: Break the Rouran in the north and in the going and returning you therefore do not see them arrive.
translations.idiomatic: "Break the Rouran in the north and, in the going and returning, you will not see them arrive."

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: "How so?"

sentences.zh: 劉裕得關中，留其愛子，精兵數萬，良將勁卒，猶不能固守，舉軍盡沒，號哭之聲至今未已。

translations.literal: Liu Yu took Guanzhong, left his beloved son, several tens of thousands of elite troops and fierce generals and strong soldiers—yet could not hold firm; the whole army perished and the sound of wailing has not ceased to this day.
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Yu took Guanzhong, left his beloved son, tens of thousands of elite troops and fierce commanders—yet could not hold it. The whole army was lost and the sound of wailing has not ceased to this day."

sentences.zh: 如何正當國家休明之世，士馬強盛之時，而欲以駒犢齒虎口也？

translations.literal: How, just when the state is in its brilliant age and horses and men are strong, can you set a foal's teeth against a tiger's maw?
translations.idiomatic: "How, in the state's brilliant age with strong horses and men, can you set a foal's teeth against a tiger's maw?"

sentences.zh: 設國家與之河南，彼必不能守之。

translations.literal: Suppose the state gave them the lands south of the Yellow River—they could certainly not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: "Suppose we gave them the lands south of the Yellow River—they could not hold them."

sentences.zh: 自量不能守，是以必不來。

translations.literal: Measuring that they cannot hold, they therefore will certainly not come.
translations.idiomatic: "Knowing they cannot hold them, they will certainly not come."

sentences.zh: 若或有眾，備邊之軍耳。

translations.literal: If they have a host, it is only border-guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: "If they field troops at all, it will be only border guards."

sentences.zh: 夫見瓶水凍，知天下之寒；

translations.literal: See water in a bottle freeze and know the cold of all under heaven;
translations.idiomatic: "See water freeze in a bottle and know the cold of all under heaven."

sentences.zh: 嘗肉一臠，識鑊中之昧。

translations.literal: taste one slice of meat and know the flavor in the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: "Taste one slice of meat and know the flavor in the cauldron."

sentences.zh: 物有其類，可推而得。

translations.literal: Things have their kind; one can infer and obtain.
translations.idiomatic: "Things have their kind—you can infer from one to all."

sentences.zh: 且蠕蠕恃遠，謂國家力不能至，自寬來久。

translations.literal: Moreover the Rouran rely on distance and think the state's strength cannot reach them; they have relaxed themselves a long time.
translations.idiomatic: "The Rouran rely on distance and think the empire cannot reach them—they have grown complacent a long while."

sentences.zh: 故夏則散眾放畜，秋肥乃聚，背寒向溫，南來寇抄。

translations.literal: Therefore in summer they scatter the host and release herds; when autumn fat comes they gather, turning their backs to cold and faces to warmth, coming south to raid.
translations.idiomatic: "In summer they scatter herds; when autumn fat comes they gather, turning from cold toward warmth and raiding south."

sentences.zh: 今掩其不備，大軍卒至，必驚駭，望塵奔走。

translations.literal: Now strike them unprepared; the great army arrives suddenly—they will surely be terrified and flee at the sight of dust.
translations.idiomatic: "Strike them unprepared now. The great army arrives suddenly—they will flee in terror at the sight of dust."

sentences.zh: 牡馬護牧，牝馬戀駒；

translations.literal: Stallions guard the herds, mares cling to foals;
translations.idiomatic: "Stallions guard the herds, mares cling to foals."

sentences.zh: 驅馳難制，不得水草；

translations.literal: driven in flight they are hard to control, cannot obtain grass and water;
translations.idiomatic: "Driven in flight they are hard to control and cannot find grass and water."

sentences.zh: 未過數日，朋聚而困弊，可一舉而滅。

translations.literal: within a few days they cluster in exhaustion and weakness and can be destroyed in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: "Within days they cluster, exhausted and weak, and can be destroyed in one stroke."

sentences.zh: 暫勞永逸，時不可失也。

translations.literal: Brief toil for lasting ease—the time cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: "Brief toil for lasting ease—the moment cannot be lost."

sentences.zh: 唯患上無此意。

translations.literal: Only I fear the ruler above lacks this intent.
translations.idiomatic: "Only I fear the throne lacks this intent."

sentences.zh: 今聖慮已決，如何止之？

translations.literal: Now the sage mind is decided—how can it be stopped?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now the sage mind is decided—how can it be stopped?"

sentences.zh: 」遂行。

translations.literal: They then set out.
translations.idiomatic: They then marched.

sentences.zh: 天師謂浩曰：「是行可果乎？

translations.literal: The Celestial Master said to Hao: "Can this campaign succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Master asked Hao, "Will this campaign succeed?"

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「必克。

translations.literal: Hao said: "It will surely conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "It will surely conquer."

sentences.zh: 但恐諸將瑣瑣，前後顧慮，不能乘勝深入，使不全舉耳。」

translations.literal: Only I fear the generals will be petty, looking before and behind, unable to press the victory deep, so that the whole cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: "Only I fear the generals will be petty, looking before and behind, unable to press the victory deep, so the whole prize cannot be taken."

sentences.zh: 及軍到，入其境，蠕蠕先不設備。

translations.literal: When the army arrived and entered their territory, the Rouran at first made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: When the army entered their territory, the Rouran at first made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 於是分軍搜討，東西五千里，南北三千里，所虜及獲畜產車廬數百萬。

translations.literal: They then divided the army to search: five thousand li east and west, three thousand li north and south; captives and livestock, carts and tents gained numbered in the millions.
translations.idiomatic: They divided the army to search five thousand li east and west and three thousand li north and south. Captives and livestock, carts and tents taken numbered in the millions.

sentences.zh: 高車殺蠕蠕種類歸降者三十餘萬落。

translations.literal: Gaoche who killed Rouran kin and came over numbered more than three hundred thousand clans.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoche who killed Rouran kin and surrendered numbered more than three hundred thousand clans.

sentences.zh: 虜遂散亂。

translations.literal: The barbarians then scattered in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran then scattered in disorder.

sentences.zh: 帝沿弱水，西至涿邪山，諸大將果慮深入有伏兵，勸帝止。

translations.literal: The emperor followed the Ruoshui west to Zhuoye Mountain; the great generals indeed feared deep advance and ambush and urged the emperor to stop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed the Ruoshui west to Zhuoye Mountain. The great generals feared ambush in a deep advance and urged him to stop.

sentences.zh: 天師以浩曩日言，固勸帝窮討，帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Celestial Master, because of Hao's words of other days, firmly urged the emperor to pursue to the end; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Master, citing Hao's earlier counsel, firmly urged pursuit to the end; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 後有降人言：「蠕蠕大檀先被疾，不知所為，乃焚穹廬，科車自載，將百人入山南走。

translations.literal: Later a surrendered man said: "The Rouran khan Datan had first fallen ill, not knowing what to do; he burned his tents, loaded carts himself, and with a hundred men entered the mountains and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Later a surrendered man said, "Khan Datan had fallen ill, not knowing what to do. He burned his tents, loaded carts, and with a hundred men fled south into the mountains."

sentences.zh: 人畜窘聚，方六十里，無人領統。

translations.literal: Men and livestock crowded together in an area sixty li square with no one to command them.
translations.idiomatic: "Men and livestock crowded together in an area sixty li square with no one to command them."

sentences.zh: 相去百八十里，追軍不至，乃徐西遁，唯此得免。

translations.literal: A hundred and eighty li apart, the pursuing army did not arrive; they then slowly fled west and only thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: "A hundred and eighty li away, the pursuing army did not arrive. They then fled west at leisure and only thus escaped."

sentences.zh: 」聞涼州賈胡言：「若復前行二日，則盡滅之矣。

translations.literal: " Hearing a Liangzhou merchant Hu say: "If you had advanced two more days, you would have destroyed them utterly."
translations.idiomatic: A Liangzhou merchant was heard to say, "Had you advanced two more days, you would have destroyed them utterly."

sentences.zh: 」帝深恨之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply regretted it.

sentences.zh: 大軍既還，南軍竟不能動，如浩所料。

translations.literal: When the great army had returned, the southern army indeed could not move, as Hao had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army returned, the southern army indeed could not move—as Hao had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 浩明識天文，好觀星變。

translations.literal: Hao clearly understood astronomy and loved to observe stellar changes.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had a clear grasp of astronomy and loved to watch the stars.

sentences.zh: 常置金銀銅鋌於酢器中，令青，夜有所見，即以鋌畫紙作字，以記其異。

translations.literal: He often placed gold, silver, and copper awls in vinegar to turn them green; when he saw something at night he would use the awl to draw characters on paper and record the anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: He often placed gold, silver, and copper styli in vinegar to turn them green; when he saw something at night he scratched characters on paper with a stylus to record the anomaly.

sentences.zh: 太武每幸浩第，多問以異事。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu whenever he visited Hao's residence asked much about strange matters.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Taiwu visited Hao's house he asked much about strange matters.

sentences.zh: 或倉卒不及束帶，奉進蔬食，不暇精美，帝為舉匕箸，或立嘗而還。

translations.literal: Sometimes in haste he could not gird his belt; Hao would present plain vegetable food, without time for refinement, and the emperor would lift spoon and chopsticks for him, or stand and taste and return.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes, in haste, Hao could not gird his belt and would offer plain vegetables without time to refine them; the emperor would lift spoon and chopsticks for him, or stand, taste, and leave.

sentences.zh: 其見寵愛如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor he enjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 於是引浩出入臥內。

translations.literal: He was then brought in and out of the sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was then admitted in and out of the imperial sleeping quarters.

sentences.zh: 加侍中、特進、撫軍大將軍、左光祿大夫，以賞謀謨之功。

translations.literal: He was further made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Special Advance, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Left Grand Master of the Palace, to reward his stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Special Advance, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Left Grand Master of the Palace to reward his stratagems.

sentences.zh: 帝從容謂浩曰：「卿才智深博，事朕祖考，忠著三世，朕故延卿自近。

translations.literal: The emperor said at ease to Hao: "Your talent and wisdom are deep and broad; you served my grandfather and father, loyal through three generations—I therefore keep you near.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said gently to Hao, "Your talent and wisdom run deep. You served my grandfather and father with loyalty through three reigns, and I therefore keep you near."

sentences.zh: 其思盡規諫，勿有隱懷。

translations.literal: Think to exhaust remonstrance and counsel; do not harbor hidden thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: "Give me your fullest remonstrance and counsel; hide nothing in your heart."

sentences.zh: 朕雖當時遷怒，若或不用，久可不深思卿言也？

translations.literal: Though I may at the time shift anger, if I do not use your words, in time could I not deeply consider what you say?"
translations.idiomatic: "Though I may flare in anger and not heed you at once, in time might I not deeply weigh your words?"

sentences.zh: 」因令歌工曆頌群臣，事在《長孫道生傳》。

translations.literal: He then had singing craftsmen go through and praise the ministers—the matter is in the Biography of Changsun Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then had court musicians sing through praises of the ministers—the matter is recorded in the Biography of Changsun Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 又召新降高車渠帥數百人，賜酒食於前。

translations.literal: He also summoned several hundred newly surrendered Gaoche chieftains and bestowed food and drink before them.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned several hundred newly surrendered Gaoche chieftains and feasted them.

sentences.zh: 指浩以示之曰：「汝曹視此人纖尪懦弱，手不能彎弓持矛，其胸中所懷，乃逾於兵甲。

translations.literal: Pointing to Hao to show them he said: "You all see this man—slender, frail, and weak, his hands unable to bend a bow or hold a spear—yet what he harbors in his breast surpasses armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Pointing at Hao he told them, "You see this man—slight, frail, unable to bend a bow or hold a spear—yet what he carries in his breast surpasses armor and arms."

sentences.zh: 朕始時雖有征討之志，而慮不自決，前後克捷，皆此人導吾令到此矣。

translations.literal: At first I had the will to campaign, yet feared I could not decide myself; the victories before and after were all because this man guided me to reach this point."
translations.idiomatic: "At first I wished to campaign yet feared I could not decide alone. Every victory before and after came because this man guided me here."

sentences.zh: 」乃敕諸尚書曰：「凡軍國大計，卿等所不能決，皆先咨浩然後行。」

translations.literal: He then charged the Masters of Writing: "Whatever great plans of army and state you cannot decide, consult Hao first and then act."
translations.idiomatic: He then charged the Masters of Writing, "Whatever great plans of army and state you cannot decide, consult Hao first, then act."

sentences.zh: 俄而南籓諸將表宋師欲犯河南，請兵三萬，先其未發逆擊之。

translations.literal: Soon the southern frontier generals memorialized that Song troops wished to invade the lands south of the Yellow River and asked for thirty thousand men to strike them before they set out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the southern frontier generals reported that Song troops meant to invade the lands south of the Yellow River and asked for thirty thousand men to strike before they marched.

sentences.zh: 因誅河北流人在界上者，絕其鄉導，足以挫其銳氣，使不敢深入。

translations.literal: They would also execute northerners south of the Yellow River living on the border, cut off their guides, enough to blunt their edge and make them not dare advance deep.
translations.idiomatic: They would also execute northerners stranded on the border, cut off their guides, blunt the enemy's edge, and keep them from advancing deep.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿議之，咸言宜許。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to debate; all said it should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered debate among the ministers; all said it should be granted.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「此不可從也。

translations.literal: Hao said: "This cannot be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "This must not be followed."

sentences.zh: 往年國家大破蠕蠕，馬力有餘。

translations.literal: In years past the state greatly broke the Rouran and horses still had strength.
translations.idiomatic: "In years past the state shattered the Rouran and our horses still have strength."

sentences.zh: 南賊喪精，常恐輕兵奄至，故揚聲動眾，以備不虞，非敢先發。

translations.literal: The southern bandits have lost their elite and constantly fear light troops arriving suddenly; therefore they raise voices and move hosts to guard against the unexpected—they do not dare strike first.
translations.idiomatic: "The southern enemy has lost its elite and constantly fears sudden light attack. They raise alarms and move hosts to guard the unexpected—they do not dare strike first."

sentences.zh: 又南土下濕，夏月蒸暑，非行師之時。

translations.literal: Moreover the southern lands are low and wet; summer months are steaming hot—not the season for marching armies.
translations.idiomatic: "The south is low and wet; summer months steam—not the season for armies."

sentences.zh: 且彼先嚴有備，必堅城固守。

translations.literal: Moreover they have first made strict preparations and will surely hold the walls firm.
translations.idiomatic: "They have already made strict preparations and will hold their walls firm."

sentences.zh: 屯軍攻之，則糧食不給；

translations.literal: Station troops to attack and grain will not suffice;
translations.idiomatic: "Station troops to attack and grain will not suffice."

sentences.zh: 分兵肆討，則無以應敵。

translations.literal: divide troops to raid widely and there will be none to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: "Divide troops to raid widely and there will be none to meet the enemy."

sentences.zh: 未見其利。

translations.literal: I do not see the profit.
translations.idiomatic: "I see no profit in it."

sentences.zh: 就使能來，待其勞倦，秋涼馬肥，因敵取食，徐往擊之，萬全之計。

translations.literal: Even if they can come, wait until they are weary; when autumn is cool and horses are fat, take food from the enemy and strike them slowly—the plan of complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: "Even if they come, wait until they are weary. When autumn cools and horses grow fat, take food from the enemy and strike slowly—that is the plan of complete safety."

sentences.zh: 在朝群臣及西北守將，從陛下征討，西滅赫連，北破蠕蠕，多獲美女珍寶，馬畜成群；

translations.literal: The ministers at court and the northwestern frontier generals who followed Your Majesty in campaigns west destroyed Helian and north broke the Rouran, gaining many beautiful women and treasures, horses and herds in droves;
translations.idiomatic: "Ministers at court and northwestern frontier generals who followed Your Majesty west destroyed Helian and north shattered the Rouran, gaining beautiful women, treasures, horses and herds in droves."

sentences.zh: 南鎮諸將，聞而生羨，亦欲南抄，以取資財。

translations.literal: the southern garrison generals, hearing, were envious and also wished to raid south for goods and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: "Southern garrison generals, hearing this, grew envious and also wished to raid south for goods and wealth."

sentences.zh: 是以妄張賊勢，披毛求瑕，冀得肆心。

translations.literal: Therefore they falsely inflate bandit strength, pluck hairs to seek flaws, hoping to indulge their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore they falsely inflate enemy strength and pluck hairs to seek flaws, hoping to indulge their hearts."

sentences.zh: 既不獲聽，故數稱賊動以恐朝廷。

translations.literal: Since they could not gain approval, they repeatedly report bandit movement to frighten the court.
translations.idiomatic: "Denied approval, they repeatedly report enemy movement to frighten the court."

sentences.zh: 背公存私，為國生事，非忠也。

translations.literal: Turning their backs on the public to serve private ends, creating trouble for the state—not loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: "They turn their backs on the public to serve private ends and create trouble for the state—that is not loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」帝從浩議。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Hao's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Hao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 南鎮諸將表賊至，而自陳兵少，求簡幽州以南戍兵佐寧。

translations.literal: The southern garrison generals memorialized that bandits had arrived, yet themselves declared few troops and asked to select garrison troops south of Youzhou to assist defense.
translations.idiomatic: The southern garrison generals reported enemies at hand yet declared themselves short of troops and asked to draw garrison forces south of Youzhou to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 就漳水造船，嚴以為備。

translations.literal: They built boats on the Zhang River and made strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: They built boats on the Zhang River and made strict preparations.

sentences.zh: 公卿議者僉然，欲遣騎五千，並假署司馬楚之、魯軌、韓延之等，令誘引邊人。

translations.literal: Those who debated among the ministers were unanimous, wishing to send five thousand cavalry and provisionally appoint Sima Chuzhi, Lu Gui, Han Yanzhi, and others to entice frontier people.
translations.idiomatic: The debating ministers were unanimous, wishing to send five thousand cavalry and provisionally appoint Sima Chuzhi, Lu Gui, Han Yanzhi, and others to entice frontier people.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「非上策也。

translations.literal: Hao said: "This is not the upper stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "This is not the best stratagem."

sentences.zh: 彼聞幽州已南，精兵悉發，大造舟船，輕騎在後，欲存立司馬，誅除宋族，必舉國駭擾，懼於滅亡，當悉發精銳，來備北境。

translations.literal: When they hear that south of Youzhou elite troops have all been sent, great boat-building, light cavalry in the rear, wishing to establish Sima and exterminate the Song clan, they will surely be alarmed throughout the state, fearing destruction, and will send all elite strength to guard the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: "When they hear elite troops south of Youzhou are all sent, great boat-building, light cavalry in the rear, and plans to establish Sima and exterminate the Song clan, they will be alarmed throughout the state, fear destruction, and send all elite strength to guard the northern border."

sentences.zh: 後審知官軍有聲無實，恃其先聚，必喜而前行，徑來至河，肆其侵暴。

translations.literal: Later learning the official army has sound without substance, relying on their prior gathering, they will surely be pleased and advance, coming straight to the river to indulge in outrage.
translations.idiomatic: "Later, learning the official army has sound without substance, they will rely on their prior gathering, advance gladly, come straight to the river, and indulge in outrage."

sentences.zh: 則我守將，無以禦之。

translations.literal: Then our defending generals will have nothing to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: "Then our defending generals will have nothing with which to resist them."

sentences.zh: 若彼有見機之人，善設權譎，乘間深入，虞我國虛，生變不難。

translations.literal: If they have men who see the moment, skilled in setting stratagems, seizing the interval to advance deep, fearing our state is empty, trouble is not hard to raise.
translations.idiomatic: "If they have men who read the moment, skilled in stratagem, seizing the interval to advance deep while our state looks empty, trouble is not hard to raise."

sentences.zh: 非制敵之良計。

translations.literal: This is not a fine plan for controlling the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: "That is not a fine plan for controlling the enemy."

sentences.zh: 今公卿欲以威力攘賊，乃所以招令速至也。

translations.literal: Now the ministers wish to repel bandits by might—that is precisely what summons them to come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: "Now the ministers wish to repel the enemy by show of force—that is precisely what summons them quickly."

sentences.zh: 夫張虛聲而召實害，此之謂矣。

translations.literal: To raise empty sound and summon real harm—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: "Raise empty sound and summon real harm—that is what is meant."

sentences.zh: 不可不思，後悔無及。

translations.literal: You cannot fail to think; regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: "You cannot fail to think—regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 我使在彼，期四月前還，可待使至，審而後發，猶未晚也。

translations.literal: Our envoys are there, due to return before the fourth month; you can wait until the envoys arrive and investigate before acting—still not late.
translations.idiomatic: "Our envoys are there, due back before the fourth month. Wait until they return and investigate before acting—still not late."

sentences.zh: 楚之人徒，是彼所忌，將奪其國，彼安得端坐視之？

translations.literal: Chu's faction is what they hate—they will seize their state; how can they sit and watch?
translations.idiomatic: "Chu's faction is what they hate—they will seize their state. How can they sit and watch?"

sentences.zh: 故楚之往則彼來，楚之止則彼息，其勢然也。

translations.literal: Therefore when Chu goes they come; when Chu stops they rest—the situation is so.
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore when Chu goes they come; when Chu stops they rest—that is the pattern."

sentences.zh: 且楚之等瑣才，能招合輕薄無賴，而不能成就大功。

translations.literal: Moreover Chu and the rest are petty talents, able to gather the light and worthless but unable to achieve great merit.
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover Chu and the rest are petty talents, able to gather the light and worthless but unable to achieve great merit."

sentences.zh: 為國生事，使兵連禍結，必此之群矣。

translations.literal: Creating trouble for the state, making arms link calamity—surely this crowd.
translations.idiomatic: "Creating trouble for the state and linking arms to calamity—surely this crowd will do it."

sentences.zh: 臣嘗聞魯軌說姚興，求入荊州。

translations.literal: Your servant once heard Lu Gui persuade Yao Xing to let him enter Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: "I once heard Lu Gui persuade Yao Xing to let him enter Jingzhou."

sentences.zh: 至則散敗，乃不免蠻賊掠賣為奴，使禍及姚泓，已然之效。」

translations.literal: When he arrived he scattered and was defeated and could not escape being seized and sold as slaves by barbarian bandits, bringing calamity on Yao Hong—a result already seen."
translations.idiomatic: "When he arrived he scattered and was defeated, was seized and sold as slaves by barbarian bandits, and brought calamity on Yao Hong—an outcome already seen."

sentences.zh: 浩又陳天時不利於彼，曰：「今茲害氣在揚州，不宜先舉兵，一也。

translations.literal: Hao also stated that heaven's seasons were unfavorable to them, saying: "Now the baleful qi is in Yangzhou—one should not first raise arms.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also argued that heaven's seasons favored the enemy, saying, "The baleful qi now sits in Yangzhou—one should not strike first. That is the first sign."

sentences.zh: 午歲自刑，先發者傷，二也。

translations.literal: A wuwu year punishes itself—whoever strikes first is wounded—second.
translations.idiomatic: "A wuwu year punishes itself—whoever strikes first is wounded. That is the second."

sentences.zh: 日蝕滅光，晝昏星見，飛鳥墮落，宿當斗、牛，憂在危亡，三也。

translations.literal: An eclipse extinguishes light; day is dim and stars appear; birds fall from flight; lodges correspond to Dipper and Ox—worry is in peril and ruin—third.
translations.idiomatic: "An eclipse extinguishes light; day dims and stars appear; birds fall from the sky; lodges correspond to Dipper and Ox—worry lies in peril and ruin. That is the third."

sentences.zh: 熒惑伏匿於翼、軫，戒亂及喪，四也。

translations.literal: Mars hides in Wings and Axletree, warning of disorder and mourning—fourth.
translations.idiomatic: "Mars hides in Wings and Axletree, warning disorder and mourning. That is the fourth."

sentences.zh: 太白未出，進兵者敗，五也。

translations.literal: The White Star has not appeared—whoever advances is defeated—fifth.
translations.idiomatic: "The White Star has not appeared—whoever advances is defeated. That is the fifth."

sentences.zh: 夫興國之君，先修人事，次盡地利，後觀天時，故萬舉而萬全，國安而身盛。

translations.literal: The ruler who founds a state first cultivates human affairs, next exhausts earthly advantage, last observes heaven's seasons—therefore ten thousand acts and ten thousand successes, the state secure and the person flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: "The ruler who founds a state first cultivates human affairs, next exhausts earthly advantage, last observes heaven's seasons—then ten thousand acts bring ten thousand successes, the state secure and the ruler flourishing."

sentences.zh: 今宋新國，是人事未周也；

translations.literal: Now Song is a new state—human affairs are not complete;
translations.idiomatic: "Song is a new state—human affairs are not complete."

sentences.zh: 災變屢見，是天時不協也；

translations.literal: calamities and changes appear repeatedly—heaven's seasons are not in harmony;
translations.idiomatic: "Calamities appear again and again—heaven's seasons are not in harmony."

sentences.zh: 舟行水涸，是地利不盡也。

translations.literal: boats travel while waters dry—earthly advantage is not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: "Boats sail while waters dry—earthly advantage is not exhausted."

sentences.zh: 三事無一成，自守猶或不安，何得先發而攻人哉？

translations.literal: Of the three matters none is accomplished; even in defense one may not be secure—how can you first strike and attack others?
translations.idiomatic: "Of the three, none is accomplished—even defense may be unsafe. How can you strike first and attack others?"

sentences.zh: 彼必聽我虛聲而嚴，我亦承彼嚴而動，兩推其咎，皆自以為應敵。

translations.literal: They will surely hear our empty sound and grow strict; we also take their strictness and move—each pushes the blame, both thinking they respond to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: "They will hear our empty alarm and grow strict; we take their strictness and move—each pushes blame, both thinking they respond to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 兵法當分災，迎受害氣，未可舉動也。

translations.literal: In the art of war one should divide calamity and meet the baleful qi—you must not act.
translations.idiomatic: "In the art of war one should divide calamity and meet the baleful qi—you must not act."

sentences.zh: 」帝不能違眾，乃從公卿議。

translations.literal: The emperor could not defy the multitude and followed the ministers' plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not defy the multitude and followed the ministers' plan.

sentences.zh: 浩復固爭，不從。

translations.literal: Hao again stubbornly debated and was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao argued again but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 遂遣陽平王杜超鎮鄴，琅邪王司馬楚之等屯潁川。

translations.literal: They then sent the Prince of Yangping Du Chao to garrison Ye and the Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi and others to camp at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: They then sent Prince of Yangping Du Chao to garrison Ye and Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi and others to camp at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 於是寇來遂疾，到彥之自清水入河，

translations.literal: Thereupon the raiders came swiftly; Dao Yanzhi entered the river from Qingshui,
translations.idiomatic: The raiders then came swiftly. Dao Yanzhi entered the river from Qingshui,

sentences.zh: 泝流西行，分兵列守南岸，西至潼關。

translations.literal: sailed upstream west, divided troops to hold the south bank, west to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: sailed upstream west, divided troops to hold the south bank, and reached Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 帝聞赫連定與宋縣分河北，乃先討赫連。

translations.literal: The emperor heard Helian Ding and the Song were dividing Hebei and first campaigned against Helian.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Helian Ding and Song were dividing Hebei, the emperor first campaigned against Helian.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆曰：「義隆軍猶在河中，舍之西行，前寇未可必克；

translations.literal: The ministers all said: "Yilong's army is still in the river; leave them and go west—the prior foe cannot be surely taken;
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all said, "Yilong's army is still on the river. Leave them and march west—the foe ahead cannot be surely taken."

sentences.zh: 而義隆乘虛，則東州敗矣。

translations.literal: yet if Yilong seizes the opening, the eastern provinces will be lost."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet if Yilong seizes the opening, the eastern provinces will be lost."

sentences.zh: 」帝疑焉，問計於浩。

translations.literal: The emperor was doubtful and asked Hao for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated and asked Hao for counsel.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「義隆與赫連定同惡相連，招結馮跋，牽引蠕蠕，規肆逆心，虛相唱和。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Yilong and Helian Ding share the same evil and are linked, recruiting Feng Ba, drawing the Rouran, scheming rebellious hearts, singing to each other in emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Yilong and Helian Ding are joined in the same evil, recruiting Feng Ba, drawing the Rouran, scheming rebellion, singing empty encouragement to each other."

sentences.zh: 義隆望定進，定待義隆前，皆莫敢先入。

translations.literal: Yilong waits for Ding to advance; Ding waits for Yilong ahead—neither dares enter first.
translations.idiomatic: "Yilong waits for Ding to advance; Ding waits for Yilong ahead—neither dares enter first."

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，有似連雞，不得俱飛，無能為害也。

translations.literal: In your servant's view they are like chickens linked by a cord, unable to fly together, and cannot harm.
translations.idiomatic: "In my view they are like chickens tied by a cord, unable to fly together, and cannot harm us."

sentences.zh: 臣始謂義隆軍屯住河中，兩道北上，東道向冀州，西道沖鄴。

translations.literal: Your servant at first thought Yilong's army would halt in the river, with two routes north: the eastern route toward Jizhou, the western route against Ye.
translations.idiomatic: "I first thought Yilong's army would halt on the river with two routes north—the eastern toward Jizhou, the western against Ye."

sentences.zh: 如此則陛下當自致討，不得徐行。

translations.literal: If so Your Majesty should campaign in person and could not advance slowly.
translations.idiomatic: "If so Your Majesty would need to campaign in person and could not advance slowly."

sentences.zh: 今則不然，東西列兵，徑二千里中，一處不過千，形分勢弱。

translations.literal: Now it is not so: east and west they array troops; within two thousand li no place has more than a thousand—form divided, momentum weak.
translations.idiomatic: "Now it is not so. East and west they array troops; within two thousand li no post holds more than a thousand—form divided, momentum weak."

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，儜兒情見，正望固河自守，免死為幸，無北度意也。

translations.literal: From this view the weaklings' intent appears: they only hope to hold the river and defend, escape death as fortune, with no intent to cross north.
translations.idiomatic: "From this the weaklings' intent appears: they only hope to hold the river, escape death as fortune, with no intent to cross north."

sentences.zh: 赫連定殘根易摧，擬之必僕。

translations.literal: Helian Ding's remnant root is easy to break; strike him and he will surely fall.
translations.idiomatic: "Helian Ding's remnant root is easy to break; strike him and he will surely fall."

sentences.zh: ＩＮ定之後，東出潼關，席捲而前，威震南極，江淮以北無立草矣。

translations.literal: After Ding is secured, east out of Tong Pass, sweeping forward, awe shaking the southern pole—north of the Jiang and Huai not a blade of grass will stand.
translations.idiomatic: "After Ding is crushed, march east out of Tong Pass, sweep forward, and awe will shake the southern pole—north of the Yangtze and Huai not a blade of grass will stand."

sentences.zh: 聖策獨發，非愚近所及，願陛下必行無疑。」

translations.literal: The sage stratagem alone issues—not what the foolish and near can reach; I beg Your Majesty to act without doubt."
translations.idiomatic: "The sage stratagem issues alone—not what the foolish and near can grasp. I beg Your Majesty to act without doubt."

sentences.zh: 平涼既平，其日宴會，帝執浩手以示蒙遜使曰：「所雲崔公，此是也。

translations.literal: When Pingliang was pacified, that day at the banquet the emperor took Hao's hand to show the envoy of Meng Xun, saying: "The Lord Cui of whom I spoke—this is he.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingliang was pacified, at the banquet that day the emperor took Hao's hand to show Meng Xun's envoy, saying, "The Lord Cui I spoke of—this is he."

sentences.zh: 才略之美，當今無比。

translations.literal: His talent and stratagem have no peer today.
translations.idiomatic: "His talent and stratagem have no peer today."

sentences.zh: 朕行止必問，成敗決焉，若合符契。」

translations.literal: My comings and goings I must ask; success and failure he decides—as if tally and seal matched."
translations.idiomatic: "My every move I must ask him; success and failure he decides—as if tally and seal matched."

sentences.zh: 後冠軍安頡軍還，獻南俘，因說南賊之言云：「宋敕其諸將，若北國兵動，先其未至，徑前入河。

translations.literal: Later Champion General An Li's army returned and presented southern captives; he therefore reported the southern bandits' words, saying: "Song charged its generals: if northern troops move, before they arrive go straight into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Later Champion General An Li returned with southern captives and reported the enemy's words: "Song charged its generals: if northern troops move, enter the river before they arrive."

sentences.zh: 若其不動，住彭城勿進。

translations.literal: If they do not move, halt at Pengcheng and do not advance."
translations.idiomatic: "If they do not move, halt at Pengcheng and do not advance."

sentences.zh: 」如浩所量。

translations.literal: As Hao had measured.
translations.idiomatic: It was as Hao had measured.

sentences.zh: 帝謂公卿曰：「卿輩前謂我用浩計為謬，驚怖固諫。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the ministers: "You before said my using Hao's plan was wrong and in terror firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers, "You said my following Hao's plan was wrong and remonstrated in terror."

sentences.zh: 常勝之家，自謂逾人遠矣，至於歸終，乃不能及。

translations.literal: The ever-victorious house thinks itself far beyond others; at the end they still cannot match him."
translations.idiomatic: "The ever-victorious think themselves far beyond others; in the end they still cannot match him."

sentences.zh: 」遷浩司徒。

translations.literal: Hao was transferred to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 時方士祁纖奏立四王，以日東西南北為名，欲以致禎吉，除災異。

translations.literal: At the time the adept Qi Xian memorialized establishing four kings named for east, south, west, and north of the sun, wishing to bring auspicious fortune and remove calamities and anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the adept Qi Xian memorialized establishing four kings named for the sun's east, south, west, and north, wishing to bring fortune and remove calamities.

sentences.zh: 詔浩與學士議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hao to debate with the scholars.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hao to debate with the scholars.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「先王建國，以作籓屏，不應假名其福。

translations.literal: Hao said: "The former kings founded the state to make frontier screens; one should not borrow names for fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Former kings founded the state to make frontier screens; one should not borrow names for fortune."

sentences.zh: 夫日月運轉，周曆四方，京師所居，在於其內。

translations.literal: The sun and moon turn and circle the four directions; the capital dwells within them.
translations.idiomatic: "The sun and moon turn and circle the four directions; the capital dwells within them."

sentences.zh: 四王之稱，實奄邦畿，名之則逆，不可承用。

translations.literal: The title of four kings in fact covers the imperial domain; to name it is rebellious and cannot be accepted."
translations.idiomatic: "The title of four kings in fact covers the imperial domain; to name it is rebellious and cannot be accepted."

sentences.zh: 」先是，纖奏改代為萬年，浩曰：「昔太祖道武皇帝應期受命，開拓洪業，諸所制宜，無不循古。

translations.literal: Earlier Xian had memorialized changing Dai to Wannian; Hao said: "In the past the Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu received the mandate in his season, opened and expanded the great enterprise; all he established followed antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xian had memorialized changing Dai to Wannian. Hao said, "Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu received the mandate in his season and opened the great enterprise; all he established followed antiquity."

sentences.zh: 以始封代土，後稱為魏。

translations.literal: Because he was first enfeoffed on the soil of Dai, he later was called Wei.
translations.idiomatic: "Because he was first enfeoffed on the soil of Dai, he later was called Wei."

sentences.zh: 故代、魏兼用，猶彼殷、商。

translations.literal: Therefore Dai and Wei were used together, like Yin and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore Dai and Wei were used together, like Yin and Shang."

sentences.zh: 國家積德，著在圖史，當享萬億，不待假名以為益也。

translations.literal: The state's accumulated virtue is recorded in the histories; it should enjoy ten thousand myriads—one need not borrow a name for increase.
translations.idiomatic: "The state's accumulated virtue is recorded in the histories; it should enjoy endless ages without borrowing a name for increase."

sentences.zh: 纖之所聞，皆非正義。

translations.literal: What Xian has heard is all not righteous."
translations.idiomatic: "What Xian proposes is all unrighteous."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時河西王沮渠牧犍內有貳意，帝將討焉，先問於浩。

translations.literal: At the time the King of Hexi Juqu Mujian harbored divided loyalty; the emperor was about to campaign against him and first asked Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hexi king Juqu Mujian harbored divided loyalty. The emperor was about to campaign and first asked Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「牧犍噁心已露，不可不誅。

translations.literal: Hao replied: "Mujian's wicked heart is already exposed—he cannot fail to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "Mujian's wicked heart is already exposed—he must be executed."

sentences.zh: 官軍往年北伐，雖不ＩＮ獲，實無所損。

translations.literal: When the official army campaigned north in years past, though it did not capture all, in truth there was no harm.
translations.idiomatic: "When the official army campaigned north in years past, though it did not capture all, in truth there was no harm."

sentences.zh: 于時行者，內外軍馬三十萬匹，計在道死傷，不滿八千。

translations.literal: At that time those who marched, inner and outer army horses, were three hundred thousand head; counting dead and wounded on the road, not full eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: "At that time inner and outer forces mustered three hundred thousand horses; dead and wounded on the road numbered fewer than eight thousand."

sentences.zh: 歲常羸死，恆不減萬，乃不少於前。

translations.literal: Each year lean deaths are constant, never less than ten thousand—thus not less than before.
translations.idiomatic: "Each year lean deaths alone are constant, never fewer than ten thousand—not less than the campaign's toll."

sentences.zh: 而遠方承虛，便謂大損，不能復振。

translations.literal: Yet distant lands heard the empty report and thought the great loss meant they could not rise again.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet distant lands heard empty report and thought the great loss meant we could not rise again."

sentences.zh: 今出其不圖，大軍卒至，必驚懼騷擾，不知所出，擒之必矣。

translations.literal: Now strike them unawares; the great army arrives suddenly—they will surely be terrified and in turmoil, not knowing what to do, and capture is certain."
translations.idiomatic: "Strike them unawares now. The great army arrives suddenly—they will be terrified and in turmoil, not knowing what to do, and capture is certain."

sentences.zh: 牧犍幼弱，諸弟驕恣，爭權縱橫，人心離解。

translations.literal: Mujian is young and weak; his younger brothers are arrogant and unrestrained, contending for power across the realm; hearts are divided and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: "Mujian is young and weak; his brothers are arrogant, contending for power; hearts are divided."

sentences.zh: 加以比年以來，天災地變，都在秦、涼，成滅之國也。」

translations.literal: Moreover in recent years heaven's disasters and earth's changes have all been in Qin and Liang—a state ripe for destruction."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover in recent years heaven's disasters and earth's changes have all fallen in Qin and Liang—a state ripe for destruction."

sentences.zh: 帝命公卿議之，恆農王奚斤等三十餘人皆表曰：「牧犍西垂下國，雖心不為純臣，然繼父修職貢，朝廷接以蕃禮。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministers to debate; Prince of Hengnong Xi Jin and more than thirty others all memorialized, saying: "Mujian is a western frontier petty state; though his heart is not that of a pure vassal, he succeeded his father in maintaining tribute and the court received him with frontier ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered debate. Prince of Hengnong Xi Jin and more than thirty others memorialized, "Mujian is a western frontier petty state. Though not a pure vassal at heart, he succeeded his father in tribute and the court received him with frontier ritual."

sentences.zh: 又王姬厘降，罪未甚彰，謂且羈縻而已。

translations.literal: Moreover a royal princess was sent in marriage; the crime is not very clear—we say only to keep him on a loose rein.
translations.idiomatic: "A royal princess was sent in marriage; his crime is not glaring—we say only to keep him on a loose rein."

sentences.zh: 令士馬勞止，可宜小息。

translations.literal: Now horses and men are weary and should rest a little.
translations.idiomatic: "Horses and men are weary and should rest a little."

sentences.zh: 又其地鹵斥，略無水草，大軍既到，不得久停。

translations.literal: Moreover their land is brackish and barren, almost without grass and water; when the great army arrives it cannot long halt.
translations.idiomatic: "Their land is brackish and barren, almost without grass and water; when the great army arrives it cannot long halt."

sentences.zh: 彼聞軍來，必完聚城守，攻則難拔，野無所掠。

translations.literal: When they hear the army comes they will surely complete walls and hold the city; attack is hard to pull down and in the wild there is nothing to seize."
translations.idiomatic: "When they hear the army comes they will complete walls and hold the city; attack is hard and the wild offers nothing to seize."

sentences.zh: 」於是尚書古弼、李順之徒皆曰：「自溫闈河以西至於涼州，地純枯石，了無水草，不見流川。

translations.literal: Then Director Gu Bi, Li Shun, and the rest all said: "From west of Wen Gate River to Liangzhou the land is pure dry stone, utterly without grass and water, no flowing streams seen.
translations.idiomatic: Then Director Gu Bi, Li Shun, and the rest said, "From west of Wen Gate River to Liangzhou the land is pure dry stone, utterly without grass, water, or flowing streams."

sentences.zh: 皆言姑臧城南天梯山上，冬有積雪深一丈，至春夏消液，下流成川，引以溉灌。

translations.literal: All say south of Guzang city on Tianti Mountain winter snow piles one zhang deep; by spring and summer it melts and flows down to form a stream drawn for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: "All say south of Guzang on Tianti Mountain winter snow piles one zhang deep; by spring and summer it melts, flows down, and is drawn for irrigation."

sentences.zh: 彼聞軍至，決此渠口，水不通流，則致渴乏。

translations.literal: When they hear the army comes they will break this channel mouth so water does not flow and bring thirst and exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: "When they hear the army comes they will break the channel so water does not flow and bring thirst and exhaustion."

sentences.zh: 去城百里之內，赤地無草，不任久停軍馬。

translations.literal: Within a hundred li of the city is red earth without grass—cannot long station horses and men.
translations.idiomatic: "Within a hundred li of the city is red earth without grass—it cannot long support horses and men."

sentences.zh: 斤等議是也。

translations.literal: Jin and the rest's plan is right."
translations.idiomatic: "Xi Jin and the rest are right."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃命浩以其前言與斤共相難抑。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Hao to use his former words and debate sharply with Jin together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Hao to take his former argument and debate sharply with Xi Jin.

sentences.zh: 諸人不復餘言，唯曰彼無水草。

translations.literal: The others had no further words and only said there was no grass or water there.
translations.idiomatic: The others had no further argument and only repeated that there was no grass or water.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「《漢書地理志》稱' 涼州之畜，為天下饒'，若無水草，何以畜牧？

translations.literal: Hao said: "The Treatise on Geography in the Book of Han says 'The livestock of Liangzhou are the richest under heaven'—if there were no grass and water, how could they pasture?
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "The Book of Han's Treatise on Geography says, 'The livestock of Liangzhou are the richest under heaven.' Without grass and water, how could they pasture?"

sentences.zh: 又漢人為居，終不於無水草之地築城郭立郡縣也。

translations.literal: Moreover Han people dwell there—they would never build walls and cities and establish commanderies and counties on land without grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: "Han people dwell there—they would never build walls, cities, commanderies, and counties on land without grass and water."

sentences.zh: 又雪之消液，裁不斂塵，何得通渠引漕，溉灌數百萬頃乎？

translations.literal: Moreover when snow melts it can barely gather dust—how could it open channels and draw irrigation for millions of qing?
translations.idiomatic: "When snow melts it can barely wet dust—how could it open channels and irrigate millions of qing?"

sentences.zh: 此言大詆誣於人矣。」

translations.literal: This talk greatly slanders men."
translations.idiomatic: "This talk grossly slanders the truth."

sentences.zh: 李順等復曰：「吾曹目見，何可共辯？

translations.literal: Li Shun and the rest again said: "We ourselves have seen it—how can we debate together?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun and the rest said again, "We have seen it with our own eyes—how can we debate together?"

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「汝曹受人金錢，欲為之辭，謂我目不見便可欺也！

translations.literal: Hao said: "You all received men's gold and wish to speak for them—you think because my eyes do not see I can be deceived!"
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "You received men's gold and wish to speak for them—you think because I did not see it I can be deceived!"

sentences.zh: 」帝隱聽，聞之乃出，親見斤等。

translations.literal: The emperor listened hidden, heard this, and came out to see Jin and the rest in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened in secret, heard this, and came out to see Xi Jin and the rest in person.

sentences.zh: 辭旨嚴厲，形於神色。

translations.literal: His words were stern and severity showed in his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His words were stern and severity showed in his face.

sentences.zh: 群臣乃不敢復言。

translations.literal: The ministers then dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers then dared speak no more.

sentences.zh: 於是遂討涼州，平之。

translations.literal: They then campaigned against Liangzhou and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: They then campaigned against Liangzhou and pacified it.

sentences.zh: 多饒水草，如浩所言。

translations.literal: Grass and water were abundant, as Hao had said.
translations.idiomatic: Grass and water were abundant, as Hao had said.

sentences.zh: 乃詔浩總理史務，務從實錄。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Hao to oversee historical affairs, striving for truthful records.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Hao to oversee historical affairs and strive for truthful records.

sentences.zh: 於是監秘書事，以中書侍郎高允、散騎侍郎張偉參著作，續成前紀。

translations.literal: He then supervised secretariat affairs, with Palace Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun and Palace Cadet Zhang Wei participating in composition, continuing the former chronicle.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised secretariat affairs, with Palace Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun and Palace Cadet Zhang Wei joining the compilation to continue the former chronicle.

sentences.zh: 至於損益褒貶，折衷潤色，浩所總焉。

translations.literal: As for additions and subtractions, praise and blame, weighing and polishing, Hao was master.
translations.idiomatic: Additions, subtractions, praise, blame, weighing, and polishing were all in Hao's hands.

sentences.zh: 浩有鑒識，以人倫為己任。

translations.literal: Hao had discernment and took human relations as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had discernment and took human relations as his charge.

sentences.zh: 明元、太武之世，征海內賢才，起自仄陋。

translations.literal: In the eras of Mingyuan and Taiwu the state sought worthy talent within the seas, raising men from humble places.
