translations.idiomatic: In the eras of Mingyuan and Taiwu the state sought worthy talent across the realm, raising men from humble places.

sentences.zh: 及所得外國遠方名士，拔而用之，皆浩之由也。

translations.literal: Worthy men of foreign and distant lands obtained and employed—all were through Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men from foreign and distant lands obtained and employed—all came through Hao.

sentences.zh: 至於禮樂憲章，皆歸宗於浩。

translations.literal: As for ritual, music, statutes, and regulations, all looked to Hao as their source.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual, music, statutes, and regulations all looked to Hao as their source.

sentences.zh: 及景穆始總百揆，浩復與宜都王穆壽輔政事。

translations.literal: When Jingmu first held the hundred offices, Hao again assisted in government with Prince of Yidu Mu Shou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingmu first held the hundred offices, Hao again assisted government with Prince of Yidu Mu Shou.

sentences.zh: 又將討蠕蠕，劉潔復致異議。

translations.literal: They were again about to campaign against the Rouran; Liu Jie again raised objections.
translations.idiomatic: They were again about to campaign against the Rouran; Liu Jie again objected.

sentences.zh: 帝愈欲討之，乃召問浩。

translations.literal: The emperor wished all the more to campaign and summoned Hao to ask.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished all the more to campaign and summoned Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「往擊蠕蠕，師不多日，潔等各欲回還。

translations.literal: Hao replied: "In the past campaign against the Rouran, the army was not many days out when Jie and the rest each wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "In the past campaign against the Rouran, the army had not been out many days when Jie and the rest each wished to return."

sentences.zh: 後獲尚書，雲軍還之時，去賊三十里，是潔等之計過矣。

translations.literal: Later they obtained a letter from the enemy saying when the army returned it was thirty li from the bandits—that was Jie and the rest's plan gone too far.
translations.idiomatic: "Later we obtained an enemy letter saying when the army returned it was thirty li from the bandits—that was Jie and the rest pushing the plan too far."

sentences.zh: 夫北土多積雪，至冬時，常避寒南徙。

translations.literal: The northern lands have much accumulated snow; in winter they always avoid cold and migrate south.
translations.idiomatic: "The northern lands hold much snow; in winter they always flee cold and migrate south."

sentences.zh: 若因其時，潛軍而出，必與之遇。

translations.literal: If you use that season and march the army out secretly, you will surely meet them.
translations.idiomatic: "Use that season, march the army out secretly, and you will surely meet them."

sentences.zh: 既與之遇，則可禽獲。

translations.literal: Once you meet them, you can capture them."
translations.idiomatic: "Once you meet them, you can capture them."

sentences.zh: 」帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃分軍四道，諸將俱會鹿渾海。

translations.literal: They then divided the army into four routes; the generals all met at Luhun Sea.
translations.idiomatic: They divided the army into four routes; the generals all met at Luhun Sea.

sentences.zh: 期日有定，而潔恨計不用，沮誤諸將，無功而還。

translations.literal: The day of meeting was fixed, but Jie, resenting that his plan was not used, discouraged and misled the generals, and returned without merit.
translations.idiomatic: The rendezvous day was fixed, but Jie, resenting that his plan was not used, discouraged and misled the generals, and they returned without merit.

sentences.zh: 帝西巡至東雍，親臨汾曲，觀叛賊薛永宗壘，進軍圍之。

translations.literal: The emperor toured west to East Yong, personally came to Fenqu, viewed the rebel Xue Yongzong's ramparts, and advanced the army to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor toured west to East Yong, came personally to Fenqu, viewed rebel Xue Yongzong's ramparts, and advanced to besiege them.

sentences.zh: 永宗出兵欲戰，帝問浩曰：「今日可擊否？

translations.literal: Yongzong sent troops wishing to fight; the emperor asked Hao: "Can we strike today?"
translations.idiomatic: Yongzong sent troops to fight. The emperor asked Hao, "Can we strike today?"

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「永宗未知陛下自來，人心安固。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Yongzong does not know Your Majesty has come in person; men's hearts are secure and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Yongzong does not know Your Majesty has come in person; his men's hearts are secure."

sentences.zh: 北風迅疾，宜急擊之，須臾必破。

translations.literal: The north wind is swift; you should strike urgently and in a moment you will surely break them.
translations.idiomatic: "The north wind is swift. Strike urgently and you will break them in a moment."

sentences.zh: 若待明日，恐見官軍盛大，必夜遁走。

translations.literal: If you wait until tomorrow, fearing they see the official army's grandeur, they will surely flee by night."
translations.idiomatic: "Wait until tomorrow and, seeing the official army's grandeur, they will flee by night."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，永宗潰滅。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; Yongzong collapsed and was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this counsel; Yongzong collapsed and was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 車駕濟河，前驅告賊在渭北。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage crossed the river; the vanguard reported bandits on the north bank of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage crossed the river; the vanguard reported bandits on the north bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝至洛水橋，賊已夜遁。

translations.literal: The emperor reached Luoshui Bridge; the bandits had already fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reached Luoshui Bridge; the bandits had already fled by night.

sentences.zh: 詔問浩曰：「蓋吳在長安北九十里，渭北地空，穀草不備，欲度渭南西行，何如？

translations.literal: An edict asked Hao: "Gai Wu is ninety li north of Chang'an; north of the Wei the land lies empty, grain and fodder are not stocked. We wish to cross south of the Wei and march west—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Hao: "Gai Wu lies ninety li north of Chang'an. North of the Wei the country is bare—no grain, no fodder. We mean to cross the Wei and march west. What do you say?"

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「蓋吳營去此六十里，賊魁所在。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Gai Wu's camp is sixty li from here—that is where the rebel chief sits."
translations.idiomatic: " Hao answered: "Gai Wu's camp is sixty li away. That is where the rebel leader sits."

sentences.zh: 擊蛇之法，當先破頭，頭破則尾豈能動？

translations.literal: The method for striking a serpent: one must first break the head; when the head is broken, how can the tail stir?"
translations.idiomatic: Strike a serpent: break the head first. Break the head and the tail cannot move."

sentences.zh: 宜乘勢先擊吳。

translations.literal: We ought to seize the moment and strike Gai Wu first."
translations.idiomatic: Take the moment and strike Gai Wu first."

sentences.zh: 今軍往，一日便到。

translations.literal: If the army goes now, we reach him in a single day."
translations.idiomatic: March now and we arrive in a day."

sentences.zh: 吳平之後，回向長安，亦一日而至。

translations.literal: After Gai Wu is pacified, we turn back toward Chang'an, and that too is one day's march."
translations.idiomatic: Once Gai Wu is down, we turn back to Chang'an—again one day."

sentences.zh: 一日之乏，未便損傷。

translations.literal: One day's fatigue will not yet do harm."
translations.idiomatic: One day's weariness will not yet harm the men."

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜從北道。

translations.literal: In my humble view we should take the northern route."
translations.idiomatic: I would take the northern road."

sentences.zh: 若從南道，則蓋吳徐入北山，卒未可平。

translations.literal: If we take the southern route, Gai Wu will slowly slip into the northern hills and in the end cannot be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Take the southern road and Gai Wu will slip into the northern hills at leisure—and never be crushed."

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，乃度渭南。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not follow him and crossed south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen. He crossed south of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 吳聞帝至，盡散入北山，果如浩言。

translations.literal: Gai Wu heard the emperor had arrived; all scattered into the northern hills—just as Hao had said.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wu heard the emperor was coming. His men scattered into the northern hills—exactly as Hao had warned.

sentences.zh: 軍無所克，帝悔之。

translations.literal: The army took nothing; the emperor repented of it.
translations.idiomatic: The army won nothing. The emperor repented.

sentences.zh: 後以浩輔東宮之勤，賜繒絮布各千段。

translations.literal: Later, because of Hao's diligence in assisting the Eastern Palace, he was granted one thousand bolts each of silk floss and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his service to the crown prince, Hao received a thousand bolts each of floss silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 帝蒐於河西，詔浩詣行所議軍事。

translations.literal: When the emperor hunted in Hexi, he edicted Hao to come to the camp to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt in Hexi the emperor summoned Hao to the camp to discuss military affairs.

sentences.zh: 浩表曰：「昔漢武患匈奴強盛，故開涼州五郡，通西域，廣農積穀，為滅賊之資，東西迭擊。

translations.literal: Hao memorialized: "Formerly Emperor Wu of Han worried that the Xiongnu were strong and flourishing; therefore he opened the five commanderies of Liangzhou, connected with the Western Regions, spread agriculture and heaped grain, gathering resources to destroy the enemy, striking east and west in alternation."
translations.idiomatic: Hao memorialized: "Han Wudi feared the Xiongnu while they were strong. He opened Liangzhou's five commanderies, reached the Western Regions, farmed and stored grain, and built the means to destroy the foe—striking east and west in turn."

sentences.zh: 故漢未疲而匈奴已弊，後遂入朝。

translations.literal: Thus Han had not yet grown weary when the Xiongnu were already spent, and afterward they came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Han had not yet worn itself out when the Xiongnu were spent—and later they came to court.

sentences.zh: 昔平涼州，臣愚以為北賊未平，征役不息，可不徙其人，案前世故事，計之長者。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was pacified in the past, I in my foolishness thought that while northern rebels were not yet pacified and levies and corvée did not cease, one ought not relocate its people—examining earlier precedents, this was the long-term calculation.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzhou was pacified I argued, foolishly, that with northern rebels still abroad and levies unceasing, its people should not be moved—that ancient precedent was the far-sighted plan.

sentences.zh: 若徙其人，則土地空虛，雖有鎮戍，適可禦邊而已。

translations.literal: If you relocate the people, the land becomes empty; though there are garrison troops, they can only barely guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Move the people and the land goes hollow. Garrisons may remain, but they can only hold the border.

sentences.zh: 至於大舉，軍資必乏。

translations.literal: When it comes to a major campaign, military stores are sure to fall short.
translations.idiomatic: For a great campaign, supplies will fail.

sentences.zh: 陛下以此事闊遠，竟不施用。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because this matter seemed broad and distant, in the end did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty thought the matter too distant and did not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚意，猶如前議，募徙豪強大家，充實涼土。

translations.literal: As in my foolish opinion, it is still as I urged before: recruit and move wealthy powerful households to fill out the Liang lands.
translations.idiomatic: My view is unchanged: recruit and settle great families to fill the Liang country.

sentences.zh: 軍舉之日，東西齊勢，此計之得者。」

translations.literal: When the armies march, east and west strike together—that is the winning plan."
translations.idiomatic: When armies move, strike east and west together—that is the winning plan."

sentences.zh: 浩又上《五寅元曆》。

translations.literal: Hao also submitted the Five Yin Primordial Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also presented the Five Yin Primordial Calendar.

sentences.zh: 表曰：「太宗即位元年，敕臣解《急就章》、《孝經》、《論語》、《詩》、《尚書》、《春秋》、《禮記》、《周易》，三年成訖。

translations.literal: His memorial said: "In the first year of Emperor Taizong's accession, he charged me to explicate the Rapid Writing Primer, the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Odes, the Documents, the Spring and Autumn, the Record of Rites, and the Changes—completed in three years."
translations.idiomatic: His memorial said: "In Taizong's first year I was ordered to master the Rapid Writing Primer, Filial Piety, Analects, Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, Rites, and Changes—finished in three years."

sentences.zh: 復詔臣學天文星曆、《易》式、九宮，無不盡看。

translations.literal: He again edicted me to study astronomical stars and calendars, Yi forms, and the Nine Palaces, and there was nothing I did not read through thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: He again ordered me to study stars, calendars, Yi forms, and the Nine Palaces—I read everything through.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，晝夜無廢。

translations.literal: For thirty-nine years, day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty-nine years I did not rest, day or night.

sentences.zh: 臣稟性弱劣，力不及健婦人，更無餘能，是以專心思書，忘寢與食。

translations.literal: My nature is weak and inferior; my strength does not match a vigorous woman's, and I have no other ability—therefore I devoted mind to books, forgetting sleep and eating.
translations.idiomatic: I am weak by nature—no stronger than a hardy woman—and have no other gift. I gave my mind to books and forgot sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 至乃夢共鬼爭義，遂得周公、孔子之要術。

translations.literal: Indeed I dreamed of quarreling with ghosts over meaning, and thus obtained the essential arts of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: I even dreamed I argued meaning with ghosts—and so came to the essentials of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius.

sentences.zh: 始知古人有虛有實，妄語者多，真正者少。

translations.literal: Then I knew that the ancients had empty and full, that those who spoke falsely were many and those who spoke truly few.
translations.idiomatic: Then I knew the ancients mixed empty with full: false words were many, true words few.

sentences.zh: 自秦始皇燒書之後，經典絕滅。

translations.literal: After the First Emperor of Qin burned the books, the classics were cut off and perished.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Shihuang burned the books, the classics died.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖以來，世人妄造曆術者十餘家，皆不得天道之正。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Gao of Han, people in the world who rashly made calendar arts were more than ten households, and none obtained the correctness of Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han Gaozu more than ten houses rashly made calendars—and none caught Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 大誤四千，小誤甚多，不可言盡。

translations.literal: Great errors numbered four thousand, small errors were very many, beyond telling.
translations.idiomatic: Great errors ran to four thousand; small errors beyond count.

sentences.zh: 臣湣其如此。

translations.literal: I pitied that it was so.
translations.idiomatic: I pitied it.

sentences.zh: 今遭陛下太平之世，除偽從真，宜改誤曆，以從天道。

translations.literal: Now, encountering Your Majesty's era of great peace, eliminating falsehood and following truth, the mistaken calendar ought to be reformed to accord with Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in Your Majesty's peace, casting out falsehood for truth, the false calendar should be corrected to Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 是以臣前奏造曆，今始成訖，謹以奏。

translations.literal: Therefore I earlier memorialized to make a calendar; it is now completed, respectfully submitted.
translations.idiomatic: I memorialized earlier to make a calendar. It is done. I submit it humbly.

sentences.zh: 惟恩省察，以臣曆術，宣示中書博士，然後施用。

translations.literal: I humbly ask Your gracious examination; let my calendar art be displayed to the Erudites of the Central Secretariat, and afterward put into use.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to examine it, show my art to the Secretariat erudites, and then put it in use.

sentences.zh: 非但時人，天地鬼神知臣得正，可以益國家萬世之名，過於三皇、五帝矣。

translations.literal: Not only people of the time—even Heaven and Earth and ghosts will know I have obtained correctness; the nation's renown for ten thousand generations may surpass the Three August Ones and Five Thearchs."
translations.idiomatic: Not only men of this age—Heaven, Earth, and ghosts will know I have the right measure. The nation's fame for ten thousand generations may surpass the Three August Ones and Five Thearchs."

sentences.zh: 」浩又以《晉書》諸家並多誤，著《晉後書》，未就，傳世者五十餘卷。

translations.literal: Hao also, because the various houses of Jin History were largely in error, composed Post-Jin History; it was not finished, but more than fifty scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Jin histories mostly wrong, Hao wrote a Post-Jin History. It was unfinished; more than fifty scrolls still circulated.

sentences.zh: 初，道武詔秘書郎鄧彥海著國記十餘卷，編年次事，體例未成，逮於明元，廢不著述。

translations.literal: At the start, Daowu edicted the Secretarial Gentleman Deng Yanhai to compose a National Record of more than ten scrolls, arranging events by year, but the form and example were not fixed; by Mingyuan's time it was abandoned and no longer written.
translations.idiomatic: At first Daowu ordered Deng Yanhai to write a National Record of more than ten scrolls, year by year, but the form was never settled. By Mingyuan the work was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 神蒨二年，詔集諸文人摭錄國書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenqi, an edict gathered literary men to compile the national annals.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenqi year two an edict gathered scholars to compile the national annals.

sentences.zh: 浩及弟覽、高讜、鄧穎、晁繼、范享、黃輔等共參著作，敘成國書三十卷。

translations.literal: Hao together with his younger brothers Lan and Gao Dan, Deng Ying, Chao Ji, Fan Xiang, Huang Fu, and others jointly participated in the compilation; they narrated and completed the National Record in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, his brothers Lan and Gao Dan, Deng Ying, Chao Ji, Fan Xiang, Huang Fu, and others compiled together and finished a thirty-scroll National Record.

sentences.zh: 著作令史太原閔堪、趙郡郤標素諂事浩，乃請立石，銘載國書，以彰直筆。

translations.literal: The Compiling Clerks Taiyuan Min Kan and Zhao commandery Xi Biao had always flattered and served Hao; they requested to set up stone and inscribe the National Record, to display the straight brush.
translations.idiomatic: Compiling clerks Min Kan of Taiyuan and Xi Biao of Zhao commandery, who had always fawned on Hao, asked to set up stone and inscribe the National Record—to show the straight brush.

sentences.zh: 並勒浩所注《五經》。

translations.literal: They also carved Hao's commentaries on the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: They also carved Hao's commentaries on the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 浩贊成之，景穆善焉。

translations.literal: Hao agreed to it, and Jingmu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Hao approved; Jingmu was pleased.

sentences.zh: 遂營於天郊東三里，方百步，用功三百萬乃訖。

translations.literal: They therefore built at three li east of the suburban altar, a plot a hundred paces square; three million work-units were spent before it was done.
translations.idiomatic: They built three li east of the suburban altar on a square plot a hundred paces across—three million work-units before it was finished.

sentences.zh: 浩書國事備而不典，而石銘顯在衢路，北人咸悉忿毒，相與構浩於帝。

translations.literal: Hao's writing of national affairs was complete but not canonical, yet the stone inscription stood conspicuous on the main road; northerners all deeply harbored resentment and together framed Hao before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's account of state affairs was full but not canonical—yet the stone stood plain on the highway. Northerners burned with hate and together denounced him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，使有司案浩，取秘書郎及長曆生數百人意狀。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and had the authorities investigate Hao, taking depositions from several hundred Secretarial Gentlemen and long-calendar clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged and ordered an inquiry, taking statements from hundreds of secretarial clerks and calendar officers.

sentences.zh: 浩服受賕。

translations.literal: Hao confessed to receiving bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Hao confessed to taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 真君十一年六月，誅浩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year of Zhenjun, Hao was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhenjun eleven, Hao was executed.

sentences.zh: 清河崔氏無遠近，及范陽盧氏、太原郭氏、河東柳氏，皆浩之姻親，盡夷其族。

translations.literal: The Qinghe Cui clan, near and far, together with the Fanyang Lu clan, Taiyuan Guo clan, and Hedong Liu clan—all Hao's affines—had their entire lineages exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The Qinghe Cui, near and far, with the Fanyang Lu, Taiyuan Guo, and Hedong Liu—all Hao's kin by marriage—were exterminated to the last.

sentences.zh: 其秘書郎史以下盡死。

translations.literal: Secretarial clerks, history clerks, and those below—all were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Secretarial clerks and recorders below them—all were killed.

sentences.zh: 浩始弱冠，太原郭逸以女妻之。

translations.literal: When Hao was first capped at twenty, Taiyuan Guo Yi gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping, twenty, Taiyuan Guo Yi gave him his daughter.

sentences.zh: 浩晚成，不曜華采，故時人未知。

translations.literal: Hao matured late and did not shine with splendor; thus men of the time did not yet know him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao bloomed late and wore no brilliance; men of the time did not yet know him.

sentences.zh: 逸妻王氏，宋鎮北將軍王仲德姊也。

translations.literal: Yi's wife was surnamed Wang, elder sister of Song's General of Pacifying the North Wang Zhongde.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's wife Wang was elder sister to Song's General of Pacifying the North Wang Zhongde.

sentences.zh: 每奇浩才能，自以為得婿。

translations.literal: She always marveled at Hao's talent and believed she had gained a worthy son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: She always marveled at Hao's gifts and thought she had won a true son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 俄而女亡，王氏深以傷恨，復欲以少女繼昏。

translations.literal: Before long the daughter died; Dame Wang deeply grieved and wished to give him a younger daughter in second marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the daughter died. Dame Wang grieved deeply and wished to give him a younger daughter in marriage again.

sentences.zh: 逸及親屬以為不可，王氏固執與之。

translations.literal: Yi and relatives thought it could not be done, but Dame Wang insisted on giving her to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and kin thought it could not be, but Dame Wang insisted.

sentences.zh: 逸不能違，遂重結好。

translations.literal: Yi could not refuse and they renewed the bond of marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yi could not refuse. The marriage bond was renewed.

sentences.zh: 浩非毀佛法，而妻郭氏敬好釋典，時時讀誦。

translations.literal: Hao was not one who slandered the Buddhist Law, but his wife of the Guo clan revered and loved Buddhist sutras and from time to time recited them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao did not slander the Buddhist Law, but his wife Guo revered the sutras and read them often.

sentences.zh: 浩怒，取而焚之，捐灰廁中。

translations.literal: Hao grew angry, took them, and burned them, casting the ashes into the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Hao seized them in anger, burned them, and threw the ashes in the privy.

sentences.zh: 及浩幽執，被置檻內，送于城南，使衛士數十人溲其上，呼聲嗷嗷，聞于行路。

translations.literal: When Hao was imprisoned in secret, he was placed in a cage and sent to the south of the city; dozens of guards urinated on him; his howling reached the road.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned, he was caged and sent south of the city. Dozens of guards urinated on him. His howls reached the road.

sentences.zh: 自宰司之被戮辱，未有如浩者，世皆以為報應之驗。

translations.literal: Since ministers and grandees suffered disgrace of execution, none had been like Hao; all in the world took it as proof of retribution.
translations.idiomatic: No minister had ever been shamed and killed like Hao. The world called it retribution.

sentences.zh: 初，浩害李順，基萌已成，夜夢以火爇順寢室，火作而順死。

translations.literal: At the start, Hao harmed Li Shun; the foundation and sprouts were already formed. At night he dreamed he set fire to Shun's bedchamber; when the fire rose, Shun died.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao harmed Li Shun the seed was already sown. He dreamed he burned Shun's chamber; the fire rose and Shun died.

sentences.zh: 浩與室家群立觀之。

translations.literal: Hao and his household stood in a crowd watching.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and his household stood watching.

sentences.zh: 俄而順弟息號哭而出，曰：「此輩吾賊也！

translations.literal: Before long Shun's younger kinsman came out crying and said: "These men are my enemies!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shun's younger kinsman ran out crying: "These are my enemies!"

sentences.zh: 」以戈擊之，悉投於河。

translations.literal: " He struck them with a spear and cast them all into the river.
translations.idiomatic: " He struck them with a spear and cast them all into the river.

sentences.zh: 寤而以告館客馮景仁，曰：「此真不善也。

translations.literal: On waking he told his lodging guest Feng Jingren: "This is truly inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Waking, he told his guest Feng Jingren: "This is truly ill-omened."

sentences.zh: 夫以火爇人，暴之極也。

translations.literal: To burn someone with fire is violence at its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: To burn a man is violence at its height.

sentences.zh: 且兆始惡者有終殃，積不善者無餘慶。

translations.literal: Moreover, an omen that begins in evil has a final calamity; he who heaps up unkindness has no surplus of blessing.
translations.idiomatic: An omen that starts in evil ends in ruin. He who heaps up wrong has no surplus of blessing.

sentences.zh: 厲階成矣，公其圖之。

translations.literal: The steps of ruin are formed; you must take thought for it.
translations.idiomatic: The stair of ruin is built. You must reckon with it.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「吾方思之。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "I am just thinking about it."
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said: "I am thinking about it."

sentences.zh: 」而不能悛，至是而族。

translations.literal: Yet he could not repent, and at this time his clan was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He could not repent—and now his clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 浩既工書，人多托寫《急就章》，從少至老，初不憚勞。

translations.literal: Since Hao was skilled at calligraphy, many people entrusted him to copy the Rapid Writing Primer; from youth to old age he never shrank from labor.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in calligraphy, many entrusted him with the Rapid Writing Primer. From youth to age he never shirked the work.

sentences.zh: 所書蓋以百數，必稱「馮代強」，以示不敢犯國。

translations.literal: What he wrote must have numbered in the hundreds; he always signed "Feng Daiqiang," to show he did not dare transgress the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His copies ran to hundreds. He always signed "Feng Daiqiang"—to show he would not offend the state.

sentences.zh: 其謹也如此。

translations.literal: So cautious was he.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his caution.

sentences.zh: 浩書體勢及其先人，而巧妙不如也。

translations.literal: Hao's calligraphic form and momentum followed his forebears, yet in subtle craft he was not their equal.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's forms followed his forebears; in subtle craft he fell short.

sentences.zh: 世寶其跡，多裁割綴連，以為摹楷。

translations.literal: The world treasured his traces; many trimmed, cut, patched, and joined them to serve as models for copying.
translations.idiomatic: The world treasured his traces. Many trimmed and patched them into copy models.

sentences.zh: 浩母，盧諶孫女也。

translations.literal: Hao's mother was a granddaughter of Lu Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's mother was Lu Chen's granddaughter.

sentences.zh: 浩著《食經序》曰：「餘自少及長，耳目聞見，諸母諸姑所修婦功，無不蘊習酒食。

translations.literal: Hao composed the Preface to the Food Classic: "From my youth to my length of years, what my ears heard and eyes saw—the womanly craft that all my maternal aunts practiced, nothing but brewing and cuisine was not stored in mind."
translations.idiomatic: Hao wrote the Preface to the Food Classic: "From youth to age I saw and heard the woman's work of every aunt—brewing and cuisine, all stored in mind."

sentences.zh: 朝夕養舅姑，四時供祭祀，雖有功力，不任僮使，常手自親焉。

translations.literal: Morning and evening they nurtured fathers-in-law and mothers-in-law; in the four seasons they supplied sacrifices—though they had servants, they could not delegate and constantly tended matters with their own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening they tended parents-in-law; in the four seasons they made offerings. Though they had servants, they worked with their own hands.

sentences.zh: 昔遭喪亂，饑饉仍臻，饣稟蔬餬口，不能具其物用，十餘年間，不復備設。

translations.literal: In past years we suffered chaos and rebellion; famine came repeatedly; coarse fare for the mouth could not supply full use of things, and for more than ten years the full array was no longer set out.
translations.idiomatic: In chaos and famine coarse food could not supply the full table. For more than ten years the full spread was not set.

sentences.zh: 先妣慮久廢忘，後生無所知見，而少不習書，乃占授為九篇。

translations.literal: My late mother, fearing long neglect and forgetting, and that the young would have no knowledge of it, and that I in youth did not study books, therefore dictated and taught in nine chapters.
translations.idiomatic: My late mother feared forgetting and that the young would never see it. I had not studied in youth. She dictated nine chapters.

sentences.zh: 文辭約舉，婉而成章，聰辯強記，皆此類也。

translations.literal: The wording was terse in selection, graceful in forming chapters; keen wit and strong memory—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: The words were terse and graceful; wit and memory were of that kind.

sentences.zh: 親沒之後，遇國龍興之會，平暴除亂，拓定四方。

translations.literal: After my parents died, I met the nation's rising dragon's fortune: pacifying violence and removing disorder, extending and fixing the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: After my parents died the realm rose like a dragon—violence pacified, the four quarters fixed.

sentences.zh: 餘備位台鉉，與參大謀。

translations.literal: I filled a position at the highest terrace and participated in great deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: I stood at the highest terrace and joined great counsel.

sentences.zh: 賞獲豐厚，牛羊蓋澤；

translations.literal: Rewards were rich and thick; cattle and sheep would have covered a marsh;
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were rich; cattle and sheep might have drowned a marsh;

sentences.zh: 貲累巨萬，衣則重錦，食則粱肉。

translations.literal: wealth piled to tens of millions; for clothes, heavy brocade; for food, fine grain and meat.
translations.idiomatic: wealth to tens of millions; clothes heavy brocade; food fine grain and meat.

sentences.zh: 遠惟平生，思季路負米之時，不可復得。

translations.literal: Looking far back on my whole life, I think of the time when Ji Lu carried rice on his back—a thing that cannot come again.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on life I think of Ji Lu carrying rice on his back—a time that cannot return.

sentences.zh: 故序遺文，垂示來世。」

translations.literal: Therefore I arrange this surviving text to hand down to coming generations."
translations.idiomatic: So I set down this surviving text for generations to come."

sentences.zh: 浩弟簡，字仲亮，一名覽。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Jian, styled Zhongliang, also named Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's brother Jian, styled Zhongliang, also called Lan.

sentences.zh: 好學，少以善書知名。

translations.literal: He loved learning and in youth was known for fine calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was known in youth for fine calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 道武初，曆中書侍郎，爵五等侯，參著作事。

translations.literal: In Daowu's early reign he served as Central Secretariat Gentleman, was enfeoffed Marquis of the Fifth Rank, and participated in compiling the National Record.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daowu he was Central Secretariat Gentleman, enfeoffed Fifth-Rank Marquis, and helped compile the National Record.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 簡弟恬，字叔玄，小名白。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Tian, styled Shuxuan, childhood name Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's brother Tian, styled Shuxuan, childhood name Bai.

sentences.zh: 位豫州刺史，爵武陽侯。

translations.literal: He held the post of Inspector of Yuzhou and was enfeoffed Marquis of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was Inspector of Yuzhou and Marquis of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 坐浩伏誅。

translations.literal: Because of Hao he suffered execution by association.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed by association with Hao.

sentences.zh: 宏祖悅，與范陽盧諶並以博藝齊名。

translations.literal: Hong's ancestor Yue, with Fanyang's Lu Chen, were both famed for broad arts.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's ancestor Yue and Fanyang's Lu Chen were famed alike for broad arts.

sentences.zh: 諶法鐘繇，悅法衛瓘，而俱習索靖之草，皆盡其妙。

translations.literal: Chen took Zhong Yao as his model; Yue took Wei Guan; both also studied Su Jing's cursive script, attaining mastery to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Chen followed Zhong Yao; Yue followed Wei Guan. Both studied Su Jing's cursive to the full.

sentences.zh: 諶傳子偃，偃傳子邈；

translations.literal: Chen passed to his son Yan; Yan passed to his son Miao;
translations.idiomatic: Chen passed to Yan; Yan to Miao;

sentences.zh: 悅傳子潛，潛傳子宏。

translations.literal: Yue passed to his son Qian; Qian passed to his son Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yue passed to Qian; Qian to Hong.

sentences.zh: 世不替業，故魏初重崔、盧之書。

translations.literal: Through the generations they did not abandon their craft; therefore in early Wei the calligraphy of the Cui and Lu clans was prized.
translations.idiomatic: Their craft never lapsed—so in early Wei the Cui and Lu scripts were prized.

sentences.zh: 宏自非朝廷文誥，四方書檄，初不妄染，故世無遺文。

translations.literal: Hong himself, unless it was an imperial document for the court or letters and proclamations for the four directions, at first did not lightly touch brush—thus the world has no surviving writings of his.
translations.idiomatic: Unless it was court edict or dispatch to the realm, Hong would not lightly take brush—so no writings of his survive.

sentences.zh: 尤善草隸，為世摹楷，行押特盡精巧，而不見遺跡。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script, a model for the age; running and draft were supremely fine and subtle, yet no traces remain.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in cursive and clerical script, the age's model; running and draft were exquisite—yet no traces remain.

sentences.zh: 始宏因苻氏亂，欲避地江南，為張願所獲，本圖不遂。

translations.literal: At first, because of the chaos of Fu Jian's house, Hong wished to flee south to the Yangtze but was seized by Zhang Yuan; his original plan was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian's house fell into chaos Hong meant to flee south but Zhang Yuan seized him. The plan failed.

sentences.zh: 乃作詩以自傷，而不行于時，蓋懼罪也。

translations.literal: He therefore composed a poem to mourn himself, but it did not circulate in the age—likely from fear of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a poem to mourn himself, but it did not circulate—likely from fear of punishment.

sentences.zh: 浩誅，中書侍郎高允受敕收浩家書，始見此詩，允知其意。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, Central Secretariat Gentleman Gao Yun received an edict to collect Hao's household books and first saw this poem; Yun knew its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: At Hao's death Gao Yun was ordered to collect Hao's books and first saw this poem. Yun understood it.

sentences.zh: 允孫綽錄于允集。

translations.literal: Yun's grandson Chuo copied it into Yun's collected works.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's grandson Chuo copied it into Yun's collected works.

sentences.zh: 初，宏父潛為兄渾等誄手筆本草，延昌初，著作佐郎王遵業買書於市，遇得之。

translations.literal: At the start, Hong's father Qian had written for his elder brother Hun and others a eulogy in his own hand on herbal medicine; in Yan chang's early years Compiling Assistant Wang Zunyue bought books in the market and happened to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hong's father Qian had written in his own hand for his brother Hun a eulogy on herbal medicine. In early Yan chang Wang Zunyue bought books in the market and found it.

sentences.zh: 年將二百，寶其書跡，深藏秘之。

translations.literal: Nearly two hundred years had passed; he treasured the calligraphic trace and hid it in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly two hundred years had passed. He treasured the trace and kept it hidden.

sentences.zh: 武定中，遵業子松年將以遺黃門郎崔季舒，人多摹拓之。

translations.literal: In Wuding, Zunyue's son Songnian was about to give it to Cui Jishu, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; many copied it by rubbing.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding Zunyue's son Songnian meant to give it to Cui Jishu of the Yellow Gate. Many made rubbings.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫姚元標以工書知名于時，見潛書，以為過於浩也。

translations.literal: Left Household Grandee Yao Yuanbiao was famed in the age for skill in calligraphy; seeing Qian's writing, he thought it surpassed Hao's.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanbiao, famed for calligraphy, saw Qian's hand and thought it surpassed Hao's.

sentences.zh: 宏弟徽，字玄猷，少有文才，與勃海高演俱知名。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Hui, styled Xuanyou, had literary talent in youth and was famed together with Bohai's Gao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's brother Hui, styled Xuanyou, had literary talent in youth and was famed with Bohai's Gao Yan.

sentences.zh: 歷位秘書監，賜爵貝丘侯。

translations.literal: He held the post of Director of the Secretariat and was granted the title Marquis of Beiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He was Director of the Secretariat and Marquis of Beiqiu.

sentences.zh: 樂安王范鎮長安，選舊德之士與範俱，以徽為平西將軍副將，行樂安王傅，進爵濟南公。

translations.literal: Prince of Le'an Fan garrisoned Chang'an and chose men of old virtue to accompany Fan; Hui was made Vice General of Pacifying the West and acting Tutor to the Prince of Le'an, advanced to Duke of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Le'an Fan held Chang'an and chose elders to accompany him. Hui was made Vice General of Pacifying the West and acting tutor to the prince, advanced to Duke of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 徽為政務存大體，不親小事。

translations.literal: In government Hui kept to the great pattern and did not attend to small matters.
translations.idiomatic: In office Hui kept the great pattern and left small matters alone.

sentences.zh: 性好人倫。

translations.literal: By nature he loved human relations.
translations.idiomatic: He loved human worth by nature.

sentences.zh: 引接賓客，或談及平生，或講論道義，誨誘後進，終日不止。

translations.literal: Receiving guests, he might speak of his whole life or discuss the Way and righteousness, instructing the young—without ceasing all day.
translations.idiomatic: He received guests—talking of his life, of the Way, teaching the young—all day without stop.

sentences.zh: 以疾，征還京師，卒，諡曰元公，士類無不嘆惜。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was summoned back to the capital and died; posthumous name Duke Yuan. Men of his kind all sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he was recalled to the capital and died. Posthumous name Duke Yuan. Scholars mourned.

sentences.zh: 始清河崔寬祖肜，隨晉南陽王保避地隴右，遂仕西涼及沮渠氏。

translations.literal: At the start, Qinghe's Cui Kuan traced his ancestry to Tong, who followed Jin's Prince of Nanyang Bao in fleeing to Longyou and then served Western Liang and the Juqu house.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe's Cui Kuan traced to Tong, who followed Prince of Nanyang Bao south to Longyou and served Western Liang and the Juqu.

sentences.zh: 肜生剖，字伯宗，每慷慨有懷東土。

translations.literal: Tong begot Pou, styled Bozong, who was often stirred with longing for the eastern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Tong begot Pou, styled Bozong, often stirred with longing for the east.

sentences.zh: 常歎曰：「風雨如晦，雞鳴不已，吾所庶幾！

translations.literal: He often sighed: "Wind and rain dark, the cock crows unceasing—that is what I hope for!"
translations.idiomatic: He often sighed: "Wind and rain, yet the cock crows—that is what I hope for!"

sentences.zh: 」及太武西巡，剖乃總率同義，使子寬送款。

translations.literal: " When Taiwu toured the west, Pou mustered men of shared purpose and sent his son Kuan to offer allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: " When Taiwu toured west, Pou rallied like-minded men and sent his son Kuan to submit.

sentences.zh: 太武嘉之，拜寬岐陽令，賜爵延水男。

translations.literal: Taiwu was pleased and appointed Kuan Magistrate of Qiyang, granting the title Baron of Yanshui.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu was pleased. Kuan was made Magistrate of Qiyang and Baron of Yanshui.

sentences.zh: 遣使與寬俱西，撫慰初附。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy to go west with Kuan and comfort those newly attached.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy went west with Kuan to comfort the newly attached.

sentences.zh: 征部詣京師，未至而卒。

translations.literal: Pou was summoned to the capital but died before arriving.
translations.idiomatic: Pou was summoned to the capital but died on the way.

sentences.zh: 文成以剖誠著先朝，贈涼州刺史、武陵公，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Wencheng, because Pou's loyalty was clear in the former court, posthumously made him Inspector of Liangzhou and Duke of Wuling, posthumous name Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng, for Pou's loyalty in the former reign, posthumously made him Inspector of Liangzhou and Duke of Wuling, posthumous name Yuan.

sentences.zh: 寬字景仁，還京，封安國子，位弘農太守。

translations.literal: Kuan, styled Jingren, returned to the capital, was enfeoffed Viscount of Anguo, and held the post of Governor of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan, styled Jingren, returned, was made Viscount of Anguo, and Governor of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 初，寬通款見浩，浩與相齒次，厚存接之。

translations.literal: At first, when Kuan offered allegiance he met Hao; Hao matched him in age and received him with deep courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuan first submitted he met Hao. Hao matched him in age and received him warmly.

sentences.zh: 及浩誅，以遠來疏族，獨得不坐。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, as a distant clan who had come from afar, he alone was not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: At Hao's death, a distant clan come from afar, he alone escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 遂家于武城，居司空林舊墟，以一子繼浩。

translations.literal: He then made his home in Wucheng, dwelling on the old site of Sikong Lin, with one son continuing Hao's line.
translations.idiomatic: He settled in Wucheng on Sikong Lin's old ground, with one son to continue Hao's line.

sentences.zh: 與浩弟覽妻封氏相奉如親。

translations.literal: With Hao's brother Lan's wife of the Feng clan he tended each other like kin.
translations.idiomatic: He and Hao's brother Lan's wife Feng tended each other like kin.

sentences.zh: 寬後襲爵武陵公，陝城鎮將。

translations.literal: Later Kuan inherited the title Duke of Wuling and was garrison commander of Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kuan inherited Duke of Wuling and was garrison commander of Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 三崤地險，人多寇劫。

translations.literal: The Three Gorges country was rugged; men often robbed and raided.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Gorges were rugged. Men often robbed.

sentences.zh: 而寬性滑稽，誘接豪右，宿盜魁帥，與相交結。

translations.literal: Kuan by nature was witty and humorous; he drew in powerful local men and old bandit chiefs and joined with them.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was witty. He drew in local powers and bandit chiefs and befriended them.

sentences.zh: 傾衿待遇，不逆細微，莫不感其意氣。

translations.literal: He poured out his breast in reception, not rejecting the smallest detail; none failed to be moved by his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He received them with open heart, not refusing the smallest courtesy. All were moved by his spirit.

sentences.zh: 時官無祿力，唯取給於人，寬善撫納，招致禮遺，大有取受，而與之者無恨。

translations.literal: At the time officials had no salary but took their support from others; Kuan was skilled at soothing and gathering them, inviting gifts and presents—he received much, yet those who gave bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had no salary then and lived on others' gifts. Kuan soothed and gathered them, accepting much—yet givers bore no grudge.

sentences.zh: 又恆農出漆蠟竹木之饒，路與南通，貿易來往，家產豐富，而百姓樂之。

translations.literal: Hengnong moreover produced lacquer, wax, bamboo, and timber in abundance; the road connected southward and trade came and went—his household was rich while the common people were content.
translations.idiomatic: Hengnong was rich in lacquer, wax, bamboo, and timber. Trade ran south. His house was rich and the people content.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮之中，號曰能政。

translations.literal: Among the garrisons he was called able in government.
translations.idiomatic: Among garrisons he was called able in government.

sentences.zh: 及解鎮，人人追戀，詣闕上疏者三百餘人。

translations.literal: When he left his post, men pursued him with longing; more than three hundred went to court with memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When he left, men followed with longing. More than three hundred memorialized at court.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺言薄葬，斂以時服。

translations.literal: At death he left instructions for a plain burial, enshrouded in timely dress.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a plain burial in timely dress.

sentences.zh: 長子敞，字公世，襲爵，例降為侯，為平原相。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chang, styled Gongshi, inherited the title, reduced by precedent to marquis, and was Chancellor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Chang, styled Gongshi, inherited—reduced by rule to marquis—and was Chancellor of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 敞性狷急，與刺史楊椿迭相表列，敞坐免官。

translations.literal: Chang's nature was narrow and hasty; he and the inspector Yang Chun repeatedly memorialized against each other, and Chang was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was narrow and hasty. He and Inspector Yang Chun denounced each other in memorials. Chang was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，為钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: In Xuanwu's early reign he was Governor of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xuanwu he was Governor of Julu.

sentences.zh: 弟朏之逆，敞為黃木軍主韓文殊所藏。

translations.literal: At Fei's rebellion, Chang was hidden by Huangmu Army Commander Han Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: At Fei's rebellion Chang was hidden by Han Wenshu, commander of the Huangmu Army.

sentences.zh: 其家悉見籍沒，唯敞妻李氏以公主之甥，自隨奴婢田宅二百餘口得免。

translations.literal: His household was entirely registered and confiscated; only Chang's wife Li, as niece of a princess, with her own servants, fields, and houses—more than two hundred mouths—was spared.
translations.idiomatic: His household was confiscated. Only his wife Li, a princess's niece, with her servants, fields, and houses—more than two hundred souls—was spared.

sentences.zh: 正光中，普釋禁錮，敞復爵郡侯，卒于趙郡太守。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang, when the general amnesty lifted bonds, Chang recovered his commandery marquisate and died as Governor of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang, when bonds were lifted, Chang recovered his marquisate and died as Governor of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 敞弟鐘，字公祿，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Zhong, styled Gonglu, was a Court Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Zhong, styled Gonglu, was Court Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 弟朏之逆，以出後被原。

translations.literal: At Fei's rebellion, because he had been adopted out he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: At Fei's rebellion, adopted out, he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 曆司徒右長史、金紫光祿大夫、冀州大中正。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, Grandee of the Golden Purple and Bright Light, and Rectifier of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, Grandee of Golden Purple and Bright Light, and Rectifier of Ji.

sentences.zh: 敞亡後，鐘貪其財，誣敞息子積等三人非兄胤，辭訴累歲，人士疾之。

translations.literal: After Chang died, Zhong coveted his wealth and falsely claimed Chang's sons Ji and three others were not legitimate heirs; lawsuits dragged on for years, and gentlemen despised him.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang died Zhong coveted his wealth and claimed Chang's sons Ji and two others were not true heirs. Lawsuits ran for years. Gentlemen despised him.

sentences.zh: 爾硃世隆為尚書令，奏除其官，終身勿齒。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong as Minister of the Masters of Writing memorialized to strip him of office, never to be ranked again.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong as Minister of the Masters of Writing stripped him of office for life.

sentences.zh: 朏好學，有文才，為京兆王愉錄事參軍，與愉同逆，伏法。

translations.literal: Fei loved learning and had literary talent; he was Recorder of Prince of Jingzhao Yu and rebelled with Yu and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Fei loved learning and had literary talent. He was recorder to Prince of Jingzhao Yu, rebelled with Yu, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 宏同郡董謐。

translations.literal: In Hong's same commandery, Dong Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hong's commandery lived Dong Mi.

sentences.zh: 謐父京，與同郡崔康時、廣陽霍原等，俱以碩學，播名遼海。

translations.literal: Mi's father Jing, with Cui Kangshi of the same commandery and Huo Yuan of Guangyang, were all famed as great scholars, their names spreading over Liaohai.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's father Jing, with Cui Kangshi and Guangyang's Huo Yuan, were great scholars famed across Liaohai.

sentences.zh: 謐好學，傳父業。

translations.literal: Mi loved learning and inherited his father's craft.
translations.idiomatic: Mi loved learning and inherited his father's craft.

sentences.zh: 中山平，入朝，拜儀曹郎，撰朝覲、饗宴、郊廟、社稷之儀。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified he entered court, was appointed Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office, and composed the rites for court audience, feasts, suburban altars, and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan fell he entered court as Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office and wrote rites for audience, feast, suburban sacrifice, and altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 張袞，字洪龍，上谷沮陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, was a man of Jieyang, Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, was from Jieyang in Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 祖翼，父卓，位並太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi and father Zhuo both held the post of governor.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Yi and father Zhuo were both governors.

sentences.zh: 袞篤實好學，有文才。

translations.literal: Gun was sincere and solid, loved learning, and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gun was sincere, loved learning, and had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 道武為代王，選為左長史。

translations.literal: When Daowu was Prince of Dai, Gun was chosen as Left Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu was Prince of Dai, Gun was chosen Left Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 從追蠕蠕五六百里。

translations.literal: He followed in pursuit of the Rouran for five or six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He followed pursuit of the Rouran five or six hundred li.

sentences.zh: 諸部帥因兗言糧盡，不宜深入。

translations.literal: The various tribal chiefs, taking advantage of Yan's report that grain was exhausted, said it was not fitting to go deep.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal chiefs, hearing Yan say grain was gone, said they should not go deep.

sentences.zh: 帝問袞：「殺副馬足三日食乎？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Gun: "If we kill the spare horses, is there food for three days?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Gun: "Slaughter the spare horses—food for three days?"

sentences.zh: 」皆言足。

translations.literal: " All said it was enough.
translations.idiomatic: " All said yes.

sentences.zh: 帝乃倍道追及於廣漠赤地南床山下，大破之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore doubled the march and caught up at south of Bed Mountain on the broad red desert, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He doubled the march and caught them south of Bed Mountain on the broad red desert and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 既而帝問袞曰：「卿曹外人，知我前問三日糧意乎？

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor asked Gun: "You outsiders—did you know my earlier meaning about three days' grain?"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he asked Gun: "You outsiders—did you grasp my three-days' grain?"

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕奔走數日，畜產失飲，至水必留。

translations.literal: The Rouran run for days; their livestock lose drink and must halt at water.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran run for days. Their herds lose drink and must halt at water.

sentences.zh: 計其道程，三日足及。

translations.literal: Calculating their route, three days is enough to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Count their route—three days is enough.

sentences.zh: 輕騎卒至，出其不意，彼必驚散，其勢然矣。

translations.literal: Light cavalry arriving suddenly takes them unawares; they are sure to scatter in alarm—that is how the momentum runs."
translations.idiomatic: Light horse arrives unawares—they scatter. That is the momentum."

sentences.zh: 」部帥聞之，咸曰：「聖策，非所及也。

translations.literal: " The tribal chiefs heard it and all said: "Sacred stratagem—beyond what we could reach."
translations.idiomatic: " The chiefs said: "Sacred stratagem—beyond us."

sentences.zh: 」袞常參大謀，每告人曰：「主上天資傑邁，必能囊括六合。

translations.literal: " Gun often participated in great deliberations and would tell others: "Our lord's heaven-born talent is outstanding; he is sure to embrace the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: " Gun often joined great counsel and told others: "Our lord's talent is heaven-born. He will embrace the six directions.

sentences.zh: 夫遭風雲之會，不建騰跳之功者，非人豪也。

translations.literal: One who meets the season of wind and cloud yet does not build leaping achievement is no true hero."
translations.idiomatic: Meet wind and cloud and build no soaring merit—that is no hero."

sentences.zh: 」遂策名委質，竭誠伏事。

translations.literal: He therefore pledged his name and gave his utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged his name and served with utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 時劉顯地廣兵強，跨有朔裔，會其兄弟乖離，共相疑阻。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Xian's territory was broad and his troops strong, spanning the northern borderlands; it happened that his brothers were estranged and mutually suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian held broad land and strong troops across the north. His brothers quarreled and suspected each other.

sentences.zh: 袞言于道武曰：「顯志大意高，今因其內釁，宜速乘之。

translations.literal: Gun said to Daowu: "Xian's will is great and his intent high; now, while their inner rift is open, we ought to strike swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: Gun told Daowu: "Xian's will is great. Strike now while they split within."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，遂破走顯。

translations.literal: The emperor followed him and broke and drove off Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened and broke Xian and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 又從破賀訥。

translations.literal: He also followed in defeating He Na.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed in defeating He Na.

sentences.zh: 道武登勿居山遊宴，從官請聚石為峰，以記功德，乃命袞為文。

translations.literal: Daowu ascended Wuju Mountain for a feast; his attendants asked to pile stones into a peak to record merit, and he ordered Gun to compose the text.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu feasted on Wuju Mountain. Attendants asked to pile stones as a peak to record merit. Gun was ordered to write the text.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶之來寇也，袞言于道武曰：「寶乘滑台功，因長子捷，頌財竭力，難與爭鋒，宜羸師以侈其心。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Gun said to Daowu: "Bao rides on the merit of Huatai and, because of his victory at Changzi, exhausts wealth and strength—it is hard to contend with him in the spear. We ought to show a weak army to swell his heart."
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao raided, Gun said: "Bao rides Huatai's merit and Changzi's victory. He has spent wealth and strength—hard to meet in the spear. Show a weak army and swell his heart."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，果破之參合。

translations.literal: The emperor followed him and indeed broke Bao at Canhe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened and broke Bao at Canhe.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 道武南伐，次中山，袞遺寶書，喻以成敗。

translations.literal: On Daowu's southern campaign he halted at Zhongshan; Gun sent Bao a letter explaining success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: On Daowu's southern campaign he halted at Zhongshan. Gun sent Bao a letter on success and failure.

sentences.zh: 寶見書，大懼，遂奔和龍。

translations.literal: Bao saw the letter and was greatly afraid; he then fled to Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Bao read it and was greatly afraid. He fled to Helong.

sentences.zh: 既克中山，聽入八議，拜幽州刺史，賜爵臨渭侯，百姓安之。

translations.literal: After Zhongshan was taken, he was admitted to the Eight Discussions, appointed Inspector of Youzhou, enfeoffed Marquis of Linwei, and the common people were settled under him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell he entered the Eight Discussions, was Inspector of Youzhou and Marquis of Linwei. The people were settled.

sentences.zh: 天興初，征還京師。

translations.literal: In Tianxing's early years he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tianxing he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後與崔逞答晉將郗恢書失旨，黜為尚書令史。

translations.literal: Later, because he and Cui Cheng answered Jin general Xi Hui's letter off the mark, he was demoted to Chief Clerk of the Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Cui Cheng answered Jin general Xi Hui's letter badly and he was demoted to chief clerk of the Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 袞遇創業之初，始以才謀見任，率心奉上，不顧嫌疑。

translations.literal: Gun met the realm at the founding of enterprise; at first he was trusted for talent and stratagem, serving with an open heart without regard for suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Gun met the realm at its founding and was first trusted for talent, serving openly without fear of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 道武曾問南州人於袞，袞與盧溥州裏，數稱薦之。

translations.literal: Daowu once asked Gun about men of the southern provinces; Gun and Lu Pu were from the same commandery and he repeatedly praised and recommended Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu once asked Gun about southern men. Gun and Lu Pu were townsmen. He praised Pu again and again.

sentences.zh: 又未嘗與崔逞相識，聞風稱美。

translations.literal: He had also never known Cui Cheng but heard his reputation and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He had never met Cui Cheng but heard his fame and praised him.

sentences.zh: 及中山平，盧溥聚黨為逆，崔逞答書不允，並乖本言，故忿之。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified, Lu Pu gathered a faction to rebel and Cui Cheng's answering letter was not compliant—both contrary to what he had said—and therefore he resented them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan fell Lu Pu rebelled and Cui Cheng's reply was not compliant—both against his word—and he resented them.

sentences.zh: 袞年過七十，闔門守靜，手執經書，刊定乖失。

translations.literal: Gun passed seventy; he closed his gates and kept quiet, holding the classics in hand, collating and correcting errors.
translations.idiomatic: Past seventy Gun closed his gates, held the classics, and collated errors.

sentences.zh: 愛好人物，善誘無倦，士類以此高之。

translations.literal: He loved worthy men and skillfully guided without weariness; gentlemen for this held him high.
translations.idiomatic: He loved worthy men and taught without weariness. Gentlemen honored him.

sentences.zh: 永興二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxing year two he died.

sentences.zh: 太武后追錄舊勳，遣大鴻臚即墓策贈太保，諡文康公。

translations.literal: Later Taiwu's empress posthumously recorded old merit and sent the Grand Herald to his tomb with patent, posthumously making him Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Duke Wenkang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taiwu's empress recorded old merit and sent the Grand Herald to his tomb with patent, posthumously Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Duke Wenkang.

sentences.zh: 子度，少有學尚，襲爵臨渭侯，卒於中都大官。

translations.literal: His son Du in youth had learning and esteem, inherited the title Marquis of Linwei, and died as Grand Provisioner of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Son Du in youth had learning, inherited Marquis of Linwei, and died as Grand Provisioner of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 度子白澤，年十一，遭母憂，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Du's son Baize at eleven suffered his mother's mourning and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Du's son Baize at eleven mourned his mother and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 長而博學。

translations.literal: Grown, he was broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was broadly learned.

sentences.zh: 文成初，除殿中曹給事中，甚見寵任。

translations.literal: In Wencheng's early reign he was appointed Attendant of the Palace Bureau and greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wencheng he was Attendant of the Palace Bureau and greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 白澤本字鐘葵，獻文賜名白澤，納其女為嬪。

translations.literal: Baize's original name was Zhongkui; Xianwen granted the name Baize and took his daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Baize's original name was Zhongkui. Xianwen granted the name Baize and took his daughter as consort.

sentences.zh: 出行雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 清心少欲，人吏安之。

translations.literal: Clear in mind and few in desires; officials and commoners were settled under him.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-minded and few in desires, officials and people were at ease under him.

sentences.zh: 獻文詔諸監臨官取所監羊一口、酒一斛者，罪至大辟；

translations.literal: Xianwen edicted that overseer officials who took one sheep or one hu of wine from those they oversaw would be guilty up to capital punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen edicted: overseers who took one sheep or one hu of wine from those they oversaw faced capital punishment;

sentences.zh: 與者以從坐論。

translations.literal: those who gave would be judged as accomplices by association.
translations.idiomatic: those who gave were judged accomplices.

sentences.zh: 糾得尚書以下罪狀者，各隨所糾官輕重而授之。

translations.literal: Those who exposed guilt among the Masters of Writing and below would each receive appointment according to the weight of the official they exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever exposed guilt among officials to Masters of Writing and below would be appointed according to the rank of the man exposed.

sentences.zh: 白澤上表，以為此法若行之不已，恐奸人窺望，勞臣懈節，請依律令舊法。

translations.literal: Baize memorialized, thinking that if this law were carried on without end, he feared treacherous men would spy and diligent ministers would slacken their integrity; he asked to follow the statutes' old law.
translations.idiomatic: Baize memorialized: carry this law on forever and treacherous men will watch while diligent ministers slacken. Follow the old statutes.

sentences.zh: 獻文納之。

translations.literal: Xianwen accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen accepted it.

sentences.zh: 太和初，懷州人伊祁苟初三十餘人謀反，文明皇太后欲盡誅一城人。

translations.literal: In Taihe's early years more than thirty men of Huai commandery, Yi Qi Gou and others, plotted rebellion; Empress Dowager Wencheng wished to execute the whole city's people.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taihe more than thirty men of Huai, Yi Qi Gou and others, plotted rebellion. Empress Dowager Wencheng wished to kill the whole city.

sentences.zh: 白澤諫，以為《周書》父子兄弟罪不相及，不誣十室，而況一州。

translations.literal: Baize remonstrated, holding that in the Documents of Zhou the crimes of father, son, and brothers do not reach one another, that one does not falsely implicate ten households—how much less a whole commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Baize remonstrated: the Documents of Zhou do not link father, son, and brother in guilt. Do not implicate ten houses—how much less a commandery.

sentences.zh: 後從之，乃止。

translations.literal: The empress later followed him and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The empress later followed him and stopped.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍、殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant and Attendant of the Palace Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant and Attendant of the Palace Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈相州刺史、廣平公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Inspector of Xiangzhou and Duke of Guangping, posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died. Posthumously Inspector of Xiangzhou and Duke of Guangping, posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 長子倫，字天念，大司農少卿、燕州大中正。

translations.literal: His eldest son Lun, styled Tiannian, was Vice Minister of the Grand Granary and Rectifier of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Lun, styled Tiannian, was Vice Minister of the Grand Granary and Rectifier of Yan.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，蠕蠕主醜奴遣使來朝，抗敵國之禮，不修臣敬。

translations.literal: In Xiping, the Rouran lord Chounu sent envoys to court, using the ritual of a rival state and not observing minister's respect.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping the Rouran lord Chounu sent envoys using rival-state ritual, without minister's courtesy.

sentences.zh: 朝議將依漢答匈奴故事，遣使報之。

translations.literal: Court discussion wished to follow Han's precedent in answering the Xiongnu and send envoys in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Court wished to follow Han's answer to the Xiongnu and send envoys in reply.

sentences.zh: 倫表以為：「虜雖慕德，亦來觀我。

translations.literal: Lun memorialized, holding: "Though the barbarians admire virtue, they also come to observe us.
translations.idiomatic: Lun memorialized: "Though the barbarians admire virtue, they also come to observe us.

sentences.zh: 懼之以強，儻或歸附；

translations.literal: If we awe them with strength, perhaps they will submit;
translations.idiomatic: Awe them with strength and perhaps they submit;

sentences.zh: 示之以弱，窺覦或起。

translations.literal: if we show them weakness, covetous watching may arise.
translations.idiomatic: show weakness and covetous eyes may open.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》所謂以我卜也。

translations.literal: What the Spring and Autumn calls 'they take us as their oracle.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn says: they take us as their oracle."

sentences.zh: 高祖、世宗知其若此，來既莫逆，去又不追。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Shizong knew this: when they came, none went against them; when they left, none pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Shizong knew this: when they came, none opposed; when they left, none pursued.

sentences.zh: 必其委贄玉帛之辰，屈膝籓方之禮，則豐其勞賄，藉以珍物。

translations.literal: Only when they came with tribute of jade and silks and bent knee in vassal ritual did they heap rewards and lend precious things.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they came with jade and silk and bent the knee in vassal ritual did the court heap rewards and lend treasures.

sentences.zh: 至於王人遠役，銜命虜庭，優以匹敵之尊，加之想望之寵，恐徒生虜慢，無益聖朝。

translations.literal: But when royal envoys went far on mission to the barbarian court, honored with rival dignity and given longing favor, I fear it would only breed barbarian insolence and benefit the holy court little."
translations.idiomatic: Send royal envoys far into the barbarian court, honor them as equals, add longing favor—I fear only barbarian insolence, little gain for the holy court."

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " They did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: " They did not listen.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，卒于大司農卿。

translations.literal: In early Xiaozhuang he died as Minister of the Grand Granary.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xiaozhuang he died as Minister of the Grand Granary.

sentences.zh: 袞弟恂。

translations.literal: Gun's younger brother Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Gun's younger brother Xun.

sentences.zh: 恂字洪讓，隨兄袞歸北，參代王軍事。

translations.literal: Xun, styled Hongrang, followed his elder brother Gun north and participated in the Prince of Dai's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, styled Hongrang, followed Gun north and joined the Prince of Dai's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 說道武宜收中土士庶之望，以建大業。

translations.literal: He advised Daowu that he ought to win the hopes of the gentry and commoners of the central lands to establish great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He advised Daowu to win the hopes of central gentry and people to build great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 帝深加器異。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued and distinguished him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In Huangshi's early years he was appointed Central Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In early Huangshi he was Central Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 帷幄密謀，頗亦參預。

translations.literal: In curtain stratagems he also participated.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined secret stratagems.

sentences.zh: 賜爵平皋子，出為廣平太守。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Pinggao and went out as Governor of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Pinggao and went out as Governor of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 恂招集離散，勸課農桑，流人歸者數千戶。

translations.literal: Xun gathered the scattered and urged farming and sericulture; refugees who returned numbered several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Xun gathered the scattered, urged farming and sericulture. Thousands of refugee households returned.

sentences.zh: 遷常山太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 恂開建學校，優禮儒士，吏人歌詠之。

translations.literal: Xun founded schools and honored scholars with courtesy; officials and people sang of him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun founded schools and honored scholars. Officials and people sang of him.

sentences.zh: 時喪亂之後，罕能克厲者，唯恂當官清白，仁恕臨下，百姓親愛之，政為當時第一。

translations.literal: In the time after chaos, few could be strict with themselves; only Xun in office was pure and white, benevolent and forgiving to those below—the common people loved him, and his government was first in the age.
translations.idiomatic: After chaos few were strict. Only Xun in office was pure, benevolent below—the people loved him. His government was first in the age.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，徵拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan acceded, he was summoned as Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan acceded he was summoned Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 恂性清儉，死日家無餘財。

translations.literal: Xun by nature was pure and frugal; on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was pure and frugal. On the day he died his house had no surplus.

sentences.zh: 贈并州刺史、平皋侯，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Inspector of Bingzhou and Marquis of Pinggao, posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Inspector of Bingzhou and Marquis of Pinggao, posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子純，字道尚，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chun, styled Daoshang, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chun, styled Daoshang, inherited.

sentences.zh: 坐事除。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped for an offense.

sentences.zh: 純弟代，字定燕，陳留、北平二郡太守。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Dai, styled Dingyan, was Governor of Chenliu and Pingbei.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Dai, styled Dingyan, was Governor of Chenliu and Pingbei.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈營州刺史，諡惠侯。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Inspector of Yingzhou, posthumous name Marquis Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died. Posthumously Inspector of Yingzhou, posthumous name Marquis Hui.

sentences.zh: 代所曆著稱，有父遺風。

translations.literal: Where Dai held office he was praised; he had his father's surviving style.
translations.idiomatic: Where Dai served he was praised. He had his father's style.

sentences.zh: 代子萇年，為汝南太守。

translations.literal: Dai's son Changnian was Governor of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai's son Changnian was Governor of Runan.

sentences.zh: 郡人劉崇之兄弟分析，家貧，唯一牛，爭不能決，訟於郡庭。

translations.literal: Brothers Liu Chongzhi of the commandery divided their property; the household was poor and had only one ox, which they disputed and could not settle, suing in the commandery court.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers Liu Chongzhi divided property. Poor, with one ox, they disputed and sued at the commandery court.

sentences.zh: 萇年淒而見之，謂曰：「汝曹當以一牛，故致此競；

translations.literal: Changnian, grieved, saw them and said: "You quarrel because you have one ox;
translations.idiomatic: Changnian saw them in grief and said: "You quarrel because you have one ox;

sentences.zh: 脫有二牛，必不爭。

translations.literal: if you had two oxen, you would surely not dispute."
translations.idiomatic: had you two, you would not dispute."

sentences.zh: 」乃以己牛一頭賜之。

translations.literal: He therefore gave them one ox of his own.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them one of his own oxen.

sentences.zh: 於是境中各相戒約，咸敦敬讓。

translations.literal: Thereupon within the district each warned the other and all became respectful and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Within the district each warned the other. All became respectful and yielding.

sentences.zh: 卒於郡。

translations.literal: He died in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子琛，字寶貴，少有孝行，位至太子翊軍校尉。

translations.literal: His son Chen, styled Baogui, in youth had filial conduct and reached the post of Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chen, styled Baogui, had filial conduct in youth and reached Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 鄧彥海，安定人也。

translations.literal: Deng Yanhai was a man of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yanhai was from Anding.

sentences.zh: 祖羌，苻堅車騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiang was General of Chariots and Cavalry under Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Qiang was Chariots and Cavalry General under Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 父翼，河間相。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Chancellor of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Father Yi was Chancellor of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂之圍鄴，以為冀州刺史，爵真定侯。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui besieged Ye, Yi was made Inspector of Ji and Marquis of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui besieged Ye, Yi was made Inspector of Ji and Marquis of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 拒對使者曰：「先君忠於秦室，翼豈可先叛乎？

translations.literal: He refused the envoy, saying: "My late father was loyal to the house of Qin; how can Yi go over to the enemy first?"
translations.idiomatic: He refused the envoy: "My father was loyal to Qin. How can Yi betray first?"

sentences.zh: 忠臣不事二主，未敢聞命。

translations.literal: A loyal minister does not serve two masters; I dare not hear the command."
translations.idiomatic: A loyal minister does not serve two masters. I dare not obey."

sentences.zh: 」垂遣喻之曰：「吾與車騎結為異姓兄弟，卿亦猶吾子弟，安得辭乎？

translations.literal: Chui sent someone to persuade him: "I and the Chariots and Cavalry General became sworn brothers of different surnames; you are also like my son and younger brother—how can you decline?"
translations.idiomatic: Chui persuaded him: "Your grandfather and I were sworn brothers. You are as my son—how can you refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「冀州宜任親賢，翼請他役效命。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Ji ought to be entrusted to kin and worthies; Yi asks for another service to offer his life."
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said: "Ji should go to kin and worthies. Give Yi another post to die in."

sentences.zh: 」垂乃用為河間太守。

translations.literal: " Chui therefore employed him as Governor of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: " Chui made him Governor of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 後卒于趙郡內史。

translations.literal: Later he died as Internal Governor of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died as Internal Governor of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 彥海性貞素，言行可復，博覽經書，長於《易》筮。

translations.literal: Yanhai by nature was pure and plain; words and conduct could be retraced; he broadly read the classics and was skilled in Yi divination.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhai was pure and plain, his words traceable. He read the classics broadly and excelled in Yi divination.

sentences.zh: 道武定中原，擢為著作郎，再遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: When Daowu pacified the central plains, Yanhai was promoted to Compiler and twice transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu pacified the central plains Yanhai was Compiler, then twice Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 彥海明解制度，多識故事，與尚書崔宏參定朝儀、律令、音樂，及軍國文記、詔策多是彥海所為。

translations.literal: Yanhai clearly understood institutions, knew many precedents, and with Minister Cui Hong fixed court ritual, statutes, music, and military and state documents and edicts—many were Yanhai's work.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhai knew institutions and precedents. With Cui Hong he fixed court ritual, law, music, and state documents—much was Yanhai's.

sentences.zh: 賜爵下博子。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Viscount of Xiabo.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted Viscount of Xiabo.

sentences.zh: 道武詔彥海撰國記十餘卷，唯次年月，起居行事而已，未有體例。

translations.literal: Daowu edicted Yanhai to compile a National Record of more than ten scrolls, only arranging year and month and daily conduct, without yet a form and example.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu ordered Yanhai to compile a National Record of more than ten scrolls—only year, month, and daily acts, without form.

sentences.zh: 彥海謹於朝事，未嘗忤旨。

translations.literal: Yanhai was careful in court affairs and never went against the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhai was careful at court and never went against intent.

sentences.zh: 其從父弟暉時為尚書郎，凶俠好奇，與定陵侯和跋厚。

translations.literal: His younger cousin by the father's line Hui was then Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, fierce and knight-errant, curious by nature, and thick with Marquis of Dingling He Ba.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Hui was then Gentleman of the Masters of Writing—fierce, curious, thick with Marquis of Dingling He Ba.

sentences.zh: 跋有罪誅，其子弟奔長安。

translations.literal: Ba had a crime and was executed; his sons and younger brothers fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was executed for a crime. His sons and brothers fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 或告暉將送出之，由是道武疑知情，遂賜彥海死。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Hui would send them out; because of this Daowu suspected he knew and therefore granted Yanhai death.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported Hui would send them out. Daowu suspected knowledge and granted Yanhai death.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之。

translations.literal: Afterward he repented of it.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he repented.

sentences.zh: 時人咸湣惜焉。

translations.literal: Men of the time all pitied and mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: All pitied him.

sentences.zh: 子穎襲爵，稍遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Ying inherited the title and was gradually promoted to Central Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Son Ying inherited and rose to Central Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 太武詔太常卿崔浩集諸文學撰述國書，穎與浩弟覽等俱參著作事。

translations.literal: Taiwu edicted Minister of Ceremonies Cui Hao to gather literary men to compile the National Record; Ying with Hao's brother Lan and others all participated in the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu ordered Cui Hao to gather scholars for the National Record. Ying joined with Hao's brother Lan and others.

sentences.zh: 太武幸漠南，高車莫弗庫若干率騎數萬餘，驅鹿百餘萬詣行所。

translations.literal: Taiwu favored the southern desert; the Gaoche Mo Fu Ku Yu Gan led several tens of thousands of horsemen driving more than a million deer to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu favored the southern desert. Gaoche Mo Fu Ku Yu Gan led tens of thousands of horse, driving more than a million deer to the camp.

sentences.zh: 詔穎為文，銘于漠南，以記功德。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ying to compose the text and inscribe it on the southern desert to record merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was ordered to write the text and inscribe it on the southern desert to record merit.

sentences.zh: 兼散騎常侍，使宋。

translations.literal: Concurrently Regular Attendant, envoy to Song.
